`net.ios.config` declares itself reversible, and validate's `reversible:` and `rollback_on_failure` rules read that
declaration. A call with `checkpoint: false` records no undo, so a block undoing itself inside the run would reach
that task and stop, with the tasks before it undone and the rest not.

**Root cause.** Whether a call records an undo depends on its parameters, and validate asked the method. That is
156's class (a property of the run declared on the method) and the case LESSONS 204 describes for check mode. 604,
on this branch, was the other direction: declaring an undo made validate refuse every call.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: `collection.Descriptor.UndoCall`, a per-call answer beside `CheckCall` and `DeviceCall`, which
`whyNotUndoable` asks (`internal/validate/rollback_rule.go`). `Register` refuses an `UndoCall` on a method that is not
reversible. `net.ios.config`'s answers no for `checkpoint: false`. Tests:
`TestReversibleRule_AsksTheCallWhenTheMethodSaysItDepends`, `TestRegister_UndoCallNeedsAReversibleMethod`,
`TestConfigUndoCall`. A device with no writable file system still records no undo at run time; only the run can find
that out, and `UndoCall`'s doc comment says so.

**Why 156's fix did not prevent it.** 156 split whether from what: the undo itself is emitted per run, but whether a
method is reversible stayed one boolean per method. LESSONS 204 added a per-call answer for check mode alone
(`CheckCall`). When `net.ios.config` gained a parameter that turns its undo off, nothing asked the same question of
reversibility.

**Lesson.** When a parameter can turn off something a method declares, the declaration gets a per-call answer
beside it, and every plan-time rule asks that answer (LESSONS 204).

## 615. Windows: the active-run reader skipped every record, because Windows reports every writable file as group and world writable (a repeat of 544 and 567) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push.
`internal/journal/active.go` skips an active-run record whose mode has a group or world write bit, so a record
another user could have planted is not believed. Windows keeps no such bits and reports 0666 for every writable
file, so every record was skipped there and the notice that another run is active never fired.

**Root cause.** Product code read POSIX permission bits that Windows does not keep.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: a build-tagged `othersMayWrite` (`internal/journal/reader_unix.go`, `reader_other.go`) reads the
bits on Unix and answers no elsewhere. `TestOthersMayWrite_ReadsTheGroupAndWorldWriteBits` (Unix) and
`TestOthersMayWrite_IgnoresAModeThisSystemDoesNotKeep` (other systems). The Windows test compiles (`GOOS=windows`
vet) and has not run yet; the Windows leg of `make pr-check` will be its first run.

**Why 544's and 567's fixes did not prevent it.** Both guarded tests that assumed POSIX modes, and 567's lesson is
about tests. This is product code. The Windows leg runs a package only once a branch changes it, after the code is
written, and this branch had not run `make pr-check` yet.

**Lesson.** Any code that reads permission bits, not only a test, belongs in a build-tagged file with a Windows
answer.

## 616. Windows: project.write compared all nine permission bits, so every run reported changed (a repeat of 544 and 567) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push.
`pleiades.builtin.project.write` reports `changed` only when the file's bytes or mode differ. It compared all nine
permission bits. Windows keeps only a read-only flag and reports 0666 or 0444, so a requested 0600 never matched and
every run reported changed there.

**Root cause.** 615's: product code comparing POSIX permission bits that Windows does not keep.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: a build-tagged `modeHolds` (`internal/engine/project_mode_unix.go`, `project_mode_other.go`)
compares every permission bit on Unix and only the owner write bit elsewhere.
`TestModeHolds_ComparesEveryPermissionBitOnUnix` and `TestModeHolds_ComparesOnlyTheReadOnlyBit`. The second compiles
for Windows and has not run there yet.

**Why 544's and 567's fixes did not prevent it.** As in 615.

**Lesson.** As in 615.

## 617. A Telnet login resent the stored password when the device asked for it again, and each resend counted against the device's lockout (a repeat of 399) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push.
IOS answers a wrong line password by asking for the password again, with no refusal text. The new Telnet login
answered each question it saw, so it sent the same wrong password again, each time a failure counted against
`login block-for` or an AAA lockout.

**Root cause.** The login read only a refusal it could recognize by text. Over Telnet, the refusal is the question
asked again.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: a password or a name asked for again is `ErrLoginRefused`, and a login has at most three steps
(`maxLoginSteps`, `pkg/telnetexec`). `TestSession_LoginsThatGoWrong` asserts the password is sent once.

**Why 399's fix did not prevent it.** 399 taught the SSH dial to recognize the SSH library's refusal text and not
retry it, and LESSONS 265 states the rule. A Telnet login is a hand-written dialog with no protocol refusal, so each
new login path has to decide what a refusal looks like, and this one recognized only text. 594, on the same branch,
handled a refusal that arrives late, not one that is never said.

**Lesson.** In a login dialog, the same question asked twice is the answer no. Send a secret once per login.

## 618. project.write's path could be rendered from device output, its mode could set execute bits, and the project's .pleiades refusal (in ReadProjectFile too) was by name, which a Windows 8.3 short name passes (a repeat of 313 and 438) (fixed; a hard link at the project root is still open)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers. Three defects
in `pleiades.builtin.project.write` and the project file guard beneath it:

- Its `path` rendered like any parameter, so an expression reading `result.` let a device's output choose which
  project file the run replaced: `inventory.yaml`, a runbook, or a file beside the external Collections approval list.
- `mode` could set execute bits on a file the run wrote.
- The guard refused `.pleiades` by its name. On a Windows volume with 8.3 names, the same directory also answers to a
  short name such as `PLEIAD~1`, which the name check passes. The same check guards `ReadProjectFile`, which
  `file.copy`'s `src` uses and which is on `main` (`14d4ec22`, 2026-10-16), so on Windows `src` could read the
  project's credential files through the short name. This is reasoned from the code, not reproduced on Windows.

**Root cause.** A path that chooses what a run overwrites was treated as data a device may supply. And the guard
judged one spelling of a directory's name, while the file system resolves others.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`:

- `collection.ParamFormatProjectPath`: an expression in such a path may read only `vars`. `TemplateRule` checks it,
  now over `rollback:` steps too (`paramTasks`), and the engine checks it again at render.
  `TestTemplateRule_AProjectPathReadsOnlyVars`, `TestTemplateProblems_AProjectPathReadsOnlyVars`.
- Execute bits are refused.
- The guarded paths (the inventory, the state file, `PLEIADES_COLLECTIONS_DIR`) are matched by identity and by name.
  `TestWriteProjectFile_RefusesTheGuardedPaths`, `TestRefuseGuarded_MatchesByIdentity`,
  `TestCLI_ProjectWriteRefusesWhatARunMustNotReplace`.
- `.pleiades` is matched with `os.SameFile` against each prefix of the path, for reads and writes.
  `TestProjectFiles_RefuseThePleiadesShortName` runs on Windows only; it compiles and has not run yet. The Windows leg
  of `make pr-check` will be its first run.

**Still open.** The identity check compares directories. A hard link at the project root to a file inside
`.pleiades` can still be read through the project. Making one needs write access to both directories.

**Why 313's and 438's fixes did not prevent it.** Each fixed its own guard (`pkg/sftpxfer`'s containment, the engine
guard's request target), and their lesson, that a guard decides on what the far side will actually use, is a rule each
new guard has to remember. The project guard was written on Linux, where the name it compared is the only name the
directory has.

**Lesson.** A guard over a file system decides by identity, not by a spelling of a name. A parameter that chooses
which file a run replaces reads only values the author chose.

## 619. The lab importers printed the server's version and node state text raw, under a comment saying every word was quoted (a repeat of 257 and 368) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push.
`pleiades import-gns3` and `import-cml` printed the server's version, API version, node state and address with `%s`.
A server could put terminal control sequences in them. The comment above the print said every word from the server
was quoted.

**Root cause.** 257's and 368's class: text a remote system wrote reached the terminal raw. The comment claimed a
coverage nobody had checked (228's shape).

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: each server-supplied field passes through `termsafe.EscapeLine`, and the comment says quoted or
escaped. `TestCLI_ImportGNS3EscapesTheServersWords` (`cmd/pleiades/importgns3_escape_test.go`) proves it through the
binary: a server whose version and node status hold escape sequences has them printed as `\x1b...`, and no raw escape
reaches the output.

**Why 257's and 368's fixes did not prevent it.** `internal/termsafe` exists, but each print site has to call it, and
nothing finds a print of remote text that does not.

**Lesson.** Every field a server wrote goes through `termsafe` at the print, and a comment claiming that is checked
against each argument of the print it describes.

## 620. Telnet reads counted only data bytes and had no bound on a whole read, so a device that only negotiated, or sent a byte at a time, held a run until its context ended (a repeat of 175 and 351) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers. `pkg/telnetexec`'s
`readUntilQuiet` bounds the output it keeps, counting the data bytes left after Telnet negotiation is filtered out,
and waits for a quiet period that each new byte restarts. A device sending only negotiation (IAC sequences) never
added to the count, and one sending a byte just inside each quiet period never went quiet. Either held the read until
the run's context ended. `readUntilQuiet` is on `main` (`telnet_exec`); this branch added the Telnet login and
`Session.ReadUntil`, which had the same shape.

**Root cause.** The byte bound counted the filtered bytes, not the bytes read, and nothing bounded the time of a whole
read.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: `Options.MaxReadDuration` (five minutes by default) bounds a whole read, and a raw byte bound
(four times the output bound) counts every byte read, negotiation included, in both `readUntilQuiet` and
`Session.ReadUntil`. `TestSession_ADeviceThatNeverGoesQuietIsCutOff`.

**Why 175's and 351's fixes did not prevent it.** 175 bounded one accumulator in `pkg/rfc2217`'s negotiation parser,
and 351 put a deadline on a test helper's handshake. Each fixed its own instance. An idle deadline that every byte
renews looks like a bound and is not one against a peer that keeps sending.

**Lesson.** A read from a remote peer has three bounds: bytes kept, bytes read, and time for the whole read. A
deadline that each byte renews is none of them.

## 621. VarsRule's advice named --extra-vars for adhoc and rollback, which have no such flag, and the rule never read rollback: steps (a repeat of 270 and 574) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push. The
new `VarsRule` told an author of `pleiades adhoc` or `pleiades rollback` to supply a variable with `--extra-vars`,
which neither command has. And it read only a runbook's tasks, not their `rollback:` steps, which render when the
task is undone.

**Root cause.** The advice was written for `run` and `validate` and shown by every command that validates. The rule
walked the DAG's nodes, as the rules before it did.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: `WorldView.VariablesFlag` carries the flag the calling command has, if any, and the advice names
only that, or says the command takes no variables. The rule reads `rollback:` steps through `paramTasks`.
`TestVarsRule_ReadsRollbackStepsAndAdvisesOnlyAFlagTheCommandHas`,
`TestCLI_AVariableAdviceNamesOnlyAFlagTheCommandHas`.

**Why 270's and 574's fixes did not prevent it.** 270's lesson (follow your own instruction once before shipping it)
is a habit, and the advice was followed only from `run`. 574 was still open, and 608, written for this same rule on
this branch, named `rollback:` steps in its lesson but fixed only the conditional case. Its siblings 561 and 572 are
the same seam.

**Lesson.** Advice in a shared refusal names only what the command showing it has. A rule that reads a task's params
reads its `rollback:` steps through `paramTasks`.

## 622. The GNS3 fixture retried a lost port race only on the kernel's wording, not Docker's "port is already allocated" (a repeat of 601) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push.
`StartGNS3` retried a start only when the error said "address already in use". When the port's taker is another
container, Docker says "port is already allocated", and the fixture failed at once.

**Root cause.** 601's fix matched the one error text it had seen.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: `lostPortRace` (`internal/testsupport/gns3.go`) recognizes both.

**Why 601's fix did not prevent it.** It was written from one observed message, and the same race has two reporters:
the kernel when a process holds the port, Docker when a container does.

**Lesson.** A retry on an error's text lists every component that can report the same cause.

## 623. add-credential read a piped passphrase and a piped enable secret through two readers of one standard input, so the first reader's buffer took the second line (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push.
`pleiades add-credential --passphrase-stdin --enable-password-stdin` read each secret with its own reader. The first
read buffered past its line, so the enable secret was lost.

**Root cause.** Two buffered readers of one pipe. The class was known in the same command: the password and enable
secret pair beside it already reads both lines with one `prompt.SecretsFromStdin(2)`, with a comment saying why. The
new pair did not.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: one `SecretsFromStdin(2)` read, passphrase first. `TestCLI_AddCredentialStoresAnEnableSecret`
drives it through the binary.

**Lesson.** Every flag combination that reads more than one secret from standard input reads them through one
reader. When adding a stdin flag, check each pairing with the stdin flags already there.

## 624. import-cml --replace over SSH of a node first imported over Telnet kept transport: telnet (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push. A
node imported with `--via telnet` and then imported again over SSH with `--replace` kept its `transport: telnet`
property, so it was still reached over Telnet.

**Root cause.** The SSH spec wrote only `host` and `port`, relying on SSH being the default. A replace keeps what the
new spec does not write.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: the SSH spec writes `transport: ssh`. `TestCMLSpec_AReplaceOverSSHUndoesTelnet`.

**Lesson.** A spec that a replace applies writes every field any other form of it writes, the default value included.

## 625. net.trace chose its container path by a non-empty value while Manifest.For chose the call's shape by presence, so container: "" was checked as a container call and ran over SSH (a sibling of 115) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push.
Validation, admission and the engine held a `net.trace` call to the container shape whenever `container` was present
(`collection.Manifest.For`). The method traced from a container only when the value was non-empty. So `container: ""`
was validated against a container host and then traced over SSH, a shape nothing had checked the device for.

**Root cause.** Two readers of one parameter decided by different tests, as 115's prefill and checkbox did.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: an empty `container` is refused, and `For`'s contract (shape by presence) is documented.
`TestTrace_AnEmptyContainerKeepsTheShapeItWasCheckedFor`.

**Lesson.** A method that has a shape-choosing parameter decides by presence, as `Manifest.For` does, and refuses a
present but empty value.

## 626. A CML or GNS3 login error could quote the response body, which a 422 echoes with the password (a repeat of 457) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push. The
new `pkg/cml` and `pkg/gns3` clients quoted a failed login's response body in their error. A validation error (422)
can echo the submitted fields, the password among them.

**Root cause.** 457's class: an error quoting what it was answering, when that can carry a secret.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: a login answer is never quoted; the error names the status. `TestConnect_RefusesWhatItCannotUse`
(`pkg/cml`), `TestConnect_RefusesWhatItCannotRead` (`pkg/gns3`).

**Why 457's fix did not prevent it.** 457 fixed `kubeapi.checkServer`. Each new API client writes its own error path.

**Lesson.** A client never quotes the answer to a request that carried a secret.

## 627. net.ios.replace quoted every difference line in its errors, and telnetexec quoted up to 1 MiB of a device's question (a repeat of 431) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent's whole-branch review, 2026-10-23, on feat/lab-importers, before push.
`net.ios.replace`'s error quoted every line the device reported as different, with no limit, and a Telnet login's
error quoted the device's unexpected question up to the read bound, 1 MiB.

**Root cause.** 431's class and LESSONS 266: text a remote system wrote reached an error unbounded.

**Fix.** `01cdbb70`: at most ten difference lines (`TestShownDifferences`) and at most 80 bytes of a quoted prompt
(`TestSession_LoginsThatGoWrong`).

**Why 431's fix did not prevent it.** 431 bounded `kubeapi`'s error text. Each new error that quotes a device's output
needs its own bound, and nothing finds one that lacks it.

**Lesson.** Bound and escape remote text where it enters an error, every time (LESSONS 266).

## 628. Windows: a file standing where the active-run or journal directory belongs read as "no directory yet", because Windows reports a file opened as a directory as a path not found (a sibling of 615) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** `make pr-check`'s Windows leg, 2026-10-23, at `5dfb5361`: `TestActive_FailuresSayWhatFailed` failed on
win-check only ("a record directory that is a file was listed", "a journal directory that is a file was read"). Linux,
macOS and FreeBSD passed.

**Root cause.** `OtherActive` and `ChangesDuring` (`internal/journal/active.go`) treated `fs.ErrNotExist` from
`os.ReadDir` as "nothing recorded yet". On Unix, reading a file as a directory fails with ENOTDIR, which is not
`ErrNotExist`, so the error surfaced. On Windows the same read fails with "the system cannot find the path specified",
which Go maps to `ErrNotExist`, so a file in the directory's place silently read as an empty directory.

**Fix.** `readDirIfAny`: when a read reports not-exist, `os.Lstat` the path; absent is no entries, anything else
standing there is an error. Test `TestReadDirIfAny_TellsAMissingDirectoryFromSomethingElse` (a dangling link reaches
the same branch on Linux); the Windows leg of the next pr-check runs the original test.

**Why 615's fix did not prevent it.** 615 fixed the mode bits Windows reports; this is a different Windows answer, to
a different question (what a failed directory read means), in the same new file.

**Lesson.** On Windows, "not found" from a directory read does not mean nothing is there. Confirm absence with
`Lstat` before treating it as empty, wherever a file in the wrong place must be an error.

## 629. The GNS3 fixture's image build failed when Docker Desktop's credential helper did, under make pr-check, though the image needed no credential (a sibling of 601 and 622) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** `make pr-check` at `c2d7b8a6`, 2026-10-23: `TestCLI_ImportGNS3ReachesANodesConsole/2.2.61` failed in the
containers pass with `ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: error getting credentials - err: exit status 1`, then
passed re-run alone. The same pass's `TestCLI_NetworkChangeIsGatedAppliedAndUndone` also passed alone after Docker
Desktop never forwarded a lab router's published SSH port within two minutes (the 575 family, contention).

**Root cause.** `docker build` asks the configured credential helper (Docker Desktop's, through WSL) for the base
image's registry even when the image is cached and public, and that helper fails now and then under load. The
fixture took the helper's failure for the build's.

**Fix.** `StartGNS3` retries the build, up to three times, only when its output says `error getting credentials`.
Any other build failure fails at once.

**Why 601's and 622's fixes did not prevent it.** They retried the container's start on a lost port; this is the build
before it, a different external step with its own transient failure.

**Lesson.** Every step of a fixture that leans on Docker Desktop (build, pull, start, port publishing) has its own
transient failure under load; retry each on its own named error and nothing else.

## 630. The image build context grew past its 32 MiB ceiling, because the deny-by-default .dockerignore still let test files and test data in (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** PR #89's `containers (3)`, 2026-10-24: `TestPackagingReleaseGate_BuildContextIsBoundedAndExcludesWhatItMust`
(`tests/e2e/packaging_images_test.go`) failed, and again alone: "build context: 32.6 MiB across 3985 files", over the
32.0 MiB ceiling. `make pr-check` leaves `tests/e2e` to CI, so no local run could see it.

**Root cause.** `.dockerignore` allows `cmd/`, `internal/` and `pkg/` whole, which also brought every `_test.go` file
and every `testdata` tree into the context of the controller and runner images, though no build reads them. The
branch added about 1.7 MiB under those trees, a megabyte of it the Genie fixtures in `pkg/iosparse/testdata`, and the
context had only about 1.15 MiB of headroom left.

**Fix.** `.dockerignore` excludes `**/testdata` and `**/*_test.go` after its allowances: the context is 18.7 MiB.
`internal/testsupport`'s dockerignore tests (which derive the builds' real inputs from `go list -deps`) and the whole
packaging release gate (compose stack, images built and run unprivileged, Kubernetes install) pass.

**Lesson.** A size ceiling on a build context measures what the builds do not need as well as what they do; keep what
no build reads (tests, fixtures) out of the context rather than raising the ceiling when it is reached.

## 631. A test in a package that only consumes a changed one failed only in CI: pr-check selects the packages a branch changes, not their dependents (a sibling of 559) (open)

**Symptom.** PR #89's `containers (6)`, 2026-10-24: `TestConnection_WaitsForANetworkDevicesPrompt`
(`internal/catalog/wait/connection_test.go`) failed, and again alone: "the IOS device received ["terminal length 0"
"terminal width 512"], want only IOS's paging command". Commit 9ab84fe4 added `terminal width 512` to `netcli.IOS`'s
session setup and updated the counting tests in `internal/catalog/net/ios` and `pkg/netcli`, not this one.

**Root cause.** `make pr-check` runs the packages `tools/prscope` selects: those the branch changes, plus a fixed census
(559) for a few central packages. `internal/catalog/wait` was unchanged and only consumes `pkg/netcli` through
`wait.connection`, so no local run tested it, and the assertion pinning IOS's setup commands broke unseen.

**Fix.** The assertion expects both setup lines. The scope gap is open: prscope does not add the packages that
import a changed package (reverse dependents).

**Why 559's fix did not prevent it.** 559's census adds named consumers of a fixed list of central packages;
`pkg/netcli` is not on it, and a list cannot keep up with every consumer of every package.

**Lesson.** A change to a shared package's behavior needs its consumers' tests run before the push, not only its own:
select reverse dependents from the module graph rather than from a list. Plan it with the pr-check leg reruns
(memory note pr-check-leg-reruns).

**Resolution of the scope gap (fixed 2026-10-24 by `76cd78ce`; recorded 2026-11-06 on branch
`fix/open-patterns-fable`).** `76cd78ce` ("feat(prscope): run the direct importers of each changed package") built
this entry's lesson on the day the entry was written, and the index went on saying open for 13 days. `tools/prscope`
now runs every package that imports a changed one directly, in its code or its tests, and says so on standard error:
"prscope: N package(s) import a changed one, so they run too (FAILURE_PATTERNS 631)".
`TestChangedPackages_AddsEachDirectImporter` holds it, with this entry's case (`pkg/netcli` changed,
`internal/catalog/wait` run). The caveat stays: importers of importers do not run (for `pkg/netcli` that would be 209
of the module's 336 packages, by the commit's count), so a consumer two steps from a change is still CI's to find.
940 (2026-11-06) rested on this entry being open; see the note added to it.

## 632. A Telnet test's "device never goes quiet" depended on a 200 ms quiet window beating a 50 ms dribble, which a loaded Windows VM did not hold (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** `make pr-check` at `d1e221fa`, 2026-10-24, Windows leg's repeat pass:
`TestSession_ADeviceThatNeverGoesQuietIsCutOff` (`pkg/telnetexec/session_test.go`) passed twice, then failed with "a
dribble at login = <nil>": the login succeeded.

**Root cause.** The fake device wrote a byte every 50 ms and the client called it quiet after 200 ms of silence. On
the 2 GB win-check VM under the full parallel run, the device's goroutine stalled past 200 ms, the read went quiet,
and the login ended normally. The test asserted a timing margin, not the behavior.

**Fix.** The login case dribbles every 10 ms against a 2 s quiet window, so only a two-second stall could break it;
the read-to-prompt cases pause a full second after the prompt before a 300 ms quiet window, after which only the
phase's deadline or byte bound ends the read.

**Lesson.** A test that needs "never quiet" must leave a margin no scheduler stall on the slowest leg reaches:
seconds, not a 4x ratio of milliseconds.

## 633. A Shell call's watcher could close the session after the call returned, when the caller cancelled the call's context at once: net.cli's next read found EOF (a repeat of 352) (fixed)

**Symptom.** PR #89's `fast` job, 2026-10-24, strict repeat:
`TestOpenSession_SendsEveryConfigLineOverOneSession` (`internal/catalog/net/cli`) failed once in three with
`net.cli.config: netcli: remoteexec: read from shell on 127.0.0.1:35569: EOF`, in 0.00 s. It never failed in 300
local `-race` runs, on any GOMAXPROCS, and appears in no earlier failed CI run. Investigated before any rerun, at
the owner's choice.

**Root cause.** `remoteexec.Shell`'s `Shell`, `WriteLine` and `ReadUntil` each started a goroutine selecting between
`ctx.Done()` (close the session) and a `done` channel the call closed as it returned. net.cli gives every line its
own timeout context and cancels it the moment the line finishes. When the goroutine was not yet scheduled by then,
both cases were ready, `select` chose at random, and half the time the session was closed under the next line. A
loaded CI runner delays the goroutine; this machine rarely does. The race predates the branch.

**Fix.** `closeWhileRunning` (`pkg/remoteexec/shell.go`): `context.AfterFunc` closes the session if the context
ends during the call, and the stop the call defers guarantees it never runs afterwards. Proven by
`TestShell_ACancelAfterTheCallLeavesTheSessionOpen`, which cancels each call's context as it returns on one CPU:
it failed within the first three lines of every run before the fix, with CI's exact error, and passes 50 times on
1, 2 and 4 CPUs after. `conn.run`'s watcher has the same shape but closes a one-command session that has already
ended, so it is harmless and left as it is.

**Why 352's fix did not prevent it.** 352 found and fixed this race in `closeOnDone`, for the handshake, and said
why in its comment; the three identical watchers in `shell.go` were not swept for it.

**Lesson.** A goroutine that selects between "the context ended" and "the call is over" can choose either when both
are ready: stop the watcher before the call returns (`context.AfterFunc`'s stop, or a stop that waits for the
goroutine), and when one such watcher is fixed, sweep every watcher of the same shape.

## 634. tools/failures' captured logs matched *.log in .gitignore, so they were never committed and its tests failed on every machine but this one (a repeat of 401) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** `make pr-check` at `ae89f745`, 2026-10-24: the Mac and Windows legs failed nine `tools/failures` tests
with "open testdata/testgate-contention.log: no such file or directory". The Linux passes, run in the working tree
that held the files, passed.

**Root cause.** The package's fixtures are captured pr-check and Actions logs named `*.log`, which `.gitignore`
ignores. `git add tools/failures` skipped them without a word, and the machine legs test the committed tree
(`git archive`), not the working tree. CI would have failed the same way.

**Fix.** A `.gitignore` exception for `tools/failures/testdata/*.log`, the fixtures committed after reading them for
anything private (they name only documentation addresses, loopback and the runner's path), and
`internal/archtest`'s `TestNoTestdataFileIsIgnored`, which fails on any file under a `testdata` directory that
`.gitignore` matches (`git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard`). Proven both ways: it named the eleven
files with the exception removed and passes with it.

**Why 401's fix did not prevent it.** 401 added an exception for one path (`pkg/cloudinit/testdata/*.log`) and
`make test-clean-room`, which `pr-check` does not run. Nothing refused the class, so the next fixture named `.log`
fell into the same rule.

**Lesson.** A fix for an ignore rule that hides a fixture must cover every fixture, not the one found: check what
the rule hides under every `testdata` directory, as a test, not by remembering.

## 635. Windows: a file standing where the failure ledgers' directory belongs read as an empty ledger (a repeat of 628) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** `make pr-check`'s Windows leg, 2026-10-24, at `ae89f745`: `TestReadLedger_Contract` failed with "a
ledger under a file was read". Linux and macOS passed it.

**Root cause.** `readLedger` (`tools/failures/ledger.go`) treated `fs.ErrNotExist` from `os.ReadFile` as "no ledger
yet". Unix reports a path under a file as ENOTDIR; Windows reports it as path not found, which Go maps to
`ErrNotExist`.

**Fix.** `absentUnderDirectories`: when a read reports not-exist, the nearest ancestor that exists must be a
directory, or it is an error. `TestAbsentUnderDirectories` reaches that branch on every system, one and two levels
under a file.

**Why 628's fix did not prevent it.** 628 fixed `internal/journal`'s directory reads, in an unexported helper, and
`CI_LESSONS.md` rule 3 written the same day says to confirm absence with `Lstat`. The new tool was written before
either was read; no check finds a not-exist branch that skips the confirmation.

**Lesson.** Every "missing means empty" branch is a Windows bug until it confirms the absence. Read CI_LESSONS.md
before writing file-system code, including in tools.

## 636. Windows: a tools/failures test asserted the ledger directory's 0700 mode, which Windows does not keep (a repeat of 544, 567 and 615) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** `make pr-check`'s Windows leg at `90a4a3e7`, 2026-10-24: `TestAppendLedger_Dedups` failed with "the
ledger's directory: ... <nil>", the directory there but its mode not 0700. Every other leg passed it.

**Root cause.** The test compared `Mode().Perm()` with 0o700. Windows keeps no POSIX permission bits and reports
0777 for a directory.

**Fix.** The test checks the mode only where `runtime.GOOS` is not windows, and the directory's existence
everywhere.

**Why 544's, 567's and 615's fixes did not prevent it.** Each fixed the file it was found in, and CI_LESSONS rule 3
says a file-system assumption is a Windows bug until the Windows leg says otherwise. Nothing finds a permission
comparison with no Windows answer before that leg runs, and this one was written the same day 615 was recorded.

**Lesson.** A permission-bit assertion is the most repeated Windows defect here (544, 567, 615, 616, 636). When a
test or code compares `Mode().Perm()`, give Windows its answer in the same line or a build-tagged file, at the
moment it is written.

## 637. A test file named login_seed_ios_test.go built only for GOOS=ios, so its tests never ran on Linux (a repeat of 374 and 428) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-24, on feat/virt-cml. `7e917737` added `internal/engine/login_seed_ios_test.go`, the tests of
the Cisco IOS login seed. Go reads a trailing `_ios` as the GOOS of Apple's mobile system, so the file built for no
platform this project tests on, and its tests passed by not running. `internal/archtest`'s
`TestFileNamesConstrainBuildsOnlyOnPurpose` failed on the name.

**Root cause.** The file was named for its subject, IOS the router system, and `ios` is also a GOOS value. A name
that describes what the tests are about read to the toolchain as where they may run.

**Fix.** `bbf4ae95` renames it `internal/engine/login_seed_cisco_test.go`, with no other change.

**Why 374's and 428's fixes did not prevent it.** 374's fix was a rename and a lesson (put the OS word first), which
held only as long as it was remembered. 428 added the archtest that caught this one, so 428's fix did hold: the file
was refused before it was pushed. What did not hold is the habit. The archtest runs only when `internal/archtest`
runs, after the name is already in a commit; nothing warns at the moment a file is named.

**Lesson.** A vendor's system name can be a GOOS value (`ios`, `aix`, `solaris`, `zos`, `hurd`, `js`). Never end a
Go file name with one; name a Cisco IOS file for `cisco` or put `ios` first, and let the archtest catch the rest.

## 638. virt.cml's lab.create, node.create and link.create dropped the undo of what they made when a later read failed, so rollback could not remove it (a repeat of 452 and 563) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-24, on feat/virt-cml. `virt.cml.node.create` made the node, recorded its undo, and then read
the node's interfaces back. When that read failed, the method returned the error. The engine drops a failed task's
undo unless the method marks it to be kept, so the node existed with no undo in the journal: `pleiades rollback`
could not remove it, and a second run was refused on the node's label. `lab.create` and `link.create` had the same
order: a read after the change, and no mark on the undo.

**Root cause.** 452's class. The engine has kept a marked undo through a failure since `e3ab59fc` (2026-10-22):
`sdk.Inverse.KeepOnFailure` on the recorded undo, allowed per undo by `sdk.InverseSpec.MayKeepOnFailure` in the
manifest. The mechanism is opt-in, and the new methods did not opt in.

**Fix.** `815f4c0e`: each of the three records its undo as soon as the controller confirms the change, with
`KeepOnFailure: true`, and declares `MayKeepOnFailure` on that inverse in its manifest. The node's failure walk in
`internal/catalog/virt/cml/node/node_test.go` now requires the undo and its keep mark once the node is made, for a
failure of every later controller call. The engine's keeping of a marked undo is proven by
`internal/engine/rollback_kept_test.go` (`e3ab59fc`). The same commit names a link's nodes by id in its undo, not by
label (the class of 570), and answers could-not-check for a lab or node an earlier task makes.

**Why 452's and 563's fixes did not prevent it.** Each fixed its own methods. `e3ab59fc` then built the general
mechanism, but nothing requires a method that records an undo before a read that can fail to mark it, so a new
method gets 452's defect by default. 563's lesson also says an undo is proven where a rollback reads it, the journal;
the new test reads the undo from the method's context, below the step that would drop it, and no test named here
drives a `virt.cml` failure through to the journal.

**Lesson.** A method that makes something and then reads anything back marks its undo `KeepOnFailure` in the same
change that records it. Until a check enforces that, ask it of every new creating method in review.

## 639. Console reads in pkg/cmlconsole had only a byte bound and the task's context, which the Crawl tier leaves unbounded, so a silent console server held a run forever (a repeat of 620) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-24, on feat/virt-cml. `pkg/cmlconsole` (`1300569d`) reaches a node through a CML controller's
console server: it reads the server's `consoles> ` prompt, its answer to `connect`, and the node's login prompts.
Each read was bounded by a byte limit and by the task's context. A run sets no deadline by default, so a console
server that never prompted, or a line that stayed quiet, held the run with no end.

**Root cause.** The reads relied on the caller's context for time, and on the Crawl tier that context has no
deadline unless the task sets `timeout:`.

**Fix.** `38df8b73`: every read goes through one helper with its own time limit, 30 seconds for the console server
and 3 minutes for the node's login (long enough for a node still printing its boot log), and says "no answer within"
the limit. `TestReads_EndOnTheirOwn` in `pkg/cmlconsole/console_test.go`. The same commit logs out only from an exec
prompt (it asks for the prompt first and types nothing at a login prompt), cuts a server's refusal text on whole
characters, and names a credential with no username or password rather than reporting a refused login.

**Why 620's fix did not prevent it.** 620 bounded the time of a whole read in `pkg/telnetexec`, through its own
`Options.MaxReadDuration`. The console is a new reader over an SSH shell (`netcli.Shell`), written beside it, and
620's three bounds lived in that one package and in a lesson. Nothing shared the bound.

**Lesson.** 620's lesson applies to every new reader of a remote peer: bytes kept, bytes read, and time for the whole
read. A task's context is not a time bound on the Crawl tier.

## 640. pkg/netcfg.Mask had no pre-shared-key rule, so an IKEv2 keyring's key went out unmasked, and it masked the command word after crypto key (a repeat of 577) (fixed)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-24, the blind CVD lab's turn A. The agent built an IKEv2 keyring with a pre-shared key and saw
the key in plain text in `net.ios.replace`'s differences. The same lines reach `net.ios.config`'s differences and
`undo_lines`, `net.ios.parse` and `net.batfish.check`'s input. Two forms leaked: `pre-shared-key [local|remote] x`
inside an IKEv2 keyring, and an IKEv2 profile's `authentication local pre-share key x`, where Mask took `local` as
the secret and left the key. An ISAKMP keyring's `pre-shared-key address y key x` was also checked.

Later the same day, measuring `net.ios.config` against the lab's BR3, the opposite fault showed: Mask replaced the word
after `key` in `crypto key generate rsa ...` and `crypto key zeroize rsa ...`, so `undo_lines` held a line a rollback
could not replay, and it masked IOS's `% The key modulus size is 2048 bits` notice.

**Root cause.** Mask is a denylist (577): it masks the word after each secret word it knows, and `pre-shared-key`
was not one. `key` is one, and Mask had no list of the words after it that name a command.

**Fix.** `fa10a343`: `pre-shared-key` is a secret word, `local` and `remote` are skipped between it and its key, and
`address` and `hostname` name a peer whose key follows a later `key`; `local` and `remote` after `authentication` are
not secrets. `d6f47b1f`: the words after `key` that name a crypto key command (`generate`, `zeroize`, `modulus`,
`pubkey-chain` and eight more) are kept. `TestMask` in `pkg/netcfg/netcfg_test.go` holds each form, the generate and
zeroize lines and the measured notice. `changelog/ike-psk-mask.fixed.md` tells a user to rotate a key that went
through one of those outputs in an earlier run.

**Why 577's fix did not prevent it.** 577 left Mask a denylist by design and said so: a secret form not in the table
passes unmasked. 577's sweep listed RADIUS, TACACS, FHRP, RIP, NHRP and SNMP forms; IKE and IPsec keys were not
among them, and its lesson (write the tests from each vendor's list of secret-bearing commands) was not carried to
the crypto commands. The pre-shared key was on `main` from Phase 127b.

**Lesson.** A denylist mask is checked against the vendor's whole list of secret-bearing commands, crypto ones
first, and against the commands that share a secret word without holding a secret. A blind user found this one; a
review against IOS's command reference would have found it before.

## 641. kubernetes_cluster accepted tls_fingerprint and ignored it (a repeat of 441) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-24, on feat/virt-cml. `eb6faa41` added `tls_fingerprint` to `pkg/devicetls`, a SHA-256 pin of
one certificate for any device. A `kubernetes_cluster` record took the property, warned about it on every use, and
reached its API server through the Kubernetes client, which verifies against an authority and never reads the pin.
The pin appeared to work and did nothing.

**Root cause.** The property was added to the shared settings parser, so every device type that parses TLS settings
accepted it. The cluster's client builds its TLS from `tls_ca_pem` alone.

**Fix.** `39ca982f`: a cluster with `tls_fingerprint` is refused at construction, saying its API server is verified
against its authority and naming `tls_ca_pem`. `TestNewCluster_Refusals` in
`internal/inventory/devices/kubernetes/cluster_test.go` has the case.

**Why 441's fix did not prevent it.** 441 fixed `container_host`, whose TLS settings were parsed and not exposed, and
its lesson was to test a setting through its reader. The fix was for one type. Adding a setting to the shared parser
adds it to every type that parses it, and no test asks each type's reader to use, or refuse, each setting.

**Lesson.** When a shared settings parser gains a setting, list every device type that parses it and decide for
each: use it through its reader, with a test, or refuse it at construction.

## 642. An example and a test fake were written from remembered IOS wording that the device never prints (a repeat of 90) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-24, on feat/virt-cml, while building `net.ios.config`'s question answering (`a2495ddb`). A forked
subagent wrote an example and a test fake in which IOS asks "% You already have RSA keys defined ... Do you really
want to replace them? [yes/no]" when a key pair is made under a label that already has one. Measured on IOL XE 17.15
through `net.ios.config` on the lab's BR3, IOS prints "% You already have RSA keys defined named PLTEST." and "% They
will be replaced." and asks nothing. The example would have taught a
user to answer a question that never comes, and the fake would have proven a dialog that does not happen.

**Root cause.** The wording came from memory of IOS, not from a device. Nothing required a measurement behind it.

**Fix.** Before the commit, the example became the measured removal (`crypto key zeroize rsa`, whose question IOS
does ask), in `docs/reference/modules/net/ios/config.md` and `docs/16-network-verification.md`, and the fake follows
the measured transcript: `TestConfigWith_AKeyPairMadeTwiceAndRemoved` in `pkg/netcli/config_dialog_test.go` makes a
key pair, makes it again and removes it.

**Why 90's fix did not prevent it.** 90's lesson was to run the real tool before designing against it, and LESSONS
109 and 317 say the same of claims about another system. Each is a sentence. The subagent was given a task, not
those records, and a fake built from memory passes its own test.

**Lesson.** Device wording in an example or a fake is measured on a device, never recalled: name the device, its
release and the run in the commit or beside the fixture. A fake that cannot cite a transcript is a guess.

## 643. Closing a console session to abandon a refused question ran the logout, whose Enter answered the question yes (a repeat of 105) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent, 2026-10-24, on feat/virt-cml, before push. `38df8b73` made
`cmlconsole.LogOut` press Enter first, to find the node's prompt before typing. `netcli.Session.stop` abandons a
question a task refused, or one nobody answered, by closing the session, and on a console device that Close ran
`LogOut`. The Enter answered the pending question. IOS takes Enter at `[confirm]` as yes, so a task refusing reload's
`[confirm]` would have reloaded the router, and a refused `no username` `[confirm]` would have removed the user. The
task would have reported a refusal over the change it refused.

**Root cause.** Two rules, each right alone. The dialog's rule was "closing the session abandons the command", which
holds over SSH: the device drops the command when its session goes. A console line outlives the session, so the
question was still open when the session closed. `38df8b73`'s rule was "log out on every exit", and the refusal path
was one of those exits. Nothing asked what the logout's first keystroke would answer.

**Fix.** `4924895f`: `Session.stop` hands the question to a shell implementing `netcli.Abandoner` before it closes.
`cmlconsole.Abandon` answers `n` to `[confirm]` and `no` to `[yes/no]` (both measured on IOL XE 17.15 on the CVD
lab's BR3), types nothing at any other question and skips the logout then. A refused login is not logged out either,
since an Enter there is an empty password that counts toward a lockout (617's class). Tests:
`TestAbandon_DeclinesOnlyWhatIsCertain` and `TestLogIn_ARefusalIsErrRefused` in `pkg/cmlconsole/console_test.go`,
`TestDialog_AnAbandonerHearsTheQuestionBeforeItCloses` in `pkg/netcli/dialog_test.go`, and
`TestConsoleShell_AbandonsAQuestionWithoutAnsweringIt` in `pkg/sdk/console_test.go`.

**Why 105's fix did not prevent it.** 105's fix was local: one guard moved ahead of the deletions, inside a
transaction. Its lesson is about a guard and a multi-row write, and a session's close is neither, so nothing tied it
to a dialog's refusal. LESSONS 214 names the review that would have found it: list every path that could act without
the rule, here "a refused question is never answered", and test each. `38df8b73` changed what Close does without
listing who calls Close, and the refusal path was one caller.

**Lesson.** On a carrier that outlives the session (a console line), abandoning a command means declining it, never
closing and never pressing Enter. When a cleanup step starts typing, list every path that reaches it and ask what
each keystroke answers there.

## 644. pkg/netcfg.Mask masked a GRE tunnel's `tunnel key 100`, a number that is not a secret, because the last word after `key` is always taken as the secret (a repeat of 640) (fixed in 129a)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, blind CVD run 3, turn A, pleiades `0.0.0-dev+d17b732f8197`. The configuration `net.batfish.check`
sent to Batfish held `tunnel key pleiades-masked-...` where the candidate said `tunnel key 100`, the mGRE tunnel's GRE
key, an identifier and not a secret. Batfish could not use the line, and the agent had to accept `tunnel key` by name
with the reason "mGRE tunnel key 100, not a secret (masked by mistake)" (`~/pleiades-cvd/claude/project/runbooks/
model_check.yaml`, line 156). Mask's output also feeds `net.ios.config`'s differences and `undo_lines` and
`net.ios.parse` (640), so the same line would be masked there; that part is reasoned from the code, not observed.

**Root cause.** `key` is one of Mask's secret words. `maskLine` (`pkg/netcfg/mask.go`) skips small numbers, encryption
types and modes after a secret word so that `key 7 <secret>` masks the secret and not the `7`, but the skip loop runs
only while `j < len(ws)-1`. The last word is never skipped, so in `tunnel key 100` the `100` becomes the target and is
masked.

**Fix.** Planned in Phase 129a. Whatever the rule, a line whose secret really is a number (a numeric password) must
still be masked, so the fix names the non-secret command (`tunnel key`) rather than sparing every final number.

**Why 640's fix did not prevent it.** 640 added a list of the words after `key` that name a command (`keyCommands`:
`generate`, `zeroize` and others), written from the crypto key lines the lab printed then. `tunnel key` puts a number
after `key`, which neither that list nor the small-number skip handles. 640's lesson asked for a check against "the
commands that share a secret word without holding a secret"; the check covered the crypto commands only, not
interface commands.

**Lesson.** For each secret word, list from the vendor's command reference the commands where the word holds no
secret, and test each one. Where a word sits in a line says nothing about whether it is secret.

**Fixed (2026-10-25, `2b12066f`):** `maskLine` in `pkg/netcfg/mask.go` keeps `key` when it is the second word of a line
whose first word is `tunnel`, so `tunnel key 100` is no longer masked. The rule names the command, as planned, so a
numeric secret anywhere else is still masked. `TestMask_ByVendor` in `pkg/netcfg/netcfg_test.go` holds both sides: it
keeps `interface Tunnel100` with ` tunnel key 100`, and masks `98765` in `tacacs server t2` with ` key 98765`.

## 645. net.batfish.check's reach from a node[interface] start location ended in Batfish's TERMINATEDABNORMALLY, and route and no_route cannot name a VRF (fixed in 129c)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, blind CVD run 3, turn A. Model runs `ad98f613` and `4c4feb1f` asserted underlay reach from an
interface (`from: node[interface]`), and Batfish's traceroute answered TERMINATEDABNORMALLY. Nine ad hoc probes
narrowed it; `reach.from` refused Batfish's own quoted interface form, and a raw `reachability` question worked. In
run `ef01d6ac`, a `no_route` assertion for the default route failed on a router whose default route is in the
front-door VRF `WAN-TRANSPORT-INET`, since the assertion has no way to say which VRF it means. Turn A spent six model
runs and nine ad hoc probes (16:51 to 16:59) before `6a1a25e1` passed, and it dropped interface start locations
(`~/pleiades-cvd/runs/analysis-a.md`, section 4).

**Root cause.** `holdReach` (`internal/catalog/net/batfish/model.go`) asks Batfish's `traceroute` question with
`startLocation` `@enter(node[iface])` and headers holding `dstIps` only, no `srcIps`. The assertion parser
(`assertions.go`, the `kindReach` case) builds that location from `node[interface]` and refuses every other form.
Which part of the question Batfish fails on is not measured yet. `holdRoute` asks the `routes` question with `nodes`
and `network` only, so a route check covers whatever VRFs Batfish returns and cannot name one.

**Fix.** Planned in Phase 129c: reach from an interface either works or fails with a clear message, and `route` and
`no_route` take a VRF.

**Lesson.** An assertion that wraps a model's question is tested against the real model with every start location
form it accepts, not only from a node. A route check names its VRF, because which table answers depends on it.

**Fixed (2026-10-25, `2d54d27c`).** Measured on the pinned Batfish (2026.08.27.3685): a traceroute from
`@enter(node[iface])` in a non-default VRF ends TERMINATEDABNORMALLY, and a node[iface] start location (the node
originating from that interface) works. So `reach.from: node[interface]` now means the node sending from that
interface in its VRF; `@enter(node[interface])` must be written to mean a packet arriving on it, and in a VRF it fails
naming the working form instead of falling back (665). A quoted interface is accepted as Batfish writes it. `route`,
`no_route` and `routes_match` take `vrf`. NHRP joined the coverage table, since every `ip nhrp` line parses silently;
the mGRE tunnel's `tunnel mode gre multipoint` was already reported unrecognised. Proven by
`TestCheck_DMVPNInAFrontDoorVRF` (`internal/catalog/net/batfish/dmvpn_live_test.go`, a DMVPN hub and spoke in a
front-door VRF) and `TestReadParams_Refusals`.

## 646. IOS informational % lines from PKI and front-door VRF commands failed net.ios.config reruns and rollbacks, and a % line in show output failed net.ios.command (a repeat of run 1's notices, fixed in a2495ddb with no entry of its own; the class of 549) (fixed in 129a)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, blind CVD run 3, turn A. Four `net.ios.config` reruns failed on lines IOS had accepted, each
on one `%` line: "% Policy already has the same matching fvrf statement", "% certificate map already used in
ikev2/isakmp profiles" and "% Trustpoint ... is already configured". Three rollbacks failed on "% Be sure to ask the
CA administrator..." and "% Can't find policy". `net.ios.command` failed on `show` output that held "% Self-signed CA
certificate:". The reruns alone took 10 minutes (18:20 to 18:30).

**Root cause.** `netcli.IOS` reads every line that starts with "% " as a rejection unless it matches one of
`iosNotices` (`pkg/netcli/netcli.go`), a list of the notices measured in run 1. `Dialect.Rejection` runs over the
whole output, and `net.ios.command` calls it on a show command's output too (`internal/catalog/net/ios/command.go`),
so a "% " line a show command prints as data fails the task.

**Fix.** Planned in Phase 129a: each notice is measured on IOL XE 17.15 first, then added.

**Why run 1's fix did not prevent it.** Run 1's fix (`a2495ddb`, and `15271a27` for show output; recorded in LESSONS
323 as a friction item, with no failure pattern of its own) listed only the notices run 1 printed: duplicate access
list entries, IKEv2 proposals and profile matches, and the crypto key lines. The list is an allowlist on purpose, since
an unknown "% " line rejecting is the safe default. Run 1's design used a pre-shared key; run 3's used PKI and a
front-door VRF, whose commands print notices nobody had measured.

**Lesson.** A list of device notices grows by feature: before a design area (PKI, VRF-aware IKE) is called supported,
apply its commands twice and undo them on a real device, and add what it prints. A show command's output is data, so
a rejection check over it must tell a refused command from a "%" line the device prints as content.

**Fixed (2026-10-25, `2b12066f`):** each notice was measured first, on IOL XE 17.15.1 through `net.ios.config` with
`accept: '%.*'` (2026-10-25). Four are now notices in `pkg/netcli`'s `iosNotices`: "% certificate map already used in
ikev2/isakmp profiles", "% Profile already contains this keyring", "% Removing an enrolled trustpoint will destroy all
certificates" and "% Be sure to ask the CA administrator to revoke your certificates.". "% Specified proposal NOPE
does not exist" stays a rejection, so a mistyped name cannot pass for one already gone. Two notices from run 3 were
not reproduced and were not added: "% Policy already has the same matching fvrf statement" (`match fvrf any` applied
twice printed nothing) and a trustpoint's "already configured". "% Can't find policy", from a run 3 rollback, is
not in the list either, so that rollback would still fail on it. For show output, `net.ios.command` gained `accept` (through the same `readAccept`
as `net.ios.config`), and a read-only command now fails only on a `netcli.IOSCommandError`: "Invalid input",
"Incomplete command", "Ambiguous command", "Unrecognized command" or "%Error". So a "%" line a show command prints as
data no longer fails the task. Tests: `internal/catalog/net/ios/command_output_internal_test.go`.

## 647. pleiades adhoc required a hosts argument for a method that needs no device, took the method name as the hosts, and accepted localhost only because the target is never resolved (fixed in 129d, except that hosts given to such a method are still ignored)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, setting up blind CVD run 3: `pleiades adhoc groundconfig.search query=...` failed, reading the
method name as the hosts. Turn A met the same thing and passed `localhost`, which names no device in its inventory,
and the call worked. The skill tells an agent to use `adhoc` to call a method once.

**Root cause.** `adhoc`'s usage is `adhoc <hosts> <method> ...`, and `runAdhoc` (`cmd/pleiades/adhoc.go`) requires two
positionals before it writes the hosts into a runbook (`adhocRunbook`). Since Phase 117a, a task whose method needs no
device (`collection.ExecutionContext`'s `Device` none) skips `hosts:` and runs once (`engine.TaskTarget`), so any word
given as hosts is ignored for such a method. `adhoc` still asks for one.

**Fix.** Planned in Phase 129d: `adhoc` takes a method with no device and no hosts.

**Lesson.** When the engine stops needing an input for a kind of call, change every front end that asks for it. An
input that is silently ignored teaches an agent something false: `localhost` "worked".

**Fixed (2026-10-26, `2d9cd379`), in part.** `adhoc` takes a method that needs no device with no hosts, or with `-`
(`needsNoDevice`, `noHosts` in `cmd/pleiades/adhoc.go`), and a comma list of devices as one task per device with its
`target:`. `TestAdhoc_AMethodThatNeedsNoDeviceTakesNoHosts`, `TestAdhocRunbook_HostsForms`. Still open, reasoned from
the code and not run: hosts given to a method that needs no device (`localhost`) are still written as the runbook's
`hosts:`, and `engine.TaskTarget` still ignores them without a word.

## 648. --help exits 1 with "missing positional argument" for adhoc, rollback, add-credential and seal, and journal --help exits 2 printing nothing (a repeat of 562) (fixed in 129d)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, blind CVD run 3. `pleiades adhoc --help`, `rollback --help`, `add-credential --help` and
`seal --help` each exit 1 with "missing positional argument". `pleiades journal --help` exits 2 and prints nothing.
An agent that checks exit codes reads each as a failure.

**Root cause.** 562 said its cause was "not yet traced further". Read from the code now: `main` (`cmd/pleiades/main.go`)
prints any error a command returns and exits 1, and nothing maps `flag.ErrHelp` to 0. Commands that take a name call
`splitPositionals` (`cmd/pleiades/addhost.go`) and check the count before their flag set parses, so `--help` without
the names is refused as a missing argument. `journal`'s dispatcher (`cmd/pleiades/journal_cmd.go`) wraps
`errUnknownCommand` for `--help`, and `main` returns 2 for that error without printing it.

**Fix.** Planned in Phase 129d: `--help` exits 0 everywhere, without the command's names.

**Why 562's fix did not hold.** 562 has no fix. Its stopgap was a sentence in the skill, and a second blind agent met
the failure on four commands anyway.

**Lesson.** A defect an agent meets in its first commands is fixed, not documented around: a skill sentence did not
stop the next agent.

**Fixed (2026-10-26, `2d9cd379`).** See 562's resolution: every command's `--help` and `-h` exit 0, `journal list
--help` and `journal show -h` included, held by `TestEveryCommandsHelpExitsZero`.

## 649. A YAML alias in a runbook failed with "got a YAML node of kind 16", because normalization never resolves aliases (a sibling of 486) (fixed in 129d; its messages still print other node kinds as numbers)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, blind CVD run 3, turn A. A runbook using a YAML anchor and alias failed with "got a YAML node
of kind 16", which names neither the alias nor what to do.

**Root cause.** The runbook normalizer reads YAML nodes as written and does not follow an alias. Its errors print
`yaml.Node.Kind` with `%v` (`internal/engine/task_syntax.go`, three messages, and `internal/engine/conditional.go`),
and 16 is `yaml.AliasNode`. A helper that follows aliases, `yamlKeyTree.resolved` (`internal/engine/schema_keys_yaml.go`),
already exists and is not used there.

**Fix.** Planned in Phase 129d: aliases are resolved, or refused by name.

**Why 486 did not prevent it.** 486 taught the build-file reader to follow merge keys and aliases. That was a
different reader, and its lesson (a reader must read what the consumer reads) was not carried to the runbook parser.

**Lesson.** Every reader that walks YAML nodes either follows aliases and merge keys or refuses them by name. An error
never prints a library's enum number.

**Fixed (2026-10-26, `2d9cd379`, and `ac7af458` for 658).** `engine.ExpandAliases` (`internal/engine/yaml_aliases.go`)
expands anchors, aliases and merge keys before any key is read, bounded at 100,000 nodes and depth 64, and an
anchor parked under a top-level key is told where to write it. `TestBuild_ExpandsAliasesAndMergeKeys`. The task-form
warning reads the expanded runbook too (658). The lesson's second sentence is not done: `task_syntax.go` and
`conditional.go` still print `yaml.Node.Kind` as a number for the kinds they refuse, though no alias reaches them now.

## 650. net.ios.command reported ping, traceroute, terminal and debug as changes, so diagnostic runs blocked rollback (a repeat of 599) (fixed in 129a; its rollback side is named in 129c and still needs --despite-run)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, blind CVD run 3, turn A. Diagnostic `net.ios.command` runs (ping, traceroute, terminal
settings, debug) each reported changed. The journal then held them as later runs that changed the device, and
rollbacks needed up to six `--despite-run` flags.

**Root cause.** `iosShow` (`internal/catalog/net/ios/command.go`) counts only `show` and its abbreviations, and `dir`
and `more` in full, as commands that change nothing. Every other command reports changed.

**Fix.** Planned in Phase 129a for ping, traceroute and terminal, which change no configuration. `debug` changes device
state though not configuration, so it belongs to Phase 129c's rollback classification rather than the read list.

**Why 599's fix did not prevent it.** 599 named `show`, the read an agent runs to prove a second run changed nothing.
It did not list the other exec commands an agent runs to diagnose a network.

**Lesson.** Sort a device's exec commands by effect (configuration, session settings, device state, none) from its
command reference, not by the one command the last incident used.

**Fixed (2026-10-25, `2b12066f`), for ping, traceroute and terminal:** they join `dir` and `more` in
`readOnlyCommands` (`internal/catalog/net/ios/command.go`), so `net.ios.command` reports them unchanged. `debug` still
reports changed, since it changes device state and its undo is `undebug`. The rollback side of this entry (how a
later run that changed only device state is judged) stays open with 652, in Phase 129c.

**Rollback side, 2026-10-25 (`2d54d27c`).** A later run that changed a device is now named by its kind (652). A debug
run records no undo, so it is `cannot_undo`, and with `rollback: []` written on its task it is `nothing_to_undo`.
Either way it still needs `--despite-run` to step over, so this side is not closed.

## 651. A net.ios.command or net.ios.config timeout dropped the device's last output, so the question it waited on was never shown (fixed in 129a)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, blind CVD run 3, turn A. `net.ios.command` timed out three times on `request pkcs10` and
showed nothing the device had printed. The agent wrote an EEM diagnostic applet to read the one prompt, about 7
minutes.

**Root cause.** `Session.command` (`pkg/netcli/netcli.go`) returns an empty string with the error when its read fails,
dropping whatever it had read. `converse` (`pkg/netcli/dialog.go`) keeps only a last line shaped like a question.

**Fix.** Planned in Phase 129a: a timeout's error carries the device's last output. It must be masked and bounded, as
627 and 578 require of every output path.

**Lesson.** A timeout's error says what the far side printed last, masked and bounded. "Timed out" alone sends the user
off to build a probe of their own.

**Fixed (2026-10-25, `2b12066f`):** a failed read keeps what it read. `pkg/netcli/read_failure.go`'s `ReadFailure`
holds the output and never prints it in its own text; `netcli.LastOutput` returns it. `net.ios`'s `maskedError`
(`internal/catalog/net/ios/config.go`) appends "the device last printed:" with the last 20 lines, at most 1 KB, masked
with the rest of the error. `TestCommand_ATimeoutSaysWhatTheDeviceLastPrinted` in
`internal/catalog/net/ios/command_output_internal_test.go` holds it.

## 652. Rollback refused a later run that left nothing to undo (a node stop, then a start) the same way as one that must be undone first, and check mode judged each undo against the device as it is now (a sibling of 551) (fixed in 129c, except that changes which cancel out are still read as undo first)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, blind CVD run 3. Turn A's and turn C's core failure tests stopped a core router's node and
started it again. Rolling back the earlier build beneath those runs was refused, and the refusal suggested
`--despite-run` exactly as it would for a later run that must be undone first. Turn B read each of the four runs'
journals and then stepped over them with `--despite-run`. In turn A, rollback check mode reported three undos failing
that would have worked after the undos planned before them.

**Root cause.** `laterRunProblems` (`internal/rollback/history.go`) refuses for any later run that recorded a change
on the same device. It never classifies that run: changes that cancel out (a stop, then a start) are refused like
changes that must be undone first. Check mode runs each undo's check against the live device, not against the
device as the earlier undos would leave it.

**Fix.** Planned in Phase 129c.

**Lesson.** A refusal that offers an override must say which kind of case it is. When a harmless later run is
refused the same way as a conflicting one, users learn to pass the override, and the override then passes the
dangerous case too.

**Fixed (2026-10-25, `2d54d27c`), in part.** The journal records an empty `rollback:` list
(`authored_rollback_empty`, sqlite migration 0038 and postgres 0035). A refusal over a later run carries its kind
(`Problem.Kind`: `undo_first`, `cannot_undo`, `nothing_to_undo`) with advice for each, and `--json` gives it; a
refusal whose undo needs a runbook edited since opens with the `--runbook` hint (`KindNoRunbook`). A later run counts
as fully undone only when it had at least one real undo. In a rollback's check, a step on a device an earlier step
changes is provisional: its failed check is reported unchecked with the reason (`engine.WithProvisionalChecks`,
`rollback.Provisional`). Tests: `TestBuild_TellsLaterRunsApart`, `TestBuild_ARolledBackRunsNothingToUndoChangesCountAsUndone`,
`TestBuild_MarksAMissingRunbook`, `TestProvisional_NamesEveryStepAnEarlierStepPrecedes`,
`TestProvisionalChecks_AFailedProvisionalCheckIsUnchecked`, `TestRollbackCommand_FindsTheRunbookThatRan`. Still open:
changes that cancel out are not detected. This entry's own case, a stop and then a start, records undos, so it is
`undo_first` unless its runbook says `rollback: []`. Provisional checks are Crawl tier only (docs/10), and
`authored_rollback_empty` is trusted from the journal row, which needs write access to the journal to forge.

## 653. net.ios.command returned the device's text unmasked, so a show of the running configuration gave an IKEv2 pre-shared key in the clear (a repeat of 578) (fixed in 129a)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-25, measured live on the CML sandbox with this branch's binary before the fix. `net.ios.command`
running `show running-config | section keyring` returned an IKEv2 pre-shared key (24 characters) in the clear in its
`stdout`. From there it reached the run report, the run's text output and any register that held the result.

**Security.** This is a secret exposure. Anyone who can run a read-only show command through `net.ios.command`, or read
its report, output or a register, could read any key the device shows in the clear. A key that went through such a run
before this fix should be treated as exposed and rotated.

**Root cause.** Masking in the IOS package is done per method. `net.ios.config`, `net.ios.replace` and `net.ios.parse`
pass device text through `pkg/netcfg`; `net.ios.command` set `stdout` to the device's text as read
(`internal/catalog/net/ios/command.go`). The engine masks only the values it was told about, and a key that sits in
the device's configuration was never resolved by the run, so the engine did not know it.

**Fix.** `2b12066f`: `net.ios.command`'s `stdout` goes through `netcfg.MaskFound`, and every value it finds of 8 or
more characters (`netcfg.Learnable`, `netcfg.MinLearnedLength` = 8, the engine's own minimum) is registered for the
run (`learnSecrets`), so it is masked everywhere else the run writes it. Every named secret the project holds is
masked from the start of each run (`credential.SecretValues`, `engine.WithKnownSecrets`), whether or not the run uses
it. `net.ios.parse` and `net.ios.config`'s backup and running-configuration reads learn values the same way. Verified
live on the same sandbox: the same show then printed `pre-shared-key pleiades-masked-...`. The live gate
`TestCLI_ANamedSecretKeysAnIKEv2TunnelAndNeverShows` (`cmd/pleiades/cml_secret_release_gate_test.go`) requires that no
report, journal file or text output of its runs holds the key, a show of the configuration included.

**Why 578's fix did not prevent it.** 578 was the same shape in the FRR package: `net.frr.facts` masked its output and
`net.frr.command`, written beside it, did not. Its lesson was to mask once where the device's text comes in and to give
every new method a test that reads a secret back through it, and it said plainly that its own fix was still per path.
The lesson was applied to FRR only. `net.ios.command` already existed (added in `e933b71e`, 2026-10-20, two days
before 578's fix in `26dca552`), and nobody swept the IOS package. 640's `pre-shared-key` rule covers this line form,
but `net.ios.command` never called the mask, so 640's fix could not reach it either.

**Lesson.** A method that returns device text masks it, and a test reads a secret back through that method. Masking
only the values a run resolved is not enough: a secret the run never touched can still be in the device's text, so
the run must know every secret the project holds, and must learn the ones it finds.

## 654. On a Cisco IOS console line, the device's own log message and the prompt after it were read as the next command's answer, leaving the session one response behind (a sibling of 596 and 606) (fixed)

**Symptom.** 2026-10-26, the live CML gate `TestCLI_ANamedSecretKeysAnIKEv2TunnelAndNeverShows`
(`cmd/pleiades/cml_secret_release_gate_test.go`), extended in Phase 129d to run `wait.routes` on P2 through the CML
console. After the login, IOS printed its own syslog line (`%SEC_LOGIN-5-LOGIN_SUCCESS: ...`) and a prompt after it.
The session read that line and prompt as the whole answer to the next command it sent, and every command after that
got the answer of the one before. The same gate's `wait.routes` on P1 over SSH did not meet it. Methods that reached a
device through a console before this fix could have shown a log line as a command's output; that is reasoned from the
code, not observed.

**Root cause.** `Session.command` in `pkg/netcli/netcli.go` reads until the dialect's prompt and takes everything before
it as the answer. A device writes log messages on a console line between commands, each followed by a fresh prompt, so
a message that arrives before the command's echo ends the read early. Nothing in the dialect named such messages.

**Fix.** `7e941028`: `Dialect.AsyncMessage`, set for IOS to `iosAsyncMessage` (an optional sequence number and
timestamp, then `%FACILITY-SEVERITY-MNEMONIC:`), measured on IOL XE 17.15 through the CML console. When a read holds
nothing before its prompt but such messages and no echo of the line sent (`asyncOnly`), the session reads again, at
most `maxAsyncReads` (3) times. The fp-reviewer agent's review of `80d0da4d..7e941028` (its F5) found three gaps, fixed
in `ac7af458`: the re-read ran only in `Command`, not in `Dialog` (`net.ios.command`) or configuration lines
(`pkg/netcli/dialog.go`); a device that never echoes could be waited on, so the re-read now runs only once the device
has echoed a line (`echoes`, `noteEcho`); and a message with no timestamp (no `service timestamps log`) was missed.
Tests: `TestCommand_PassesOverTheDevicesOwnMessages`, `TestDialog_PassesOverTheDevicesOwnMessages`,
`TestCommand_ADeviceThatNeverEchoesIsReadAtOnce` (`pkg/netcli/async_message_test.go`); the first was checked by
mutation. The live gate then passed with `wait.routes` on P1 over SSH and P2 through the console.

**Why 596 and 606 did not prevent it.** Both found text the terminal adds around what the session expects: 596 a
shell's terminal query after the prompt, 606 an echo scrolled sideways. Each fix made the reader tolerate that one
form. Neither asked what else a device writes on its line unasked, and every earlier live IOS run went over SSH.

**Lesson.** A CLI session reader lists every source of text on its line: the echo, the answer, the prompt, and what the
device prints on its own between commands. A method that claims a carrier (SSH, Telnet, console) is run live through
each one; this message appears only on the console (LESSONS 335).

## 655. The device root's properties were a strip list of secret names, so any property named otherwise, an operator's own included, reached a template (a repeat of 458 and 577) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Review by the fp-reviewer agent of `80d0da4d..7e941028` (its F4), 2026-10-26, reasoned from the code. The
first device root (`internal/engine/device_root.go` in `7e941028`) gave a template and a condition every property of
the device that was a single text, number or boolean, except a reserved one or one whose name `redact.SecretName`
matched. A secret kept under a name that list does not match, or a value an operator stored for themselves, would reach
any template that reads `device.properties`. A template's output reaches a task's output and a device's command line.

**Security.** Had it shipped, anyone able to write a runbook could print a device property holding a secret under an
unlisted name. It was found before any push.

**Root cause.** The root was a denylist by name. Its own doc comment said what it may read "is allowed by what it is,
never everything not known to be secret"; the code did the opposite, the shape of 228 (a comment claiming more than the
code does).

**Fix.** `ac7af458`: an allowlist. The properties are only the keys the device's type declares its accessors read
(`record.DispatchProperties`, which `internal/archtest` holds free of any key naming a secret), and of those, never a
reserved key, a secret-named key (`redact.SecretName`) or a text shaped like a secret (`redact.SecretShaped`). Only
single texts, numbers and booleans are there. An operator's own grouping belongs in a tag, which the root carries.
`TestDeviceRoot_RendersAndDecidesPerDevice` refuses reads of `snmp_password`, a nested map, an operator's own `note`
and a declared key holding a key-shaped text.

**Why 458 and 577 did not prevent it.** 577's lesson ("a mask that names what to hide fails open") and LESSONS 190 ("a
content rule written as a denylist ... fails OPEN") are both in the records. They were written about masking and
content checks. Choosing what a template may read is the same decision, and the first draft did not treat it as one.

**Lesson.** What a template, an output or a log may read is an allowlist of what each value is (declared by its type,
shaped like no secret), never a list of names to strip (LESSONS 337).

## 656. Unit blocks, rollback_on_failure undo steps and rendered within: targets ran a task reading device by fewer rules than the per-device path, though validate accepted all three (a repeat in kind of 572 and 574) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Review by the fp-reviewer agent of `80d0da4d..7e941028` (its F1 and F2), 2026-10-26, reasoned from the
code. A task reading the device root runs through `runPerDevice` (`internal/engine/device_root.go`), which decides and
renders it once per device. Three other ways of running a task did not go through it. A task in a block that runs as
one unit (`internal/engine/handlers_run.go`) and an undo step that `rollback_on_failure` runs
(`internal/engine/rollback_on_failure.go`) got no device root, so a template reading `device` would fail at the moment
it ran. A task whose `target:` is rendered from data with `within:` resolved its devices from the unrendered text.
`pleiades validate` accepted all three.

**Root cause.** The per-device path was written for the forward walk of ordinary tasks. The other callers that prepare
a task (`run.prepare`) were not listed when it was added.

**Fix.** `ac7af458`: a unit's task that reads `device` runs through `runPerDevice`, every device reading the unit's
failure as `error`; an undo step is prepared with its device's root; and `renderTarget` renders a `within:` target
before its devices resolve. `TestDeviceRoot_EveryPathAndItsLimits` (`internal/engine/device_root_test.go`) covers the
rendered target, the unit block and an authored undo step reading `device` (`77bcc32e` added the undo case), and
`TestDevicePaths_FailureBranches` (`internal/engine/device_paths_test.go`) covers the failure branches of each of
those paths, including an undo step that cannot render.

**Why 572 and 574 did not prevent it.** Both found a path that runs a task (an undo step) held to fewer rules than the
forward run. LESSONS 309 says to list every caller of `run.prepare` before changing how a task runs. The device root
changed how a task is decided and rendered, and the sweep was not done for it.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 309 applies to any new way of running a task, not only to splitting the engine: list every caller
of `run.prepare` by reference, and give each a test.

## 657. A task reading device took lock_acquisition: all_at_plan_time and ran per device without it, with no word (a repeat in kind of 540) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Review by the fp-reviewer agent of `80d0da4d..7e941028` (its F3), 2026-10-26, reasoned from the code. A
task reading the device root runs once per device. `lock_acquisition: all_at_plan_time` asks for every device's lock
