**Fix.** `7f7a8ed3`: `fnmatchPattern` (`internal/catalog/facts/gather.go`) translates a pattern into `path.Match`'s
grammar (`[!` becomes `[^`) before both the malformed-pattern check and every match. Keys hold no slash, so the two
agree on what `*` spans. Test: `TestGatherMatches_ReadsFnmatchsNegation`.

**Found on review.** The branch's fp-reviewer agent, 2026-11-05, before push: two more constructs the grammars spell
differently. fnmatch also reads `[^a]` as a class holding `^` and `a`, where `path.Match` reads every character but
`a`, and fnmatch has no escape, so a backslash is an ordinary character, where `path.Match` reads it as an escape.
Fixed in `529c032c`: `fnmatchPattern` escapes a `^` that opens a class and doubles each backslash. Tests: new cases in
`TestGatherMatches_ReadsFnmatchsNegation` (`[^a]` becomes `[\^a]`, `a\[!b]` becomes `a\\[^b]`, and the matches each
gives).

**Lesson.** When a parameter takes another program's pattern language, translate it into the matcher's, and test the
constructs the two spell differently.

## 935. launchd never reported a disabled daemon, so it vanished from the facts at reboot, and its status was the last exit status, which moves on an unchanged Mac (its status a repeat in kind of 870 and 874) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the API-model review sweep on 2026-11-04 (facts verdicts, item 16) and the macOS review; fixed
on 2026-11-05 on `fix/facts-sweep-gatherers`, before push. launchd does not load a disabled daemon, so `launchctl
print system`'s services block never lists one. `parseLaunchd` read only that block, so a daemon disabled since boot
was missing from the facts and read as removed after a reboot. And the stored `status` was the last exit status
`launchctl` prints, which changes each time an on-demand daemon runs or is killed, on a Mac nobody changed.

**Root cause.** The list came from the loaded set, not the configured one. The status field held a runtime value no
other service source puts there.

**Why 870 and 874 did not hold.** As in 927, a field that moves on its own was stored as stable state, and each
earlier fix lives in its own probe. Sweep item 10 holds the rest of the question.

**Fix.** `7f7a8ed3` (`internal/catalog/facts/gather_bsd_items.go`): each label in `launchctl print-disabled system`
that the services block does not list is reported `stopped`, not enabled, status `disabled`; every status is now
`enabled` or `disabled` (`launchdStatus`). `55ea70bc` added `checkLaunchd`, which refuses an answer with no services
block. Test: `TestDarwinParsers_ReadBrewPkgutilAndLaunchd`, updated for both changes.

**Found on review.** The branch's fp-reviewer agent, 2026-11-05, before push: `launchctl print-disabled system` keeps
an override for a daemon after it is uninstalled, so the fix would have reported a removed daemon as present and
disabled for as long as its override stayed. Fixed in `529c032c`: the probe also lists `/System/Library/LaunchDaemons`
and `/Library/LaunchDaemons`, and a disabled daemon is reported only while its plist is in one of them
(`gather_bsd_items.go`). Test: the fixture case `com.example.removed` in
`TestDarwinParsers_ReadBrewPkgutilAndLaunchd`.

**Lesson.** A service list comes from what is configured, not only from what is loaded, and each field means the same
thing across every source that fills it.

## 936. After facts.Resumed wrote a value back at its last sighting, a late observation of the same value just before it added a second row of that value, which read as a change from A to A (a repeat of 923, a case its fix opened) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found on PR #117's own review on 2026-11-05, not by the sweep; fixed on 2026-11-05 on
`fix/facts-sweep-gatherers`, before push. 923's fix (`facts.Resumed`) writes back the value that was current before a
late change, dated at its last sighting. A value A confirmed at 11 and again at 15 comes back dated 15. A late
observation of A at 12 then lands just before that row, and the history reads A, B, A@12, A@15: two rows of one value
in a row, which a reader takes as a change from A to A. The conformance case "a value that follows itself in the
history reads as one" was red on the old code.

**Root cause.** Write-on-change keeps one row per change and only the last sighting of each value, so a written-back
value cannot be dated at the sighting that actually followed the late change.

**Why 923 did not hold.** 923's fix was tested by what the next in-order run records; no case sent a second late
observation of the value it had written back.

**Fix.** `a21b15e7`: `InRunOrder` (`internal/facts/file_store.go`), which both stores' histories use, merges
consecutive entries of the same hash and kind on read (`mergeRepeats`, `internal/facts/late.go`): first observed as
the earlier says, last confirmed as whichever was confirmed later. The stored rows and the chain are untouched. Test:
the conformance case above, in `internal/facts/factstest`, run by both stores.

**Open.** Dating a written-back value exactly needs per-sighting history, which conflicts with write-on-change. The
choice (leave it documented, keep per-sighting rows with a retention bound, or keep the first and last sighting per
spell) is the owner's, before Phase 41d.

**Lesson.** A fix that writes a row back is tested with the late arrivals that land next to the row it wrote.

## 937. file.remove's new check refusal took remotefile.Removable's no as the device's no, but Removable also answered no where it could not tell (root under a BusyBox shell), so every rollback check of a recorded file.remove undo on an Alpine root login would have failed, with advice a recorded undo cannot follow (a repeat in kind of 270, 488, 600 and 621; LESSONS 138) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the branch's fp-reviewer agent on 2026-11-05, on `fix/facts-sweep-gatherers`, before push.
`6539ed41`, this branch's own change, made `file.remove`'s check refuse a removal by default when
`remotefile.Removable` answered no, and its message told the author to set `check_forbidden: warn` "where the
device's permissions cannot be read as they apply". `Removable` answers no for a root login under a BusyBox shell
whether or not the removal would work, because there it cannot tell. So a check of `file.remove` as root on an Alpine
host failed by default. A rollback check is worse: the undo's params come from the run journal, so an author has no
task on which to set `check_forbidden: warn`, and every rollback check of a recorded `file.remove` undo on such a
login would have failed with advice that cannot be followed.

**Root cause.** `Removable` has two answers (yes, or no) for three states (allowed, refused, cannot tell). 812's fix
mapped "cannot tell" to no on purpose, which was safe while every caller leaned only on a yes (the check's ledger of
predicted removals). `6539ed41` added the first caller that acts on a no, and it read the folded answer as the
device's own.

**Why 270, 488, 600 and 621 did not hold.** Each is a refusal whose advice does not work for the person who sees it,
and each lesson says to follow the advice once from every place the refusal can be shown. Here the advice was written
for a task an author writes, and the refusal is also shown by a rollback check, whose undo nobody writes by hand.
LESSONS 138 (give "I could not look" a third answer) was applied in 925 on this branch to the facts families and not
to `Removable`, whose own comment already said it answers no where it cannot tell.

**Fix.** `c70f147e`. The removable script (`pkg/remotefile/locate.go`) exits 3 for "the shell cannot tell" (root
under BusyBox), where it exited 1. `remotefile.RemovableKnown` reports whether the answer was known; `Removable` keeps
its meaning for its other callers (no unless known and allowed). `file.remove`'s check
(`internal/catalog/file/remove.go`) refuses only a no the device gave, warns (`sdk.RecordWarnings`) where the device
cannot say, and still warns on a no when the task sets `check_forbidden: warn`. Measured:
`TestRemovableScript_RefusesWhatItCannotVouchFor` runs the script under BusyBox as root through `unshare -r` on this
machine and now expects exit 3. No test drives `file.remove`'s new warning through a real BusyBox root login; that
branch rests on the measured exit code and on reading the code.

**Lesson.** When a new caller acts on an answer that an older caller only leaned on, read what that answer folds
together before refusing on it. A refusal's advice is followed once from every path that can show it, the
generated ones (a rollback, a converted playbook) included.

## 938. govulncheck failed main's push run after pull request #117 merged, on GO-2026-6865 in klauspost/compress v1.20.0, an advisory published after the pull request's checks had passed (a repeat in kind of 552) (fixed)

**Symptom.** 2026-11-05, GitHub Actions run 42131068662, the push run on `main` at `dd91a345` after pull request #117
merged. Only govulncheck failed, in the `ci (ubuntu-24.04, true)` job: GO-2026-6865, a panic on two-block frames in
`klauspost/compress` v1.20.0 (its `fse` and `huff0` packages). The trace: `internal/api/projects.go:407`,
`api.ProjectHandler.StreamSyncLogs` calls `middleware.compressResponseWriter.Flush`, which eventually calls
`fse.Compress`. The pull request's own checks had passed; no code changed between them and the push run.

**Root cause.** The commit had not changed; the advisory database had. GO-2026-6865 was published after the pull
request's checks ran, so the first scan to see it was main's push run. The module is an indirect dependency.

**Security finding.** The weakness is a panic in the compressor on two-block frames. This module reaches it when the
Controller compresses a project's sync log stream (the trace above). What input triggers it, and so what an attacker
would need, was not measured here. A fixed release exists, v1.20.2, and taking it changed only `go.mod` and `go.sum`;
the build and vet are unchanged. Confidence: reasoned from govulncheck's call trace, not reproduced.

**Why 552 did not hold.** 552 is the same cause (a check's answer moved without the commit moving, because the
advisory database moved), seen there as a memory kill at pr-check. Its fix pinned the toolchain and moved where the
scan runs; nothing can make a scan see an advisory before it is published, and this one surfaced where the design
expects: main's push run and the scheduled `vulns` job.

**Fix.** `60f50721` on `fix/facts-sweep-gatherers`: `klauspost/compress` v1.20.2. `main` stays red on govulncheck until
this branch merges. The Actions ledger holds the run (`record-actions`); its entry is a job (`leg`) entry, which
`tools/failures annotate` does not match, so it carries no pattern number.

**Lesson.** A govulncheck failure on a commit that already passed is a new advisory, not a regression: read its trace,
take the released fix as its own commit on the branch in hand, and report it as a security finding. A rerun cannot
turn it green.

## 939. POST /jobs/{id}/rollback merged a request's method_settings over the job's own without the template's lock that a launch is held to, so a caller could set on a rollback what the template's author had locked (a repeat in kind of 268; LESSONS 363) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer on 2026-11-06, on `feat/method-run-settings`, before push, by reading the code;
not observed on a Controller. A launch takes the runbook kind's `method_settings` field only when the template opens
it (`Promptable`). `Dispatcher.Rollback` (`internal/api/dispatcher_rollback.go`) took `RollbackRequest.MethodSettings`
and merged them over the job's own settings without asking the template. So a caller could set, on the rollback job,
a run setting the template's author had locked: `file.remove.check_forbidden: warn` over a template that keeps the
default `refuse`.

**Security finding.** The weakness: a per-template lock on a launch field was enforced at launch and not on a route
that builds a job from a job. Our code reached it through `POST /jobs/{id}/rollback` into `Dispatcher.Rollback`'s
merge. A caller needed `runbook:execute` (the route's scope) and a finished job from a template that does not open
`method_settings`. What it got: today, only a check's refusal turned into a warning, since the one run setting is
`file.remove`'s `check_forbidden` and a real run ignores it. A later run setting that changes what a real run does
would have widened this. No upstream code is involved. Confidence: reasoned from the code; the fix's test proves the
lock now holds.

**Root cause.** The rollback route does not go through `LaunchTemplate`'s resolver, which is where a launch meets the
template's open fields. It already applied one template rule of its own (`refuseUnrepeatableCredentials`), so the
lock had to be added there by hand, and the new field's lock was not.

**Why 268 did not hold.** 268's lesson is that any mechanism which causes work to happen has to check the permission
to do that work. Its fix was a scope check at a schedule's write. A rollback is a second door into a job, and the
rule a new launch field carries (the template's lock) has to be added at each door. LESSONS 363 (check a rule along
every route a method can take, each path that runs an undo included) names this. The branch carried the settings
themselves to every route (the CLI's rollback, the Runner, the rollback route), but carried the template's lock only
along the launch.

**Fix.** `0c44e498`. A job launched from a template takes a rollback request's `method_settings` only when the
template opens the field (`tmpl.Promptable(launch.MethodSettingsField)`), and is refused otherwise with a 422
(`api.ErrSettingLocked`). A job launched without a template is unchanged. The job page's rollback form gained the
field, each entry held to its method. `TestRollback_MethodSettingsAreHeldToTheTemplatesLock`
(`internal/api/dispatcher_rollback_test.go`) and `TestRollbackRunSettings_HoldsEachToItsMethod`
(`internal/ui/resources/jobs/rollback_test.go`). No end-to-end test runs the rollback route through to a Runner yet.

**Lesson.** A new launch field is held to the template's lock at every route that creates a job, not only at
launch: list the routes (launch, saved configuration, schedule, relaunch, rollback, check) when the field is added,
and give each one a test.

## 940. internal/forge/collectionscaffold's renderDoc dropped the new collection.Param.RunSetting, and its every-field fixture would have failed only in CI's fast job, since pr-check selects neither that package nor its census (a repeat of 631, which is open; LESSONS 380) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer on 2026-11-06, on `feat/method-run-settings`, before push. Commit `6f79f42f`
added `RunSetting` to `collection.Param`. `renderDoc` (`internal/forge/collectionscaffold/docrender.go`), which writes
a method's `Doc` as Go source for `forge new-collection --doc-json` and for `go generate` over
`internal/forge/catalogdata`, wrote every `Param` field but the new one. A scaffolded method would have come out with
no run setting. The package's fixture test (`fullyPopulatedDoc`, held by `assertNoZeroFields` through `reflect`) fails
when a field is left zero, so it would have failed once `collectionscaffold` was tested.

**Root cause.** `tools/prscope` selects the packages a branch changes plus a fixed census. `collectionscaffold` was
unchanged and is not on the census list for `pkg/collection`, so `make pr-check` would not have run its tests. The
first run to see it would have been CI's `fast` job, after the push.

**Why 631 did not hold.** 631 is still open: prscope does not add the packages that import a changed package. Its
lesson (select reverse dependents from the module graph) has not been built. LESSONS 380's rule (run `tools/gendocs`'
tests when a counted property moves) covers one known consumer, not this one.

**Fix.** `6cebdd23`. `renderDoc` writes `RunSetting: true`, and the fixture sets the field. The scope gap stays open
under 631.

**Lesson.** A field added to a type that a renderer or scaffold reflects over needs that consumer's tests run in the
same commit, whatever pr-check selects. Until 631 is built, list a changed type's reverse dependents by hand
(`go_symbol_references` on the type) and run the ones that copy or render every field.

**Note (2026-11-06, branch `fix/open-patterns-fable`).** The root cause above rests on 631 being open, and it was not:
`76cd78ce` (2026-10-24) made prscope run every direct importer of a changed package. `go list` shows
`internal/forge/collectionscaffold` importing `pkg/collection` directly, and `6f79f42f` changed `pkg/collection`, so by
prscope's code pr-check would have selected it. This is reasoned from the import graph and prscope's code, not
measured by running prscope at that commit. The fix and the lesson stand. Only a consumer two steps from the change
would still be left to CI.

## 941. A run setting's refusal quoted the value it refused ("got %q"), so a value pasted into the wrong place would be printed back in the CLI's message and the API's 422 (a repeat of 457, the class of 298 and LESSONS 266) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer on 2026-11-06, on `feat/method-run-settings`, before push.
`collection.CheckRunSetting` (`pkg/collection/run_settings.go`) refused a value outside a setting's choices with `run
setting %q must be one of %s, got %q`, quoting the value. That error reaches the terminal for `--setting`, a launch's
or a rollback's 422, and a Runner's refusal of a dispatch (`RunSettings.Check`).

**Root cause.** The class of 298 and 457: a validator's error quotes the input it refused. A run setting is one word
of a closed set, so a correct value is never secret; a wrong one can be anything, a secret typed into the wrong field
included.

**Why 457 did not hold.** 457's lesson is to name the problem instead of the input when the input can carry a secret.
It was read as being about inputs that are meant to hold one (addresses, URLs). A field of choice words looks safe,
and the thing it can carry is a mistake, not its purpose.

**Fix.** `f5cb8a61`. The refusal names the setting and its choices, never the value. `0c44e498` gave the job page's
rollback form the same rule: a malformed entry is refused without echoing what was typed.
`TestRollbackRunSettings_HoldsEachToItsMethod` (`internal/ui/resources/jobs/rollback_test.go`) asserts that the form's
refusals hold neither a typed secret nor the refused value. `TestCheckRunSetting_NamesWhatIsWrong` and the BusyBox
gate's refused cases assert the message `must be one of refuse, warn`, not the value's absence.

**Lesson.** A refusal of a value that should be one of a closed set lists the set and never quotes the value: what
fails to match the set is exactly what nobody checked.

## 942. The proof's port holder dropped its connections and Go's finalizers closed them, so the first proof of 470's cause showed held ports working (a repeat in kind of 436 and 679) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** 2026-11-06, branch `fix/docker-desktop-lost-ports`, proving 470's cause. The first run of the harness that
held ports and then started containers showed containers on "held" ports answering, which read as evidence against
the cause.

**Root cause.** The helper that held the ports opened each connection and discarded the `net.Conn` it got back. Go
closes a socket's file descriptor through a finalizer once nothing refers to it, so after a garbage collection the
ports were free again before the containers drew them. The harness never checked that the ports were still held when
it measured. It is the class of 436 and 679, a check that passes without its precondition; here the language undid
the precondition silently.

**Fix.** The helper keeps every connection it opens until the measurement ends. With the connections kept, the proof
gave 470's result: 8 of 8 containers on held ports refused, 32 of 32 others answered.

**Lesson.** An instrument that holds a resource for a proof keeps a live reference to it until the measurement ends,
and the proof checks its precondition at the moment it measures (the socket table holds the port), not the helper's
own count. A proof that contradicts a well-supported diagnosis is a reason to test the proof first (LESSONS 357: an
instrument is a check too).

## 943. Startup output with no trailing newline (a printf in ~/.ssh/rc) ran into the first line of each answer a detached run reads, so the start's answer named no job directory and the job just started was stopped and its task failed (a repeat of 900, a case its fix left) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** 2026-11-06, branch `fix/remoteexec-detach-hardening`, before push. Found by an independent review of
`1bb5288e`'s diff by a second model (LESSONS 392; Batch API, $1.25), then measured against the sshd container before
the fix. With `~/.ssh/rc` printing text that does not end in a newline (a `printf`, or `echo -n` in zsh's `.zshenv`),
the start's answer read `welcome/config/.pleiades-async-1000/job.<name>`: the banner and the job directory on one line.
That is no job directory, so the run stopped the job it had just started and failed the task. The poll's marked line
(`xpleiades-rc=0`) and the job file's marker line would break the same way; that part is read from the code, not run
on its own.

**Root cause.** `lastLine` and `afterMarker` read each answer from a line of its own. The start script, the poll and
`readJobFile` printed their answer first, which starts a line only when the output before it ended one.

**Why 900 did not hold.** 900 (and 779 before it, for the start) made each answer a marked line: the directory as the
last line, the status after `rcPrefix`, a job file after a marker line. Both assumed that whatever the login printed
first ended with a newline. 900's test, `TestSSHContainer_ADetachedCommandSurvivesStartupOutput`, wrote `~/.ssh/rc` as
`echo <banner>`, which does, so the other case was never run.

**Fix.** `649d5890`. Every answer leads with a newline of its own: an `echo` before the start script's `echo "$d"`, the
poll's `printf '\n<rcPrefix>'`, and an `echo` before the job file's marker (`pkg/remoteexec/detach.go`,
`detach_script.go`). `TestSSHContainer_ADetachedCommandSurvivesStartupOutput`
(`internal/transport/ssh/ssh_detach_container_test.go`) is now a table over a banner line and a banner with no
newline; before the fix the second failed with the error above, and both pass now.
`TestSSHContainer_ADetachedCommandWithNoSetsidIsStillStopped` and `TestAsyncReleaseGate_DetachedOnARunner`
(`cmd/runner`) pass with it.

**Lesson.** A marker that must start a line writes that newline itself, because text a login prints ahead of it need
not end in one. A test of startup output includes a banner with no trailing newline.

## 944. withoutCommand took any start error holding the command line for the server's refusal, so a short Raw-view command inside another error ("session" in "ssh: session already started") came back as ErrCommandRefused and the real cause was lost (a repeat in kind of 820, at a case 898's fix opened) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Carried on 2026-11-06 from work left in `stash@{0}` on 2026-11-04 (branch `fix/ssh-sweep-b`), after
checking that work hunk by hunk against `main`. `withoutCommand` (`pkg/remoteexec/conn_watch.go`), added by 898's fix,
replaced a start error with `ErrCommandRefused` whenever the error's text contained the command line. A Raw view sends
a command as written, so the line can be one short word, and a short word can sit inside an unrelated error. With the
line `session`, Start's own `ssh: session already started` was read as the server refusing a command, and the caller
was told the wrong thing. Not seen in a run. `TestWithoutCommand_KeepsOtherErrors` shows it and fails on `main`'s
code. (`1bb5288e`'s message gives a channel-open failure as its example; `649d5890` changed the test to an error Start
really returns.)

**Root cause.** The class of 820: a match on text that a path other than the intended one can produce too. Here the
matched text was a value the caller supplies (the command), tested for as a substring of text from somewhere else.

**Why 898's fix did not hold.** 898 asked "does this error quote the command?" and answered it with `strings.Contains`,
which is true of the refusal and of any error that happens to hold a short command. Its test used a dropped connection
and the line `echo hi`, which no other error holds.

**Fix.** `1bb5288e`: only x/crypto/ssh's whole text, `"ssh: command " + line + " failed"` (`ssh: command %v failed` in
its `session.go`), becomes `ErrCommandRefused`; any other error is returned as it is. The test asserts both: Start's
own error with the line `session` is kept, and the refusal itself is still `ErrCommandRefused`. The exact match depends
on the library's format; `TestSSHContainer_ARefusedCommandIsNotInItsError`
(`internal/transport/ssh/ssh_refused_exec_container_test.go`, from 898) runs a real refusal and fails if an update
changes that text, which would otherwise put the command back in the error.

**Lesson.** Classify an error by the whole text its source writes, or by its type, never by whether it contains a
value the caller supplied: a short value turns up inside other errors.

## 945. A detached start's answer was accepted as any job directory, not this job's own, so a damaged answer could have had the run poll, read and remove another job's directory (a repeat of 902, a case its fix left; the class of 313) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Carried on 2026-11-06 from the same 2026-11-04 stash as 944. `runDetached` (`pkg/remoteexec/detach.go`)
checked the last line of the start's answer against `jobDir`, the shape of any job directory. Since 902 the client
chooses the job's name (`newJobName`) and the script names the directory `job.<name>`, but the answer was never held
to that name. An answer naming another job's directory would have been polled, its files read, and the directory
removed with `rm -rf` when that job finished. Not seen on a device. `TestAnsweredJobDir`
(`pkg/remoteexec/detach_script_test.go`) shows it and fails with `main`'s check.

**Root cause.** The class of 313: trusting the far side's answer for a name the near side already knows.

**Why 902's fix did not hold.** 902 moved the choice of name to the client, so that a lost answer could still be
stopped by name (`jobByName`). It kept reading the directory from the answer and checked only its shape.

**Fix.** `1bb5288e`: `answeredJobDir` (`pkg/remoteexec/detach_script.go`) requires a `jobDir` match and the suffix
`/job.<name>`. An answer that is not this job's is handled as no job directory at all: the job is stopped by its own
name and the run fails. `TestAnsweredJobDir` refuses another job's name, a longer name, a relative path, a trailing
newline and a `..` step.

**Lesson.** When this side chose a name, an answer that names it is checked against that name, not only its shape.
Act only on what this run created.

## 946. A poll whose exit status was not a number stopped the job and threw away the stop's result, and quoted strconv's error, which holds the whole status line up to the poll's 64 KiB bound (a repeat of 910 and of 627; LESSONS 244) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Branch `fix/remoteexec-detach-hardening`. The first half was carried on 2026-11-06 from the same
2026-11-04 stash as 944; the second was found by the same independent review that found 943 (Fable 5.1, Batch API) and is fixed in `649d5890`. When a job's `rc` file held something that is not a number,
`runDetached` called `stopDetached` and dropped its return, so the error said nothing about the job. And `pollRC`
returned `strconv.Atoi`'s error, which quotes the whole text, and a job's `rc` file can make that text as long as the
poll's answer bound (64 KiB, `detachAnswerLimit`). `pollRC`'s other refusal ("no exit status line") already quoted
`boundedText`.

**Root cause.** LESSONS 244, a guard on one of two sibling paths. The start's error path reported the stop (910), and
`pollRC`'s other branch bounded its text; this exit and this branch had neither.

**Why 910 and 627 did not hold.** 910 made a failed start's error carry the stop's outcome, at that one exit; the poll
loop's exit for a status that is not a number kept the old shape. 627 says each new error that quotes a device's text
needs its own bound and nothing finds one that lacks it. A standard-library error that quotes its input does not look
like a quote of device text, so nobody bounded it.

**Fix.** `1bb5288e`: the error now ends "not a number, and the job <the stop's outcome>", such as "and the job was
stopped". `TestDetached_AnExitStatusThatIsNotANumberSaysWhatTheStopDid` (`pkg/remoteexec/detach_test.go`, against the
real in-process SSH server, with HOME a fresh directory) also asserts that no job directory is left. `649d5890`:
`pollRC`'s refusal quotes `boundedText(text)`. `TestPollRC_BoundsWhatItQuotes` holds a 60 KiB status line's error under
4 KiB. Both tests fail on `main`'s code.

**Lesson.** Every exit that runs a stop says what the stop found. An error built from a library's error over a
device's text is bounded like any other quote of that text: `strconv` quotes its input.

## 947. facts.gather reported ansible_distribution and its version from os-release NAME and VERSION_ID, which are not Ansible's values, and emitted no ansible_os_family, so a converted `when: ansible_distribution == "Debian"` was false on every Debian host (a repeat in kind of 848 and 334) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Found by the facts sweep of 2026-11-04, by reading; fixed on 2026-11-06 on `fix/facts-churn`. The defect
was on `main`, and the Linux part shipped in 0.3.0. `facts.gather` gave `ansible_distribution` from `NAME` and
`ansible_distribution_version` from `VERSION_ID` in `/etc/os-release`, and no `ansible_os_family` at all. Measured on
2026-11-06 with ansible-core 2.17.1 (`ansible.builtin.setup` through the `community.docker` connection) in 22 container
images: Debian 12.12, 13 and testing, Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04, Rocky 9.6 (full and minimal), AlmaLinux 9.6, RHEL UBI
9.6, CentOS Stream 9, Oracle Linux 9, Fedora 42, Amazon Linux 2 and 2023, Alpine 3.20.10 and 3.22.8, Arch, openSUSE
Leap 15.6 and Tumbleweed, SLES 15 SP6, Kali and Devuan. Examples of the gap:

- Debian: "Debian GNU/Linux" and "12", where Ansible says "Debian" and "12.12" (the point release, from
  `/etc/debian_version`, which is distro's best version).
- "Rocky Linux" where Ansible says "Rocky"; "Red Hat Enterprise Linux" where it says "RedHat"; "Alpine Linux" where it
  says "Alpine".
- No release where Ansible gives one: Blue Onyx or Plow (the parenthetical in `VERSION`), Stream, the SUSE minor.

So a playbook converted with `when: ansible_distribution == "Debian"` skipped on every Debian host, and a condition
on `ansible_os_family` had no fact to read.

**Root cause.** The facts carried Ansible's names, but their values were never measured against Ansible. The class of
334 and 848: another program's interface written from its names, not from what that program does with them.

**Why 848 and 334 did not hold.** 334's test checks the converter's argument names and values against `ansible-doc`.
848's fix made the converter map `gather_subset` by its meaning. Both cover what the converter passes in; neither
compares a value `facts.gather` emits with the value Ansible emits for the same host.

**Fix.** `3660d3e5` and `a9c1a6a2`: `internal/catalog/facts/gather_distribution.go` (new) maps the os-release `ID`
through a table of Ansible's names, reads the first line of Debian's `debian_version`, takes the codename by distro's
rule, and handles CentOS Stream and the SUSE release. `ansible_os_family` comes from Ansible's `OS_FAMILY_MAP`, and only
where that map knows the name; it is never guessed for a `NAME` the map does not list. The `min` probe is now
`cat /etc/os-release; echo MARK; cat /etc/debian_version 2>/dev/null`. Tests:
`TestGatherOSRelease_MatchesAnsibleOnEveryMeasuredDistribution` (each image's files in
`internal/catalog/facts/testdata/distribution`, with Ansible's recorded values in `ansible.json`),
`TestGatherOSRelease_ReadsWhatTheFileSays`, and the live `TestGatherDistribution_MatchesAnsibleOnRealDistributions`
(`internal/catalog/facts/live/distribution_test.go`, 4 containers).

**Found on review.** The branch's fp-reviewer agent, before push: the first version guessed a family for a derivative
the map does not list (Raspbian, Kali and Devuan would have read the family "Kali GNU/Linux" and the like). Fixed in
`a9c1a6a2`: a family only where Ansible's map lists the name, and Kali and Devuan, measured against
`ansible.builtin.setup`, are in the `ID` table. An independent second-model review found that Debian's
`debian_version` must be read to its first line, as distro reads it; fixed in the same commit.

**Lesson.** A fact named after Ansible's is held to Ansible's recorded value for the same image or machine (LESSONS 404).

## 948. On macOS every gather added one launchd job and removed the last one's, because launchd lists a job per SSH connection and per session (com.openssh.sshd.<UUID>), and a gather is itself a login (a repeat in kind of 935 and 870) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Fixed on 2026-11-06 on `fix/facts-churn`; the defect was on `main`. `launchctl print system` lists a job
for each SSH connection and each session: `com.openssh.sshd.<UUID>`, and on the lab Mac also
`com.apple.loginwindow.<UUID>`, `com.apple.security.agent.login.<id>`, `com.apple.security.authhost.<id>`,
`com.apple.diskimagesiod.<UUID>` and `com.apple.metadata.mds.index.<UUID>`. Each gather logs in, so each one recorded a
new service and the last gather's as removed. Reproduced: three gathers 20 seconds apart on the lab Mac each swapped
one `com.openssh.sshd.<UUID>` for another.

**Root cause.** The services list took every label launchd prints, and some of those labels name one login, not a
configured service.

**Why 935 and 870 did not hold.** 935 fixed disabled daemons and the exit-status field, not instance labels. 870 and
927 were drift fixed inside their own probes. The Mac lab gate gathered once and compared counts at one moment, so a
label that changes with each login could not show.

**Fix.** `3660d3e5` and `a9c1a6a2` (`internal/catalog/facts/gather_bsd_items.go`): `parseLaunchd` skips a label whose
last dot part is a UUID unless a plist of that name is installed (`launchdInstance`), in the loaded list and in the
disabled-daemon loop. Tests: `TestParseLaunchd_LeavesOutEachLoginsInstanceJobs`, and the lab gate
`TestCLI_FactsGatherOnMacOSKeepsItsServicesAcrossLogins` (`cmd/pleiades/facts_churn_lab_release_gate_test.go`), which
passes with the fix and fails on `main`'s code.

**Lesson.** A source that makes an item per login changes on every gather; gather twice on an unchanged machine
(LESSONS 405).

## 949. On Windows a per-user service gets an instance per signed-in user (Template_<LUID>), so its instance keys changed across two boots of an unchanged machine, and the template Windows never lists was missing (a repeat in kind of 935, 870 and 874) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Fixed on 2026-11-06 on `fix/facts-churn`; the defect was on `main`. Windows makes an instance of each
per-user service for each signed-in user, named `<template>_<LUID>` (for example `WpnUserService_3d08a`).
`Win32_Service` lists the instances and never the template. Across two boots of an unchanged win-check, with a
throwaway user signed in by autologon, the four instance keys changed from `_3d08a` to `_2151b`. Measured on
win-check: CIM gives an instance's `ServiceType` as "Unknown"; the registry `Type` is `0x60` for a template and `0xe0`
for an instance (`0x80` is `SERVICE_USERSERVICE_INSTANCE`); a WinRM network logon and an S4U scheduled-task logon make
no instance, only an interactive sign-in does.

**Root cause.** The list came from what the service manager reports, which names one user's sign-in, not from the
configured services in the registry.

**Why 935, 870 and 874 did not hold.** Each fixed drift inside its own probe. None gathered across a sign-in or a
reboot, and a gather over WinRM makes no instance, so a test gathering twice over WinRM alone sees no change.

**Fix.** `3660d3e5` and `a9c1a6a2` (`internal/catalog/facts/gather_win.go`): the services script reads every service's
registry `Type` and skips `0x80`. Where a key cannot be read, it skips a name made of a known template and a hex LUID.
It lists each template from the registry with `per_user` true and no state. Tests:
`TestParseWindowsServices_ATemplateHasNoState`, and the lab gate
`TestCLI_FactsGatherOnWindowsReportsPerUserServicesByTemplate` (opt-in with `PLEIADES_WINRM_SIGN_IN=1`: it signs a
throwaway user in through autologon, with a password made in the guest, and compares the services gathered before and
after the sign-in). The gate passes with the fix and fails on `main`'s code.

**Found on review.** The branch's fp-reviewer agent, before push: a `Type`, `Start` or `DelayedAutostart` value that
is not a DWORD failed the whole task. Fixed in `a9c1a6a2`: such a value is read as unknown.

**Lesson.** A sign-in makes items a network logon never does; gather across a sign-in or a reboot (LESSONS 405).

## 950. A service's running state was part of its stable service.<name> fact, and it moves on its own, so an unchanged Mac or Windows host recorded changes between gathers (a repeat in kind of 927 and 870) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Fixed on 2026-11-06 on `fix/facts-churn`; the defect was on `main`. The state (running or stopped) was a
field of `service.<name>`, a stable fact, so every change was kept. On the lab Mac, `com.apple.ManagedClient` and
`com.apple.mdmclient.daemon` each flipped between running and stopped within 3 minutes. On win-check, `KeyIso`,
`TrustedInstaller`, `WaaSMedicSvc` and `wlidsvc` started on their own within 30 seconds. Nobody changed either host.

**Root cause.** A runtime value was stored as configuration. On-demand services start and stop without anyone changing
the machine.

**Why 927 and 870 did not hold.** 927 took the uptime out of an OpenRC status but kept the state inside the stable
fact. Its entry named the rest of the question, sweep item 10 (service runtime state and other fields that move on
their own), as still open. This is that item.

**Fix.** `3660d3e5`: `splitServiceState` and `familyItems` (`internal/catalog/facts/gather_subsets.go`) move the state
to a volatile `service_state.<name>` (a string), after `gatherNames.distinct` so the two keys pair, in `Gather` and in
`Probe.Read`; the planner learns the second family (`familiesOf`). `service.<name>` keeps `enabled`, `status` and
`source`. Checked on win-check with `pleiades facts win-check --json`: the store keeps `service_state.WinRM` as volatile
and `service.WinRM` as stable without a state. Tests: `gatherHoldsServiceStatesApart` in
`TestGather_PackagesAndServicesMatchThisMachine`, `TestGatherFacts_AServicesStateIsVolatileAndTheRestStable`,
`TestFamilyItems_SplitsAServicesStateUnderItsOwnKey`, and the lab gate
`TestCLI_FactsGatherOnWindowsKeepsItsServicesAcrossGathers`.

**Lesson.** A field that can change with nobody changing the machine is its own volatile fact, not part of a stable
one (LESSONS 405).

## 951. Hardware facts held values Ansible does not report: a swap total on macOS, the page file size on Windows where Ansible reports 0, and Windows memory rounded down where Ansible rounds up (the class of 947) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Fixed on 2026-11-06 on `fix/facts-churn`; the defect was on `main`.

- macOS: `ansible_swaptotal_mb` came from `vm.swapusage`. Ansible does not emit it on Darwin (`hardware/darwin.py` has
  `memtotal_mb` and `memfree_mb` only), and macOS changes it as it makes and removes swap files. That movement is
  reasoned, not seen: the fact did not move on the lab Mac in 3 days. Ansible's absence was measured from its source.
- Windows: `ansible_swaptotal_mb` came from `Win32_PageFileUsage` `AllocatedBaseSize` (4864 on win-check), where
  ansible.windows' `setup.ps1` sets it to 0.
- Windows: memory was rounded down (4095), where `setup.ps1` uses `[Math]::Ceiling` (4096 on win-check).
  `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` and CIM gave the same byte count.

**Root cause.** 947's: the facts carried Ansible's names, and their values were not held to Ansible's.

**Why 947 did not hold.** 947 is on the same branch and covered the distribution facts; these are the hardware ones.

**Fix.** `3660d3e5` and `a9c1a6a2`: no swap probe on Darwin, 0 on Windows, and Windows memory rounded up. Tests:
`TestBSDHostProbes_AMacReportsNoSwap`, `TestWindowsProbes_ReportAnsiblesSwapAndFamily`, and the Windows and Mac lab
gates (`TestCLI_FactsGatherOnWindowsMatchesItsOwnTools`, `TestCLI_FactsGatherOnMacOSMatchesItsOwnTools`).

**Lesson.** As 947 (LESSONS 404).

## 952. The Mac lab gate compared the launchd fact count with the services block's line count, which 935's fix had made unequal wherever an installed daemon is disabled, and the gate runs only where a Mac is configured, so nothing noticed (a repeat in kind of 790) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Found on 2026-11-06 on `fix/facts-churn` when the Mac lab gate ran; the test defect was on `main`.
`TestCLI_FactsGatherOnMacOSMatchesItsOwnTools` (`cmd/pleiades/facts_lab_release_gate_test.go`) wanted as many launchd
facts as lines in `launchctl print system`'s services block. Since 935's fix a disabled daemon with an installed plist
is a fact too, and launchd never lists it, so the counts differ whenever one exists
(`com.apple.mdmclient.daemon.runatboot` on the lab Mac).

**Root cause.** 790's class: a change to a behavior an older test reads, where that test does not run in the passes
the change was checked with. Here the test runs only where `PLEIADES_MAC` is set.

**Why 790 did not hold.** 790's rule is to run the whole package an older test lives in before the push. A lab gate
skips in that run unless its machine is configured, so the package passed with the gate unchecked.

**Fix.** `3660d3e5`: every label launchd lists, except a per-login instance (948), must be a fact, and any fact
launchd does not list must be a disabled daemon.

**Lesson.** A change to what a family reports runs the lab gates that read that family on their machines, not only
the package in a pass where those gates skip.

## 953. win-check hung at a black screen on the boot after a guest restart, so win.reboot timed out after 600 s, and the sign-in test's cleanup could not reach the guest (possibly in kind of 362; open: cause not proven)

**Symptom.** 2026-11-06, during the Windows sign-in lab gate on `fix/facts-churn`. After a guest restart, win-check
showed a black screen. `win.reboot` timed out after 600 seconds, and an ACPI shutdown went unanswered for 2 minutes.
The guest's log shows a clean shutdown (event 1074, then 6006) and nothing from the hung boot (no 41, no 6008), so the
boot stopped before Windows started. Five other restarts of the same VM that day worked.

**Cost.** The sign-in test's cleanup could not reach the guest. After a power cycle, autologon signed the throwaway
user in again from the `DefaultPassword` value. It was cleaned by hand and checked.

**Root cause.** Not proven. It fits the boot hangs seen under NEM (WHPX) on this host, such as 362's EFI hang, but
nothing ties it to them.

**Fix.** None yet. The knowledge is written to Groundconfig as
`knowledge/unreviewed/virtualbox_whpx_guest_restart_boot_hang.txt`, awaiting the owner's review.

**Lesson.** A lab test that changes a guest's sign-in settings must expect its cleanup to fail when a restart hangs;
after a power cycle, check the guest for what the test left before anything else runs.

## 954. facts.gather listed systemd units that last only as long as a login, a connection or a process, so service.<name> keys came and went on an unchanged host, and a socket-activated sshd's per-connection key held the peer's address and port (a repeat in kind of 948 and 949) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Found and fixed on 2026-11-06 on `fix/open-patterns-batch2`; the defect was on `main`. Measured on a
booted `pleiades-probe/rocky-systemd:1` container (systemd 252, dbus-broker 28, sshd started from an `Accept=yes`
socket). Each gather is an SSH login, and each one added a new key, `service.sshd@<n>-172.17.0.4:22-172.17.0.1:<port>.service`,
so the key also stored the client's address and port. `user@1000.service` and `user-runtime-dir@1000.service`
appeared while a user lingered and left 12 seconds after the lingering ended. A D-Bus activation added the transient
`dbus-:1.1-org.pleiades.Probe@0.service`. None of these is a configured service.

**Root cause.** The systemd probe took every unit `systemctl` lists, and some units exist only for one connection, one
login session or one process.

**Why 948 and 949 did not hold.** Each fixed its own system's per-login source: launchd's per-connection labels (948)
and Windows' per-user service instances (949). LESSONS 405 named systemd's `sshd@` and `user@` units as the open Linux
case. A gather of an sshd run as an ordinary service makes no per-connection unit, so a Linux test needs a
socket-activated sshd to see this.

**Fix.** `62033dae` and `b4338348` (`internal/catalog/facts/gather_services.go`): `sessionUnit` leaves out transient
units, `user@` and `user-runtime-dir@` instances (a lingering user's too, on purpose, though it lasts as long as the
host), and `<socket>@<n>-...` instances of a loaded `<socket>.socket`. To tell those apart, the probe prints a third
listing, the loaded sockets. `getty@tty1`, `modprobe@*` and `sshd-keygen@*` stay. On systemd before 230,
`list-unit-files` does not mark a transient unit (systemd NEWS, CHANGES WITH 230), so one is still listed there; the
module's documentation says so. Tests: `TestCLI_ServiceFactsHoldStillWhileLoginsComeAndGo`
(`cmd/pleiades/services_facts_release_gate_test.go`, through the real binary: two gathers, with a socket-activated
sshd, a lingering user and a transient unit coming and going between them) and
`TestParseSystemd_LeavesOutUnitsThatLastOnlyAsLongAsALogin`. A probe answer cut off before the new third listing is
958's.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 405, whose open Linux case this closes. A fact's key built from a device's own names is device
data: a per-connection name can carry a peer's address into the store.

## 955. The 560 fix's settle read, when it failed after a successful start, stop or restart, failed the task, so the engine journaled a failure during the action with no undo, and with 551's fix a known, undoable change became an unknown_effect (a repeat of 563, 452 and 638) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found on 2026-11-06 on `fix/open-patterns-batch2` by the fp-reviewer agent and a second model's review
(rv2), before any push. 560's fix (`5d468d73`) made `container.start`, `container.stop` and `container.restart` read
the container once after the change (`settle`). When that read failed after the change had succeeded, the method
returned the error.

**Root cause.** 452's class. A failed task's undo is dropped before the journal unless the method marks it
`sdk.Inverse.KeepOnFailure` and its manifest allows that with `MayKeepOnFailure` (`keepsUndo`,
`internal/engine/collection_action.go`, used by `internal/engine/executor.go`); the container methods set neither.
So the journal held a failure during the action and no undo for a change that did happen. With 551's fix (on the same
branch), that failure also turned a known, undoable change into an `unknown_effect` refusal for any rollback beneath
the run.

**Why 563, 452 and 638 did not hold.** 563 fixed its four methods, and 638 already said nothing makes a method that
reads after its change keep its undo. 563's lesson is that an undo is proven where a rollback reads it, the journal.
`5d468d73`'s test called the method directly, below the step that drops the undo, so it could not see this.

**Fix.** `501f7196` (`internal/catalog/container/lifecycle.go`): a failed settle read is a warning
(`sdk.RecordWarnings`), and the method returns success with its undo. The read runs on `context.WithoutCancel`, even after
the task's own context has ended, with its own 10 second bound (`settleTimeout`) so it cannot hold a stopped run. Test:
`TestStop_AFailedReadAfterTheStopKeepsTheUndoInTheJournal` (`internal/catalog/container/settle_engine_test.go`), through
the real executor and dispatcher, with a socket proxy that refuses every inspect after the stop.

**Lesson.** 563's, again: a method that reads after its change is tested through the engine to the journal, never by
calling the method.

## 956. container.stop of an auto-remove container recorded container.start as its undo, which no rollback could ever run, since the engine removes the container when it stops (a repeat in kind of 666 and 156) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Found on 2026-11-06 on `fix/open-patterns-batch2` while checking 955; the defect was on `main`. A
container created with auto-remove (`docker run --rm`) is deleted by the engine when it stops. `container.stop`
still recorded `container.start` of it as the undo, so a rollback would fail on a container that no longer exists.

**Root cause.** 666's and 156's: the undo was chosen by the method (a stop undoes to a start), not by what the stop
leaves behind.

**Why 666 and 156 did not hold.** Each was fixed in its own method. 666's lesson asks for an undo written for every
state a target can start in; auto-remove is a setting of the container, not a state, and no check reads it.

**Fix.** `501f7196` (`internal/catalog/container/stop.go`, `lifecycle.go`): a stop of an auto-remove container records
no undo and a warning saying why. Test: `TestStop_AnAutoRemoveContainerIsSettledAndHasNoUndo`.

**Lesson.** Before recording an undo, ask whether the change leaves anything the undo can act on.

## 957. 551's fix kept the "cancels out" skip ahead of its new rule, so a later run that had been rolled back was skipped although a task of it had failed during its action on the device, and its advice to roll that run back first could never clear it (a case 551's fix left; the class of 652) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found on 2026-11-06 on `fix/open-patterns-batch2` in review, before any push. 551's fix (`4f8a30fe`)
made a later run's task that failed during its action refuse a rollback beneath it. But the planner skipped a later
run whose changes its own rollback had undone ("cancels out", from 652's work) before it applied that rule. Such a
run could be rolled back with `--allow-unknown` accepting its failed task, and was then skipped, though the failed
task's partial effect was still on the device. Its advice ("roll it back first") also could not clear it, since no
rollback undoes a failed task.

**Root cause.** The new rule was added to one path of `laterRunProblems` (`internal/rollback/history.go`), and the
skip ran first.

**Fix.** `b39700eb` (`internal/rollback/history.go`, `later_run.go`): a rolled-back later run is skipped only when none
of its tasks failed during their action on the shared devices; otherwise it is reported as `unknown_effect`. The
advice names `--allow-unknown` for the rollback of that run, then `--despite-run` to step over it. A device that saw
only a failed action is named as "may have changed". Tests:
`TestBuild_ARolledBackLaterRunStillRefusesForWhatFailedDuringItsAction`,
`TestBuild_ALaterRunsAdviceSaysWhatClearsAFailedTask`.

**Still open (owner design call).** A later rollback run skipped as "cancels out" when it ran after the target.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 407: a rule for the run being undone applies to every later run, in every path that can skip one.

## 958. Three small defects from review: the Controller's rollback refusal had no kind or unknown_effects though the production guide says a refusal gives them (a repeat in kind of 571 and 789), the tftpxfer bind test passed with the fix reverted (the class of 54), and checkSystemd still asked for two listings after the probe grew a third (the class of 571) (fixed before push)

**Symptom and fix.** Found on 2026-11-06 on `fix/open-patterns-batch2` in review, before any push.

- **The Controller's refusal.** `RollbackProblem` (`internal/api/dispatcher_rollback.go`) kept each problem's node,
  device, reason and accepting field, and dropped the planner's `kind` and `unknown_effects`, which the CLI's `--json`
  carries and docs/10 describes as part of a refusal. `kind` was missing on `main` too, since the planner gained it in
  652's fix; `unknown_effects` is this branch's. Fixed in `b4a32d91`: each problem carries both, omitted when empty,
  and the OpenAPI document (`internal/apispec/template_endpoints.go`) describes them. Test:
  `TestRollbackJob_NamesALaterJobsKindAndWhatFailedThere`. 571's and 789's class: text promising more than the code
  gives.
- **A false green in 448's test.** `TestAnIPv4ClientSocketLeavesItsPortFreeOnIPv6` gave the client 300 ms and one
  retry, so a delayed goroutine let the client close its socket before the test's `[::1]` bind, and the test passed
  with the fix reverted. Fixed in `07929043`: the client waits 30 seconds, and the server ends the transfer with a TFTP
  error only after the bind, which must reach the client (a client that had closed its socket would never see it).
  The class of 54: a test that cannot fail on the defect proves nothing.
- **checkSystemd.** 954's probe prints three listings, but `checkSystemd` still asked for two sections, so an answer
  cut off before the socket listing was parsed with no sockets and kept every per-connection unit the gather leaves
  out. Fixed in `b4338348`: `checkSystemd` and `parseSystemd` require exactly three, and the comments that said two
  say three.

**Lesson.** When a change adds a field or a section, every reader and every checker of the old shape is part of the
change: the API's copy of the planner's problem, and the probe's own answer check.


## 959. The strict journal reader kept its own copies of the engine's stages, skip kinds and node id grammar, so it refused a handler's entries and a parallel group's fan-out and join entries, and one such run made `journal list` and `rollback` refuse every journal (a repeat in kind of 768; the parallel case shipped in v0.3.0) (fixed)

**Symptom.** Found on 2026-11-06 on `feat/contracts-135`, before any push, in two steps.

- **Handlers.** `TestCLI_HandlersRunOnceInTheirOrderOnlyWhenNotified` (`cmd/pleiades/handlers_release_gate_test.go`),
  extended to run `pleiades journal list --json` through the real binary, failed: "the journal of run <id>, line 4:
  names node \"tasks.handlers[0]\", which is not a graph id". The reader also had no place for the handlers' skip kind
  `not_notified`. A handler's copy is journaled as `tasks.handlers[N]` or `pretasks.handlers[N]`. Found while writing
  golden tests.
- **Parallel groups.** Review of the first fix (fp-reviewer, finding F2) found a second shape the reader refused: a
  parallel group's synthetic fan-out and join nodes (`tasks[N].fanout`, `tasks[N].block[M].join`), which the engine
  journals with outcome `not_reached`. `TestEveryNodeIDTheBuilderMakesReadsBack` (`internal/journal/node_ids_test.go`)
  showed it: a DAG built by `engine.NewBuilder(eval).BuildFromYAML`, recorded by `FileStore` and read by `ReadRun` failed
  with "names node \"tasks[0].block[1].fanout\"".

One such run broke more than itself. `journal.ListRuns` returns on the first journal that fails to read, so `pleiades
journal list` and `pleiades rollback` (which reads every later run) refused every journal in the project's directory.
`journal show` reads one run through `ReadRun`, so it refused the bad run only.

**Who met it.** Handlers (Phase 90) came after v0.3.0 and are not in a release, so no user met that half; `main` has it.
Parallel groups did ship: in v0.3.0 the builder makes `<group>.fanout` and `<group>.join` nodes, the engine journals
them as `not_reached` (`journalEntry`, `internal/engine/journal_entry.go`), and the reader's `nodeIDPattern` has no
`.fanout` or `.join`. That was read in the tag's source, not reproduced with a v0.3.0 binary.

**Root cause.** `internal/journal/reader.go` kept its own copies of what the engine writes: the failure stages
(`knownStage`), the skip kinds (`knownSkip`) and the builder's id grammar (`nodeIDPattern`). Handlers and the parallel
nodes added shapes the copies never learned, and no test built every shape the builder makes and read it back.

**Fix.** `343edef1` (handlers) and `bf331d04` (parallel nodes and the builder test). The reader holds stages and skip
kinds to `engine.IsRecordedFailureStage` and `engine.IsRecordedSkipKind`, whose lists the engine documents as only
growing, so the reader's maps are gone. `nodeIDPattern` takes `.handlers[N]` after a section and `.fanout` or `.join`
after a group. `TestEveryNodeIDTheBuilderMakesReadsBack` holds the pattern to the builder's own output, and
`TestJournalFormatOneReadsEveryKind` (`internal/journal/golden_test.go`, from `44068d03`, extended in `bf331d04`) reads
a frozen format-1 journal (`internal/journal/testdata/format-1/every-kind.jsonl`) holding every stage, skip kind,
outcome and node shape, so removing one from the reader fails.

**Still open.** One copy remains: `knownOutcome` in `reader.go`, five values with no validator exported by the engine.
The frozen journal holds each of them, so a removal fails, but a new outcome the engine starts to write would still be
refused until the reader learns it.

**Why 768's fix did not hold.** 768 found a hand-kept list of engine names in `internal/validate` and made it read the
engine's own table. Its review looked at that one list and did not look for other copies of the engine's closed sets
in other readers; the journal reader's copies predated it.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 408: a reader of a format holds it to the writer's own source, never to a copy beside the reader,
and the format's tests read a frozen file of every kind the writer has written.

## 960. A depth-1 CI checkout with `fetch-tags: true` holds no release tag, so `schema-compat` in `ci-remote` would have failed the `ci` job's Linux row on every pull request (a repeat of 418; the class of 416) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found on 2026-11-06 on `feat/contracts-135` by fp-reviewer, before any pull-request run. `e1c5505a` added
`make schema-compat` (`tools/schemacompat`) to `ci-remote`. It reads the newest release's schemas with `git tag --list`
and `git show v0.3.0:<path>`, and with no tag it stops with "no release tag at or below ...". To give it the tags, the
same commit set `fetch-tags: true` on the `ci` job's `actions/checkout`, which fetches one commit. fp-reviewer and a
depth-1 clone made here both measured that such a fetch holds no `v0.3.0`: `fetch-tags` only drops the `--no-tags`
flag, and a shallow fetch brings only tags that point at the fetched commit. `ci-remote` runs only on the Linux row
(`ci (ubuntu-24.04, true)`, a required check), so that row would have failed on every pull request.

**Root cause.** The step assumed that asking for tags brings every tag. A checkout shaped like CI's was not tried before
the step was written, and the workflow lint checks a step's shape, not what git fetches.

**Fix.** `bf331d04` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `fetch-tags` is gone, and a step before `ci-remote`, Linux only, runs
`git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin '+refs/tags/v*:refs/tags/v*'`, which brings each release tag one commit deep. The
step's comment says why `fetch-tags` is not enough.

**Why 418's fix did not hold.** 418 found that a CI checkout has one commit and no `main`, and fixed it for the jobs that
needed `main` (the containers and nightly jobs fetch full history). Its fix was per job and per ref: the `ci` job kept
its one-commit checkout, and tags are a different ref from `main`. 418's lesson ("anything that names a ref by its local
name has to be proved in a checkout shaped like CI's") covers this case. It was not applied when the new gate was
added, and nothing checks for it. 416's lesson, that a step only CI runs is unverified until it has run somewhere, is the
same miss.

**Not yet proven on a runner.** The new step has not run in GitHub Actions yet. The first pull-request run of the
branch is its proof: the `ci (ubuntu-24.04, true)` row passing `schema-compat`.

**Lesson.** 418's lesson, unchanged; no new lesson. A gate that reads git history needs a test in a depth-1 clone of the
kind `actions/checkout` makes before it is wired into a CI job.

Verified after the fix (2026-11-06): in a `git clone --depth=1 --no-tags` of the branch, that refspec fetch brought `v0.3.0` and `git show v0.3.0:docs/reference/schemas/run-report.json` read it.

## 961. A Runner terminated a newer dispatch it could not decode with no reported result, since the `payload_version` check ran only after a full decode, so the job would read dispatched until the Reaper republished it into the same refusal (the class of 208; its test a repeat in kind of 380) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found on 2026-11-06 on `feat/contracts-135` by fp-reviewer (findings F3 and F4), before any push; never
released. `0332b8cd` gave the dispatch payload a `payload_version` and made a Runner refuse a newer one by name. The
check ran only on a payload that decoded. A newer Controller that retypes a field (say `capabilities` from a list to an
object) sends a payload this Runner cannot decode, and the decode-failure path terminated the message with no result.
Its job would then read dispatched until the Reaper republished it, and a Runner of the same build would drop it the
same way. This was read from the code; the second half of the finding is why the test did not show it.

**The test could not fail on it.** `TestAgent_HandleMessage_ANewerPayloadIsRefusedNeverRun`
(`internal/runner/agent_payload_version_test.go`) built its Agent with no result bus, so it checked that the message was
terminated and the adapter never ran, and could not see a missing report. The real Runner always passes
`runner.WithResultReporting`. That is 380's shape: a harness Agent composed with less than the binary's options.

**Root cause.** The decode-failure path treated every payload that would not decode as malformed. Whether redelivery can
help was decided right (it cannot, so the message is terminated), but whether the failure is the Runner's to report
was not asked: a payload from a newer Controller is a job someone is waiting on. 208's class, a failure split on the
wrong axis.

**Fix.** `bf331d04`. On a decode failure, `newerUndecodable` (`internal/runner/agent_version.go`) reads only the
version and the job's identity (job, device, device name, runbook). When the version is past this build's, the job is
reported failed with a reason naming the version, then the message is terminated; any other decode failure is malformed
as before. The test now passes `runner.WithResultReporting(bus)`, subscribes to the job's results, and fails with "no
failed result was published" when none arrives. Its subtest
`TestAgent_HandleMessage_ANewerPayloadIsRefusedNeverRun/version_2_with_a_field_retyped` is red without the fix.

**Still open.** `TestAgent_HandleMessage_AnUnroutableKindIsReportedThenTerminated` (`internal/runner/agent_test.go`) has
the same gap: its name says the dispatch is reported, and it builds its Agent with no result bus, so it cannot fail on a
missing report.

**Why 380's fix did not hold.** 380 fixed `cmd/runner`'s release-gate harness to report results as the real Runner does.
The unit tests in `internal/runner` construct their own Agents and were not swept.

**Lesson.** No new lesson. LESSONS 351: a harness wiring a production object copies every option the composition root
passes. And 208's: split a consumer's failures on what each one means, not on which layer said no; here, a message
terminated for a job someone is waiting on is reported first.

## 962. The rollback planner ordered one node's changes on two devices by Go's map order, so one journal planned two different rollbacks (fixed)

**Symptom.** `make pr-check`'s repeat pass (2026-11-06, the contracts branch) failed
`TestRollbackPlanMatchesTheGolden` once and passed it once: the plan named `tasks[0]` on `h2` before `h1` where the
golden had `h1` first. `TestBuild_TheSameJournalPlansTheSameRollback` (`internal/rollback/determinism_test.go`) shows it
directly: on `main`'s planner fifty calls of `rollback.Build` on one request do not all agree (the refusal's problems
flipped at call 22 in its first run), with the plan's levels and the refusal's problem list both affected.

**Root cause.** `changesOf` (`internal/rollback/steps.go`) gathers a run's changes into a map keyed by node and device,
then sorts them by attempt and sequence alone. On the Walk tier each device's Runner numbers its own entries, so one
node's entries on two devices share a sequence; with nothing else deciding, the map's order did. Every later step (each
entry's level, the problem list) follows that order, so the same journal produced a different plan from one call to the
next. The golden test, written that evening, was the first test to compare a whole multi-device plan byte for byte.

**Fix.** The sort breaks ties by node and then device, and the unknown-effect list by device, so the order is total.
`TestBuild_TheSameJournalPlansTheSameRollback` is red on the old planner and green on the fix (thirty runs with
`-race`).

**Still open (an owner design call).** Each change is its own level (`levelKey{order, index}` with `order` the change's
own position), so one node's undo on several devices runs one device after another, though `Plan.Levels`' doc says a
level's devices run side by side. Grouping by node changes the plan's shape and the order steps run in, so it is left
for the owner, with the golden pinning today's shape.

**Lesson.** The new contract (docs/13: "the same journal producing a different plan" breaks rollback planning) made the
property testable; a golden test of a whole plan is what found it. Any order built from a map is total by construction:
the sort that follows names every field down to a unique one.

## 963. `pleiades collection list --describe` ran a program before checking its bytes were the approved build (fixed before merge)

**Symptom.** Found in review of the protocol window branch (fp-reviewer F2, Fable's independent review item 3), never
released. `describeProtocol` (`cmd/pleiades/collection.go`) called `loader.Inspect`, which runs the program's
`describe`, and compared the file's digest with the approval only afterwards; the first version of
`TestCLI_CollectionListNamesEachBuildsProtocol` even approved a program under a digest it did not have and listed it.

**Root cause.** `Inspect` exists for `approve`, where running an unapproved program is the operator's explicit act on
it. Reused for a list, it put the approval check after the work it gates: a check-after-use (CWE-696). Bytes swapped
into the collections directory after approval ran, confined by Landlock and given no secret, whenever someone listed
approvals; each old approval of the same program ran it again.

**Fix.** `edf183b3`. `loader.ProgramDigest` hashes the file with the same directory and file checks and runs nothing;
`describeProtocol` names a mismatch "not this build" without running the program. The test's `replaced` program fails
its `describe`, so running it would print "unknown"; the test requires "not this build" and no "unknown". Submitted to
vuln-corpus as a C10 lead.

**Lesson.** A function that runs code under an explicit approval step is not a read; a caller that only lists or
inspects runs the integrity check first and the code only when it passes.

## 964. The loader agreed a protocol version with a program and never told the program (fixed before merge)

**Symptom.** Found in review of the protocol window branch (Fable item 1, fp-reviewer F1), never released. The loader
picked the highest version both sides speak and kept it on `Program.Protocol`, which nothing read, and the invoke
request carried no version. A program speaking 1 and 2 agreed at 1 by a 0.4.0 loader would have answered in 2.

**Root cause.** The negotiation was built where the ranges are known (describe) and stopped there; the invoke side,
where the agreed version has to be used, was never part of the change. 116's shape: a value resolved and never read.

**Fix.** `edf183b3`. `wire.ChildRequest.Protocol` carries the agreed version on every call (absent means a loader
from before the field, which spoke only the program's newest), the SDK refuses one it does not speak
(`checkRequestProtocol`), and `TestProxy_DeliversTheRequestAndReturnsTheResponse` reads the version from the request a
real child received.

**Lesson.** A negotiation is finished only when both sides act on its result: test the agreed value at the place it
is used, not where it is chosen (a repeat in kind of 116).

## 965. A new Controller fact rule was held by an older test's batch, which named no emitting method (fixed before merge)

**Symptom.** `make branch-containers` for the protocol window branch (run 42347669082, shard 5) failed
`TestFactDigestOptions_KeyWhatARunnerSealedThroughTheConsumerMainBuilds` (`cmd/controller/fact_digest_keys_test.go`):
"stored []", the subscriber having logged "dropping facts a built-in holds that a batch says a method outside the
catalog emitted ... method=\"\" facts=[file.x]". It failed again alone, so not contention. pr-check had passed:
`cmd/controller` is a container package it leaves to Actions (CI_LESSONS 1).

**Root cause.** The branch made the Controller's facts consumer (`newFactsSubscriber`) keep a built-in fact only from a
built-in method (`entstore.WithBuiltinProvenance`). The test written for that rule set `By.Method`; an older test of
the same consumer built its batch with no `By` at all, a shape no Runner sends: the engine stores only keys the
emitting method's registered manifest declares, so every stored fact carries a registered method.

**Fix.** The older test's batch names `facts.gather`, the built-in that declares `file.`; the whole `cmd/controller`
package passes with `-tags integration`. The only other subscribers built in tests (`internal/facts/entstore`) do not
take the new option.

**Lesson.** No new lesson; 837's: a rule added at the Controller's fact seam is checked against every test that feeds
that seam, found by the constructor (`newFactsSubscriber`), not only by the new test, and a fixture holds the shape a
real producer sends.

## 966. The live distribution test was rewritten to start all 22 images ansible.json records, four of them rolling, named only in JSON where tools/testimages cannot see them (a repeat of 125; in kind of 124, 917 and 745) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found in review of `feat/native-fact-names-41h` (fp-reviewer F1), before any push. Commit `23f08687`
rewrote `TestGatherDistribution_MapsToAnsibleOnRealDistributions` (`internal/catalog/facts/live/distribution_test.go`)
to start every image `internal/catalog/facts/testdata/distribution/ansible.json` records (22) and hold each to the
values Ansible printed there on 2026-11-06. Four of those images are rolling: `opensuse/tumbleweed`, `archlinux:base`,
`kalilinux/kali-rolling` and `debian:testing`. Several others name a major version only (`debian:13`, `oraclelinux:9`,
`amazonlinux:2`, `quay.io/centos/centos:stream9`). The same commit dropped the Go constants `debianImage` and
`ubuntuImage`, so the images the test started were named only in JSON. The first fresh pull of a rolling image in CI,
after its next snapshot, would have failed the test with nothing in the repository changed.

**Root cause.** A measurement taken on one day was turned into a CI assertion over images that move. And the images
left the place every image guard reads: `tools/testimages` keeps Go constants and fields whose names hold `Image`, so a
JSON-only image was missing from CI's image cache key and from pr-check's `testimages -served` step. The package's run
time grew with it: `tools/testgate/durations.json` records 20 seconds for `internal/catalog/facts/live`, and 22
container starts were never measured against that (745's class; not measured on this branch).

**Why 125 did not hold.** 125's fix wrote the pin rule as a predicate (`rejectPin`), but `TestPinsNameAnExactVersion`
applies it to a hand-listed map of `internal/testsupport`'s constants. An image named in another package's test, or in
a data file, is never checked. 124 is the same blind spot from another side: a value outside the files a guard reads.
917 is the same moving source under a pinned image (a package index there, an image tag here). 465 and 736 concern the
same list, `tools/testimages`', but the opposite error: they let in things that are not images, and here real images
were left out.

**Fix.** `85a4c89f`. CI runs the four pinned images (`debian:12.12`, `ubuntu:24.04`,
`rockylinux/rockylinux:9.6-minimal`, `alpine:3.20.10`), each named as a Go constant (`debianImage`, `ubuntuImage`,
`rockyImage`, `openrcImage`) so the scanner sees it, and each checked against the image `ansible.json` recorded for its
slug; the test fails if `ansible.json` lacks one. All 22 run only with `PLEIADES_LIVE_ALL_DISTRIBUTIONS=1`, a
measurement on a given day, which passed 22 of 22 on 2026-11-07.

**Lesson.** A test that CI runs starts only images pinned to a release and named where `tools/testimages` reads them;
a recorded measurement over rolling or major-only images runs when asked, never as a gate.

## 967. The playbook converter copied setup's filter to facts.gather's, so once fact keys became native every converted ansible_* filter matched nothing and failed on every host (a repeat of 848 and 334) (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found in review of `feat/native-fact-names-41h` (fp-reviewer F2), before any push. The converter's
`setup` entry (`internal/forge/playbook/modules_misc.go`) mapped `filter` straight to `facts.gather`'s `filter`.
Commit `23f08687` made `facts.gather`'s keys native (`os.*`, `host.*`, `hardware.*`), so a converted
`filter: ansible_distribution*` matched none of them. `pleiades validate` passed it, since the refusal of a filter that
matches nothing is inside the method (`TestGather_RefusesAFilterThatMatchesNothing`), and the task would have failed on
every host. The test case "setup no subset" (`internal/forge/playbook/modules_test.go`) asserted the copy-through.

**Root cause.** 334's and 848's: an argument copied across because its name is the same on both sides. A filter's value
is a pattern over the other side's fact names, so its meaning changed when the names did, with the spelling unchanged.

**Why 848 did not hold.** 848 fixed `gather_subset` by computing its meaning and left `filter` as a copy, which was
correct then: both sides used Ansible's names. Nothing tied the converter's argument table to the method's key names,
so the rename that changed what `filter` matches did not touch the converter. 334's `ansible-doc` check compares
argument names and values, not what a pattern matches.

**Fix.** `85a4c89f`. The converter refuses `filter` for review (`ArgBlock`, code `args.unmapped`), with a reason that
names the native families and the migration guide's fact table. The test case is now "setup filter" and asserts the
refusal. A later converter change is to translate the patterns rather than refuse them.

**Lesson.** When a method's key names change, every converter argument whose value names those keys (filters,
patterns, selectors) is reviewed in the same change; a pattern copied across holds only while both sides spell the
keys alike.

## 968. The converter's first fact conditions changed Ansible's meaning on every path but the comparison it was written for (fixed before merge, a repeat in kind of 848 and 967)

**Symptom.** Found by two reviews of the converter rewrite (Phase 41h PR 2, 2026-11-07), never released: the first
version turned `ansible_os_family == "Debian"` into a native read correctly, and read the native fact on every other
condition path as if it were Ansible's: an absent native fact (no codename on Alpine, Arch, Fedora) failed the task
where Ansible's `NA` compares false; `ansible_distribution_major_version >= "8"` compared an integer where Ansible
compares text ("10" < "8"); `| int` on a version string or an absent fact gave a CEL error or false where Jinja gives 22
or 0; `is match("Ubuntu|Debian")` matched Ansible's word against `ubuntu`; a fact read as a truth failed on an absent
fact where `NA` is true; `ansible_architecture == "x86_64"` was true on Windows, where Ansible says `64-bit`; the
inserted gather had no tag, so `--tags` dropped it and every fact condition failed; a play var shadowing a fact was
read as the fact; a refusal quoted the playbook's value (a repeat of 330).

**Root cause.** The value rewrite was hooked into `compare` only, and the translated read was an ordinary CEL term
every other node (filter, regex, truth) treated as the value Ansible would have, though only `compare` knew it was not.

**Fix.** `5c9ca2fc`, `17d4e2b4`, `65182d96`. The conversion keeps to equality and membership against strings, with an
absent fact guarded as unequal (`guardFact`); every other path on a fact term (filters, `| int` included, orderings,
pattern tests, truth reads) refuses `when.fact`, and so do values with no one native word on every host
(`ansiblefacts.NativeValue`: architecture, swap, a release starting with a digit, a non-canonical major version). The
gather is tagged `always`; a localhost play or one tuning its gather keeps its facts dropped; a shadowed fact is left to
the ordinary resolution; refusals name the value's kind. `TestTranslate_AFactReadKeepsAnsiblesMeaning` and the live
`TestMigratePlaybook_AFactReadDecidesPerHostAsAnsibleDoes`, whose absent-codename case on Alpine is red without the
guard.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 410.

## 969. The two fact stores kept a value's last confirmation differently, and the shared conformance suite had no case that showed it (fixed before push, a repeat in kind of 113 and 749)

**Symptom.** Found 2026-11-07 by the random differential written for Phase 41h ("seen versus changed"), on its first
run, never released. The Crawl file store kept the last sighting per (key, value hash) in `<device>.state.json`, so after
a late change wrote a value back (A, B, A), the first A's history entry claimed the later A's sighting, a time after B
had started; the ent store kept it per row. The file store's Current also read every stable value before every
volatile one, while the ent store read rows in the order written, so where orders from several sources mix (where
`facts.Later` is not transitive) the two could name different current values for one key.

**Root cause.** Both stores implemented one contract by hand, and `internal/facts/factstest`'s conformance cases
covered the ordinary orders only: no case had a late change followed by a later confirmation, or a kind change under
mixed order sources.

**Why 113 and 749 did not prevent it.** Both were two statements of one rule that disagreed and were reconciled once;
nothing kept them agreeing afterwards. Here a shared suite existed, and still passed both stores, because a suite
proves only the cases written into it.

**Fix.** Branch `feat/facts-seen-vs-changed-41h`. One derivation, `facts.Sightings`, now gives both stores their last
confirmations, per stored value; the file store reads its values in the order written (`device.written`). The suite
gained `derivedReadsMatchTheOracle`, which replays 120 random sequences into each store (SQLite, PostgreSQL, files)
