passed. 815 was path cleaning removing a `..` a test needed; here it resolved one a link was built from.

**Fix.** `8bb76bb2`: every CML request goes through `httpapi.Join`, which refuses a dot segment, and `FindLab` looks a
reference of `.` or `..` up among the titles, since no lab id can be one (`TestLab_SendsTheIDEscapedOnce`,
`TestFindLab_FindsADotTitleByItsTitle`, `pkg/cml`). `0043a3b4` and `210afa18`: every record link the UI builds goes
through `view.Addressable`, `view.RecordPath` or `view.RowPath` (`internal/ui/view/paths.go`), which escape the id as
one segment and give no link for `""`, `.` or `..`. A write to such a record returns to its list, and a middleware
(`internal/ui/web/dotsegments.go`) answers 404 to a dot segment, or to an empty segment anywhere but the start and the
end, before sign-in. `TestNothingElseBuildsAPathFromAnID` (`internal/ui/view/paths_rule_test.go`) refuses a path built
from an id anywhere else (1017). Tests: `TestRecordLinks_WithholdALinkNoURLCanCarry`, `TestRoutes_RefuseADotSegment`,
`TestRoutes_RefuseADotSegmentBeforeSignIn`, `TestResourcePath_ReturnsAnUnaddressableRecordToItsList`.

**Lesson.** An id of `""`, `.` or `..` has no URL, and escaping does not give it one. Refuse it where the path is built,
in one helper every link goes through.

**Class.** C4 (path traversal and confinement escape; CWE-22)
**Portable.** yes: any path built from url.PathEscape(id) without refusing "", "." and ".."
**Detector.** ids "", "." and ".." through each path builder, expecting a refusal or no link; see
~/vuln-corpus/README.md

## 1012. chi v5.4.0 routes on r.URL.RawPath whenever a request has one and records the parameter still escaped, so the API's link builder escaped sw%2F1 again into sw%252F1, and the 405 handler, matching r.URL.Path, found no route and sent no Allow header (fixed on this branch; on main since 5387aaa8, 2026-08-07, 72's fix)

**Symptom.** The sweep marked the link case as not settled by the files it was given. It was settled in chi's source:
`Mux.routeHTTP` (`mux.go` line 462 in v5.4.0) routes on `r.URL.RawPath` when it is set. A request for
`/inventory/devices/sw%2F1` was handed links to `sw%252F1`, another device. `PUT /inventory/devices/sw%2F1` got a
405 with no `Allow` header.

**Root cause.** 72's fix (`5387aaa8`) built each href from the matched route pattern and escaped each parameter value
with `url.PathEscape`, taking the value as decoded. A request has a RawPath exactly when a name holds a character whose
escaping differs from the default (a `/` or a `;`), and then chi's value is still escaped. `internal/api/options.go`
matched the decoded path, which splits `sw%2F1` into two segments.

**Fix.** `220fd100`: `routedValue` (`internal/api/links.go`) decodes a value only when the request has a RawPath, so a
literal `%` in a value chi already decoded is never read as an escape. `8aa9bb00`: `routedPath` gives the 405 handler
the form chi routed on, and the href test gains rows holding a literal `%` beside a slash, which pass only while chi
records a value still escaped, so a chi release that changes that fails the test. Tests, red on the old code:
`TestHrefFor_EscapesARoutedNameOnce` and `TestHrefFor_RefusesAnUndecodableEscapedValue`
(`internal/api/hypermedia_internal_test.go`), `TestMethodNotAllowed_FindsTheRouteOfAnEscapedName`
(`internal/api/options_test.go`). The handlers still read the value escaped (1013).

**Lesson.** Code beside a router reads the path the router matched, and a value in the form the router recorded it; for
chi that is RawPath when it is set. Pin the router's behavior in a test, so a release that changes it fails.

## 1013. The API's handlers read chi.URLParam still escaped, so a device named sw/1 cannot be addressed, and 1012's links now point at /devices/sw%2F1, where the handler acts on the literal name sw%2F1 (open: passed to the owner's separate pull request, N1; on main since 9224cd24, 2026-08-04)

**Symptom.** Found by fp-reviewer on `fix/url-escaping`, 2026-11-08, reviewing 1012's fix. Each handler in
`internal/api` reads its id with `chi.URLParam`, which returns the value chi recorded: still escaped when the request
has a RawPath (1012). A request for `/inventory/devices/sw%2F1` is served for the record named literally `sw%2F1`, and
so is one for `sw%252F1`. A record named `sw/1` has no URL. Since 1012's fix, a response's links name `/devices/sw%2F1`,
which a client reads as `sw/1`, while the handler there acts on `sw%2F1`.

**Root cause.** 1012's fix corrected the side that builds an address and left the side that resolves it. Decoding in
the handlers is a change of its own, since it changes which record a name holding `%` reaches.

**Status.** Open. Passed to the owner's separate pull request (N1). Whether this has a security effect has not been
checked.

**Lesson.** Pending the fix. LESSONS 420: a fix to one side of an encode and decode pair names and tests the other.

**Resolved 2026-11-08 (fixed on `fix/addressable-names`, `bdba8259` and `fb7f98dc`, with `3a952e13` from review).**
Every value chi routes is decoded once, through `api.PathParam` (`internal/api/pathparam.go`), which decodes only when
the request has a RawPath, so a literal `%` in a value chi already decoded is never read as an escape. The UI's handlers
read theirs through `Handler.param` (`internal/ui/web/params.go`), which calls it. An escape that does not decode is a
400, never a 404. `TestOnlyPathParamReadsARoutedValue` (`internal/archtest/routed_value_test.go`) refuses chi's
`URLParam` outside that file and holds every other read of a routed path by type (1038). Tests, red on the old code:
`TestDeviceRoutes_FetchTheDeviceTheURLNames`, `TestDeviceRoutes_UpdateTheDeviceTheURLNames` and
`TestDeviceRoutes_DeleteTheDeviceTheURLNames` (`internal/api/pathparam_router_test.go`), which run GET, PATCH and DELETE
through `api.NewRouter` over a real ent repository on SQLite, with each name seeded beside a decoy record named as its
escaped form, the record the old handlers acted on instead; `TestPathParam_DecodesOnlyWhatChiRecordedEscaped`
(`internal/api/pathparam_internal_test.go`); `TestRoutedHandlers_AnswerAnUndecodableEscapeWith400`; and, for the UI,
`TestDevices_ANameAURLMustEscapeIsReachedByItsLink` (`internal/ui/resources/addressed_names_test.go`) and
`TestRoutes_AnswerAnUndecodableEscapeWith400` (`internal/ui/web/params_test.go`). The same branch refuses `""`, `.` and
`..` as a new device name or fact key (`internal/recordname`), in both stores, the hosts.yaml backstop, the API, the UI
form, the CLI and sync (`OutcomeRefused`), since 1011 showed no URL can carry them. Whether the old reads had a
security effect was not checked. Defects found while fixing it: 1032 to 1041.

## 1014. Keeping catalystcenter's base path as written gave one controller two BaseURL() values, a%2fb and a%2Fb, and BaseURL is the synced controller's DeviceID (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/url-escaping`, 2026-11-08, before push. `520f18f6` (1008) kept the operator's own spelling
of the base path, so `a%2fb` and `a%2Fb`, or `%7E` and `~`, gave two `BaseURL()` values for one appliance, and BaseURL is
the synced controller's DeviceID.

**Root cause.** The fix kept text as written where that text is also an identity, and RFC 3986 allows several
spellings of one path.

**Fix.** `d7f20082`. `basePath` and `normalizeEscapes` (`pkg/catalystcenter/baseurl.go`) put the path in RFC 3986
section 6.2.2's normal form: an escaped unreserved character is decoded, and every other escape's hex is upper case. A
literal `;` and `%3B` stay apart, and an escaped slash stays escaped. Escaping the whole path with `url.PathEscape` was
rejected, because it rewrites `;` and `,`, which a Java server reads differently. Test:
`TestNew_GivesOnePathOneIdentity`.

**Lesson.** When a fix keeps text as written, check whether that text is also an identity. If it is, give one value one
spelling through the normal form the standard defines.

## 1015. The database backup built its DSN host as host + ":" + port, so an IPv6 host such as ::1 gave postgres://...@::1:5433/..., which lib/pq reads as the host ::1:5433 on the default port (fixed on this branch; on main since ed27c14e, 2026-09-18)

**Symptom.** Found by the same sweep, 2026-11-08. `internal/backup/pg.go` opens its own connections for backup and
restore, and a `DB_DSN` naming `[::1]:5433` became a DSN pointing at the wrong host and port.

**Root cause.** Concatenation instead of `net.JoinHostPort`. `pkg/winrmexec`'s `Host` field documents the same kind of
failure (a bracketed IPv6 literal once built an unparsable WS-Man URL), but it never had an entry here, so no search
looked for other host joins.

**Fix.** `17496325`. The host is `net.JoinHostPort(t.host, t.port)`. Test, red on the old code:
`TestTargetDSN_BracketsAnIPv6Host` (`internal/backup/words_internal_test.go`). User-visible:
`changelog/backup-ipv6-dsn.fixed.md`.

**Lesson.** A host and a port are joined only with `net.JoinHostPort`, and a test of each join uses an IPv6 literal.

## 1016. Two of the branch's first tests could pass with the fix removed: a FuzzJoin property that the old Join also met, and a dot-segment middleware test whose passing half asserted what a probe handler that echoed any id served (fixed before push, a repeat of 54 and 958; LESSONS 213, 338)

**Symptom.** fp-reviewer, on `fix/url-escaping`, 2026-11-08, before push. `15e2d5a8` added a FuzzJoin property: what
is sent decodes to the path Join checked. The old Join sent the decoded path, so it met that property too. The first
middleware test (`0043a3b4`, `internal/ui/web/dotsegments_test.go`) asserted that paths it should pass were served,
through a probe that echoed any id, so it said nothing about what the middleware passed on.

**Root cause.** Each test asserted a property the old code also had.

**Why 54, 958, 213 and 338 did not prevent it.** LESSONS 213 and 338 ask for a run with the protection removed for each
test of a protection. The branch's named regression tests were held red on the old code; the fuzz property and the
middleware test were not run that way until review.

**Fix.** `556bedef`: FuzzJoin varies its base over five (with and without a path, with a trailing slash, with an
escaped path) and counts every escaped slash the base and the ref wrote, which the original Join fails. `210afa18`: the
middleware test asserts what the middleware passes on (`TestRefuseDotSegments_PassesEveryOtherPath`).

**Lesson.** A fuzz property and a middleware test of a fix are tests of that fix: each is run on the old code and must
fail there.

## 1017. The UI's first guard against building a path from an id outside paths.go matched one spelling, url.PathEscape called through the name url, so an aliased import, url.JoinPath, path.Join, an fmt format or a concatenation passed it (fixed before push, a repeat in kind of 194; LESSONS 114)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/url-escaping`, 2026-11-08, before push. `0043a3b4`'s `TestNothingElseEscapesAnIDIntoAPath`
walked the syntax trees of `internal/ui/view` and `internal/ui/web`, those two directories only, for a selector
`PathEscape` on the identifier `url`.

**Root cause.** The guard was written against the one call the fix had removed (LESSONS 114). Like 194's, it matched a
name rather than the thing the name stands for.

**Why 114 and 194 did not prevent it.** Both say a guard written against a spelling misses the next spelling. The first
guard was still written from the incident rather than from the rule it states.

**Fix.** `210afa18`. `TestNothingElseBuildsAPathFromAnID` (`internal/ui/view/paths_rule_test.go`) finds net/url under
any import name and refuses `PathEscape`, `JoinPath`, `path` and `filepath` Join, fmt formats holding a `/` and string
concatenation, in both packages and their subpackages.

**Lesson.** As 114: state the rule as what may not happen (a path built from an id outside `paths.go`), then list
each way to write it and hold the guard to each.

## 1018. A recorded undo value was never held to its parameter's declared Choices, since ParamFits checks only the type, the engine skips ChoiceProblem for a value with no template, and a rollback runbook is never validated, so a probe planned state: purged where the choices were [absent] (fixed on this branch; on main since 27f72c8f, 2026-09-28, Phase 40's planner; a sibling of 534)

**Symptom.** Phase 136b PR 5 (`feat/provider-identity-136b-5`), 2026-11-08, found in review. A probe journal entry
recorded `state: purged` for an undo method whose `state` parameter declares the choices `[absent]`, and the rollback
planner planned it.

**Security.** Low. Writing the journal needs the operator's account (Crawl) or a Runner (Walk), and each can already
act on its devices. This is a validation fix, not a security one.

**Root cause.** Three gaps lined up. `collection.ParamFits` checks only the type. `internal/engine/render_params.go`
skips `ChoiceProblem` for a value with no template, since validation is expected to have checked a literal. A rollback
runbook is built from the journal and never validated. Before the branch, the planner checked a recorded value's type
only for being a list (`recordableValue`).

**Why 534 did not prevent it.** 534 held every value to its declared type at validation and at dispatch. The choices
rule (`collection.ChoiceProblem`, on main since `2dbfa586`) runs in validation and the engine's render path. A value the
planner builds from stored data reaches neither.

**Fix.** `e3bb4cbc`. `checkParamValue` (`internal/rollback/recorded.go`) holds every recorded value to `ParamFits` and
`ChoiceProblem`, on every entry, in the planner and in the Runner's `Verify`. `--leave` is the only answer; no
`--allow-skew` accepts it. Tests, red on the old code: `TestBuild_AValueOutsideTheDeclaredChoicesIsLeaveOnly` and
`TestVerify_ARunnerHoldsRequiredParametersAndChoicesWhateverIsAccepted` (`internal/rollback/skew_review_test.go`).

**Lesson.** A value the system builds from stored data skips validation, so it is held to every rule a written value
meets, at the place that builds it.

## 1019. The Controller's facts subscriber erased a correct Runner's Collection identity in a mixed-version window, since CheckCollection compared the Runner's group with the Controller's own FirstPartyGroupOf, and logged that it "names one no build writes", which was false (fixed on this branch; on main since 7bee73af, 2026-11-08, merged in #134; a repeat in kind of 988, LESSONS 415)

**Symptom.** Phase 136b PR 5, 2026-11-08, found in review. When a release adds a group or moves a method to another
group, a Runner and its Controller route the method to different groups. `facts.Provenance.CheckCollection` then failed
on the Controller, and its facts subscriber (`internal/facts/entstore/subscriber.go`, lines 172 to 176 on main) zeroed
the identity with the warning "storing facts with no Collection identity, since the batch names one no build writes for
its method". The ent store's `Record` refused the same observation outright. The chain hashed the empty identity, so
the provenance cannot be recovered.

**Root cause.** A rule on release data (the first-party group list) ran in a process of another release than the one
that made the value. 988's fix moved `CheckCollection` to where a value is written, and the Controller writes its own
store, so it kept the check. vuln-corpus finding C19_auto-roboto_2026-11-08 had kept that write-side check on purpose.

**Why 988 did not prevent it.** 988 and LESSONS 415 say a rule on release data runs only where the value is written,
and both looked at one process across two releases. Here two processes of two releases run at once. The Controller
writes the row, but the Runner's build made the identity, so the Controller's release data says nothing about it.

**Fix.** `0928e94b`. `CheckCollection` is now `CheckDeliveredCollection` (`Valid` only) plus `CollectionRouting` (the
group rule), in `internal/facts/provenance.go`. The Controller's subscriber and ent store hold a delivered identity to
`CheckDeliveredCollection`, log a routing difference at info, and store the identity as sent. `CheckCollection`, both
parts, stays on the Runner's engine and the CLI's file store, whose own build routed the method. Test, red on the old
code: `TestStores_KeepTheSameIdentityForOneTask` (`internal/facts/entstore/identity_agree_test.go`) feeds one task's
identity to the Controller's journal store and its fact store and finds the two agree.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 422: in a mixed-version window, a rule on release data runs only in the process whose release made
the value.

## 1020. The Controller's facts subscriber drops every fact under collection.FactFloor() from a method missing from its catalog, with a warning that calls them spoofed, so a Runner newer than its Controller loses its new built-ins' facts (open: an owner decision; on main since f61076b7, 2026-11-07, Phase 135b; the class of 1019)

**Symptom.** Found by two reviewers reading the code during Phase 136b PR 5, 2026-11-08. Not run. `builtinProvenance`
(`internal/facts/entstore/provenance.go`, lines 64 to 78) keeps a fact whose key falls under `collection.FactFloor()`
only when the Controller's catalog holds the batch's method. Otherwise the subscriber drops it and logs "dropping facts
a built-in holds that a batch says a method outside the catalog emitted". Two cases follow:
- A Runner newer than its Controller runs a built-in that the Controller's catalog lacks, and the facts it gathers under
  the floor are dropped. That happens only against the documented upgrade order.
- The Controller's FactFloor may grow on a minor release. An older Runner's external program whose namespace a newer
  Controller has since reserved would have its facts dropped.

**Root cause.** Reasoned, not measured: the same shape as 1019. The Controller judges a Runner's batch by its own
release's catalog and floor.

**Status.** Open. It is an owner decision (task #11). Nothing was changed on this branch.

**Lesson.** Pending the decision. LESSONS 422 names the class.

## 1021. The PR 5 plan deadlocked: its section 4 refused a needless --allow-skew, while its section 6 told the operator to add one where the Controller's declarations match the recording and the Runner's may not (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found in review of the PR 5 plan, before push. On the Walk tier the Controller
plans and a Runner runs. Where the Controller's declarations matched the recording, the plan's section 4 refused an
`allow_skew` name as needless, and section 6 told the operator to add that name so a Runner whose declarations differ
would replay the step. No request could satisfy both.

**Root cause.** The "needless" rule judged by the planner's declarations. Only on the CLI, which plans and runs in one
process, are those the executor's declarations too.

**Fix.** `74afeaa9`. `rollback.Request.ExecutorIsPlanner` (`internal/rollback/plan.go`). The CLI sets it
(`cmd/pleiades/rollback.go`) and refuses a needless name. The Controller marks each named node `SkewAccepted`
(`wire.RollbackStep.SkewAccepted`) even where its own declarations match. On the Runner, `SkewAccepted` relaxes only the
digest comparison. Tests: `TestBuild_AllowSkewNamingNoSkewDependsOnWhoRunsIt` (`internal/rollback/skew_test.go`),
`TestRollback_AllowSkewMarksANodeTheControllerFindsUnskewed` (`internal/api/dispatcher_rollback_skew_test.go`),
`TestRollbackCommand_RefusesANeedlessAllowSkew` (`cmd/pleiades/rollback_skew_internal_test.go`), and the Walk rollback
gate (`cmd/runner/rollback_release_gate_test.go`).

**Lesson.** When one process plans and another runs, a rule that calls a request needless says whose data it judges by.
A planner cannot call a name needless for an executor whose declarations it has not seen.

## 1022. The required-parameter check ran only once a skew was found, so an entry with no identity, or one on the group-digest fallback, planned an undo missing a parameter its method requires; the first fix still waived it when the undo digest matched (fixed before push, a repeat in kind of 557 and 823; LESSONS 244)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, before push. The check that a recorded undo gives every parameter
its method requires sat inside the skew branch. An entry with no identity, or one with an identity and no undo digest
(the group-digest fallback), never reached that branch. The first fix (`e3bb4cbc`) ran the check unless the undo digest
matched this build's. A second review (Fable) found that this still waived it for a forged entry carrying a matching
digest.

**Root cause.** The guard was placed on one branch of a comparison, so it ran only where a difference was found. The
cases where nothing could be compared were the sibling path.

**Why 557, 823 and LESSONS 244 did not prevent it.** Each is about a guard on one path and not on its sibling: two
callers, or validation and the run. Here both paths were branches of one function, and the missing case was the one
where the comparison had no input. That does not read as a second path until it is listed.

**Fix.** `9b701120`. The required check is unconditional on both tiers, in the planner and in the Runner's `Verify`. Of
the four built-in undos that leave a required parameter out of `Record`, all four withhold it, so that case is already
refused as "not recorded in full"; the check costs a real undo nothing. Tests, red on the old code:
`TestBuild_ARequiredParameterIsAlwaysHeld` and `TestVerify_ARunnerHoldsRequiredParametersAndChoicesWhateverIsAccepted`
(`internal/rollback/skew_review_test.go`).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 421: a rule that holds in every case runs beside a comparison, never inside the branch a difference
opens.

## 1023. The rollback planner and the Runner's Verify first held a stored Collection identity to Valid, whose format-character check reads Go's Unicode tables (fixed before push, a repeat of 1003 and 988; LESSONS 415)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, before push. The two new readers of a stored identity, the planner and the
Runner's `Verify`, called `wire.CollectionIdentity.Valid`. A Go release that updates the Unicode tables could make an
identity one build wrote fail another build's reader, and refuse its rollback.

**Root cause.** 1003's class exactly: a writer's rule used by a reader.

**Why 1003 and 988 did not prevent it.** 1003 was fixed one day earlier, in Phase 136b PR 4, and LESSONS 415's
correction says a reader holds an identity to `Shape`. Both fixed the readers that existed then. The planner and
`Verify` were new readers, and nothing makes a new reader call `Shape`; the rule lives in a lesson and a doc comment.

**Fix.** `74afeaa9`, as committed. `checkIdentity` (`internal/rollback/recorded.go`) holds a stored identity to `Shape`,
and the package text in `internal/rollback/skew.go` says why. `TestBuild_AGroupHoldingAFormatCharacterIsPrintedEscaped`
(`internal/rollback/skew_test.go`) stores a group holding U+202E, which `Shape` accepts and `Valid` refuses, and holds
the planner to reading it.

**Lesson.** As 1003: a new reader of a stored value calls the reader's rule, and its test stores a value only the
writer's rule refuses.

## 1024. A fragment change moves an undo's UndoDigest but not its GroupDigest, since a manifest names its fragments as strings, so the plan's rule "group digests equal means no skew" would have missed it (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found in review of the PR 5 plan and design, before push. `collection.UndoDigest` expands the parameter
fragments an undo method uses. `GroupDigest` hashes the group's manifests, which name their fragments by string, so a
change inside a fragment leaves it equal. The plan compared group digests first and called equal group digests no skew.

**Root cause.** The plan treated the coarser digest as a summary of the finer one. It is not: the two digests cover
different inputs.

**Fix.** `74afeaa9`. The undo digest decides. The group digest is used only for an entry that recorded no undo digest
(`internal/rollback/skew.go`). Tests of the order: `TestBuild_AChangedGroupWithAnUnchangedUndoReplaysWithAWarning` and
`TestBuild_AChangedUndoIsRefusedUntilAcceptedByName` (`internal/rollback/skew_test.go`).

**Refuted.** Fable said `UndoDigest` misses a parameter's `Default`. It already hashes `Type`, `Required`, `Default`,
`AliasOf`, `Choices`, `ChoicesIgnoreCase`, `Format`, `RunSetting` and `SecretRefs` (`pkg/collection/identity.go`, lines
150 to 184; 986's fix added the last three).

**Lesson.** Before ordering two digests, list what each one hashes. A digest that names a part by string does not move
when the part changes.

## 1025. The group-digest fallback compared a recorded group digest with the digest of the group this build routes the method to, which is release data (fixed before push, the class of 988 and 1019; LESSONS 415)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, before push. For an entry with an identity and no undo digest, the
planner compared the recorded group digest with the digest of the group this build's `FirstPartyGroupOf` names. After a
release moves the method, that is another group's digest, and the comparison reads as a skew for a reason that has
nothing to do with the undo.

**Root cause.** 988's class: the reader compared against a value its own release decides.

**Fix.** `9b701120`. The fallback compares the recorded digest with the digest of the group the entry recorded, while
this build holds methods of that group. Only when this build holds none of that group's methods is the routed group
compared. Test, red on the old code: `TestBuild_TheGroupFallbackComparesTheGroupTheEntryRecorded`
(`internal/rollback/skew_review_test.go`).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 422: compare a stored value with what its own release said, not with this release's routing.

## 1026. The plan's warnings and the Runner's skew note reached only process logs, so a Walk operator never saw what a rollback accepted (fixed before push; two parts left open by design)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, before push. The Controller's plan warnings and the Runner's note for a
step run under an accepted skew went only to the process logs, which a Walk operator does not read.

**Root cause.** The warnings were written for the CLI, where the operator reads the process's output. The owner's rule
for the dispatch's identity warnings (PR 4: the Runner's log plus a `task.warning` job event) had not been applied here.

**Fix.** `baa22d2c`. The Runner publishes a `task.warning` job event for each step it runs under an accepted skew,
beside its own log line. `POST /jobs/{id}/rollback` answers 202 with `warnings`, always a list, each with its node,
device and message. Tests: `TestAdapter_Execute_PublishesTheSkewItAccepted`
(`internal/adapters/native/rollback_skew_test.go`), `TestRollbackJob_AnswersWithThePlansWarnings`
(`internal/api/dispatcher_rollback_skew_test.go`), and the Walk rollback gate, which reads the skewed rollback's job log
and finds each step's warning.

**Open, by design.** The Controller does not post the plan's warnings as job events: its NATS grant
(`meshid.ControllerGrant`) does not publish on job log subjects, which only a Runner does, so under operator mode such a
publish would be denied with no reply. The UI's record action can only redirect, and no notice survives a redirect.

**Lesson.** A warning is written where the person who acts on it reads, on each tier.

## 1027. The Controller computed GroupDigest eagerly for every rollback step, about 1 ms each, or about 5 s for 1,000 devices (fixed before push, the class of 490 and 855)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, before push. The Controller's planner digested a step's whole group
for every step, whether or not the result was compared or printed.

**Root cause.** A per-item cost that grows with the group, paid where most items never use it.

**Fix.** `e3bb4cbc`. The group digest is computed only for an entry that recorded no undo digest, or for a message.
Test: `TestSkew_DigestsTheGroupOnlyWhenItMustCompareOrSayIt` (`internal/rollback/skew_lazy_internal_test.go`).

**Lesson.** As 490 and 855: a cost paid once per item is measured against the largest job, and computed only where its
answer is read.

## 1028. Stored FQCNs and node ids were printed raw in rollback refusals, warnings, job events and the API's problem and warning fields, so a U+202E reached the 422 body (fixed before push, a repeat of 257 and 619)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, before push. A Walk journal row is a Runner's to write. Neither the
Controller's subscriber nor the planner holds its FQCN, undo FQCN or node id to a shape, so a direction override or a
zero-width character in one reached a refusal, a warning, the API body and the job's log as written. A U+202E reached
the 422 body.

**Root cause.** `internal/termsafe` escapes only what a terminal acts on, and JSON escapes only control characters. A
format character passes both.

**Why 257 and 619 did not prevent it.** Both were third-party text printed raw, and each fix quoted the text at the
place that printed it. The rollback's text comes from a stored row, and the new messages were written without asking
where their names came from.

**Fix.** `4a9de8bd`. `rollback.Printable` (`internal/rollback/printable.go`) passes plain visible ASCII as it is, which
every registered method and graph node id is, and quotes anything else. Every rollback message uses it, as do the API's
problem and warning node fields, a Runner's skew note and the CLI's accept hints. Tests:
`TestPrintable_QuotesOnlyWhatIsNotAPlainName`, `TestBuild_PrintsAStoredMethodNameAndNodeIdEscaped`
(`internal/rollback`), `TestRollbackJob_PrintsAStoredGroupAndNodeEscaped` (`internal/api`),
`TestAdapter_Execute_PrintsADispatchedNameEscapedInTheJobLog` (`internal/adapters/native`), and
`TestRollbackCommand_PrintsAGroupEscaped` (`cmd/pleiades`).

**Lesson.** A name read from a stored row is third-party text. Print it through one helper that passes only what a
reader can see as written.

## 1029. Text claimed more than the code did: "every recorded value is still checked", "a moved group is never a refusal", "a Runner under an older Controller refuses every changed step", a "matches" warning when nothing was compared, and a test comment citing "finding 1's deadlock" (fixed before push, a repeat of 228, 571 and 1006)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, before push.
- "Every recorded value is still checked" was said in three places while the planner held a recorded value to its type
  and not its choices.
- "A moved group is never a refusal" was true only off the group-digest fallback.
- "A Runner under an older Controller refuses every changed step": an older Controller sends no digests, so nothing is
  compared.
- The warning for a node `allow_skew` named with no digests said the undo "matches" this Controller's declarations,
  when nothing was compared.
- A test comment cited "finding 1's deadlock", which no record holds.

**Root cause.** 228's class: sentences written to the plan rather than to the code, and not reread when the code
changed.

**Why 228, 571 and 1006 did not prevent it.** Their rule is still checked only by a review. 1006 was the day before, in
PR 4 of the same phase.

**Fix.** The first claim became true with 1018's fix (`e3bb4cbc`), which holds every recorded value to its type and its
choices. The "matches" warning now says nothing was compared, and the test comment is gone (`e3bb4cbc`;
`TestBuild_AllowSkewOnANodeWithNoDigestsSaysNothingWasCompared`). The guide's moved-group and older-Controller sentences
were corrected in `044cf7b4`.

**Lesson.** As 1006: before review, reread each sentence the branch added against the code it describes, and say each
exception in the same sentence.

## 1030. The journal's EntStore.saveOne cleared an identity with no log, so a caller other than the subscriber lost an identity with no trace (fixed before push, a repeat in kind of 883; LESSONS 244)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, before push. `b62e4d37` (1007's fix) held each saved entry to the identity
rule in the store and logged the reasons in the subscriber only. The store's `Save` dropped them, so any other caller
cleared an identity silently.

**Root cause.** The rule moved into the store, and its report stayed with one caller.

**Why 883 did not prevent it.** 883's lesson says each drop names what it dropped. The drop here was named on the
subscriber's path and not on its sibling (LESSONS 244).

**Fix.** `8b7f1b6e`. The store logs each cleared identity or undo digest with the job, device, node, fqcn and reason,
through the logger `cmd/controller` hands it (`WithStoreLogger`) or the process default. Test:
`TestEntStoreLogsToTheLoggerItIsGiven` (`internal/journal/ent_store_logger_test.go`).

**Lesson.** A drop is reported where the drop happens, so every caller of that code gets the report.

## 1031. The Controller holds a Runner's delivered Collection identity to wire.CollectionIdentity.Valid, whose format-character check reads Go's Unicode tables, so a Controller built with a newer Go could clear an identity an older Runner's Valid accepted (open: an owner decision; low severity; in the facts subscriber on main since 7bee73af, 2026-11-08, and in the journal store since b62e4d37 on this branch; the class of 1003 and 1019)

**Symptom.** Found by records-keeper on `feat/provider-identity-136b-5`, 2026-11-08, while writing 1019 and 1007's
resolution. Reasoned from the code, not run. Two places on the Controller hold an identity a Runner sent to `Valid`:
the journal store (`identityProblems`, `internal/journal/identity.go`) and the facts subscriber
(`facts.Provenance.CheckDeliveredCollection`, `internal/facts/provenance.go`). `Valid`'s format-character check reads
Go's Unicode tables (1003). Unicode can move an assigned code point into another category: U+180E MONGOLIAN VOWEL
SEPARATOR went from Zs to Cf in Unicode 6.3. So a Controller built with a newer Go than its Runner could refuse, under
`Valid`, an identity the Runner's `Valid` accepted, and clear it.

**Severity.** Low. The identity is cleared and logged, never refused. The facts and the journal row are kept. Every
first-party group name is ASCII (the 30 in `pkg/collection/firstparty.go`), so only a group named by an external program
could carry such a character.

**Root cause.** LESSONS 422's class, with the toolchain as the release data. 1019's fix moved the Controller from
`CheckCollection` to `CheckDeliveredCollection` and kept `Valid` there, on the view that `Valid` depends on no release.
1003 showed it reads the Unicode tables, and LESSONS 415's correction says the same of readers. A Controller storing a
Runner's value is in the reader's position for the release data its check reads.

**Remedy options, for the owner.**
- At the Controller, hold a delivered identity to `Shape` plus the Program and ProviderProgram rule, and keep `Valid`
  only where the identity is made (the Runner's engine and the loader).
- Or accept it, and say so in `docs/13-releases-and-stability.md`.

**Status.** Open. Nothing was changed on this branch.

**Lesson.** Pending the decision. LESSONS 415 and 422: a check on a value another process made reads only what no
release, the toolchain's included, can change.

## 1032. The API's request log and trace span recorded the decoded r.URL.Path, so GET /inventory/devices/sw%2Ffacts, the device "sw/facts", was logged as /inventory/devices/sw/facts, the facts of the device "sw" (fixed on this branch; on main since d907d123, 2026-08-01, in the log, and 25e59f3d, 2026-08-06, in the trace; the class of 1012)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/addressable-names`, 2026-11-08, while fixing 1013. `StructuredLoggerMiddleware` and
`TracingMiddleware` (`internal/api/middleware.go`) recorded `r.URL.Path`, which is decoded, so a name holding an
escaped slash read as one segment more. The request log is close to an audit record: an operator reading it after an
incident could not tell the two requests apart, and its `route` field alone does not say which record was named.

**Root cause.** 1012's class: code beside the router read another form of the path than the one chi matched.

**Why 1012 did not prevent it.** 1012's fix moved the code that resolves a route (the link builder and the 405 handler)
to the form chi routed on. The logger and the tracer record a path rather than resolve one, so they were not on its
list. Since this branch the typed archtest (1038) holds every read of a URL's path in the routed packages.

**Fix.** `c0f86091`, then `8462a125`. `requestPath` records the path as the client sent it (`api.SentPath`, 1035).
Test, red on the old code: `TestRequestLog_RecordsThePathAsSent` (`internal/api/requestpath_test.go`).

**Lesson.** As 1012: whatever records a request records the path the router matched.

## 1033. The UI's appearance forms built their return address from the decoded path, so a theme change on the page of "sw/1" returned to /ui/devices/sw/1, and on the page of "50%" sent Location: /ui/devices/50%, which is not a valid URL (fixed on this branch; on main since db3b8b9f, 2026-09-13; the class of 1012)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-08. `currentURL` and `constrain` (`internal/ui/web/preferences.go`) built the
return address from `r.URL.Path` and `parsed.Path`, both decoded. The reader landed on another page, or on a
`Location` header no client can read as written.

**Root cause.** A decoded path cannot be turned back into the address it came from: decoded, `sw/1` is two segments
and `50%` is a broken escape.

**Fix.** `27b1351b`, then `8462a125`. The return address keeps the path as it was escaped (`api.SentPath`). `constrain`
judges the decoded form, which is what a browser resolves, and refuses a path whose decoded form holds a dot or an empty
segment rather than cleaning it, so keeping the escapes opens no redirect. Tests, red on the old code:
`TestThemeChange_ReturnsToTheRecordItWasMadeOn` (`internal/ui/web/returnaddr_test.go`), and escaped-traversal rows
(`%2E%2E`, `%2F%2F`, a raw backslash beside a raw `|`) in `TestSafeReturn_CannotBeRedirectedOffOrigin`
(`internal/ui/web/safereturn_test.go`).

**Lesson.** An address handed back to a client is built from the path as it was sent, and judged in the form the client
will resolve.

## 1034. A record named like a fixed segment beside {id}, "new" or "chart.json", linked to the UI's create form or chart data rather than its own page, under a comment in handler.go saying such a name could not exist (fixed on this branch; on main since 9de3c7fe, 2026-08-11; a sibling of 1011)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-08. `internal/ui/web/handler.go` registers `/{resource}/new` and
`/{resource}/chart.json` beside `/{resource}/{id}`. chi matches a fixed segment before a parameter, so
`/ui/devices/new` is always the create form. The comment beside them said "a record can never be named "new" or
"chart.json"", but nothing refused either name, and `new` is a legitimate hostname. Such a device's links went to the
create form or the chart JSON. The API's `hrefFor` had the same shape in one place, `/schedules/preview` beside
`/schedules/{id}`; schedule ids are generated, so no link reached it.

**Root cause.** The comment stated an effect of route order as if it were a rule on names.

**Why 1011 did not prevent it.** 1011 found the names no escaping can carry (`""`, `.` and `..`) and refused them. A
name equal to a fixed sibling can be carried, but only by an escaping `url.PathEscape` does not make, and 1011's sweep
did not read the route order.

**Fix.** `44192e90`, with `2f9d1023`. The names are kept. `recordname.Segment` (`internal/recordname/recordname.go`)
percent-encodes the first byte of a name equal to a fixed sibling (`new` becomes `%6Eew`), so chi hands it to `{id}`
and the handler decodes it back to `new`. The UI registers both segments from `view`'s constants, the one list
`view.RecordPath` escapes against, and `TestRecordSiblings_AreTheRoutersOwn` (`internal/ui/web/siblings_test.go`)
walks the built router and holds the two equal. The API derives each pattern's fixed siblings from the route table
`NewRouter` registers (`staticSiblings`, `internal/api/links.go`) and applies the same rule in `hrefFor`. Tests:
`TestDevices_ANameEqualToAFixedSegmentOpensItsOwnPage` (`internal/ui/resources/addressed_names_test.go`),
`TestSegment_EscapesANameEqualToAStaticSibling` (`internal/recordname/recordname_test.go`),
`TestHrefFor_ALinkToAValueEqualToAFixedSegmentReachesItsOwnRoute` and `TestStaticSiblings_ReadsEachShapeOfPattern`
(`internal/api/siblings_internal_test.go`), and `TestStaticSiblings_OfTheAPIsOwnRouteTable`
(`internal/api/siblings_table_test.go`).

**Lesson.** Where a fixed segment sits beside a parameter, a value equal to it is a name the router does not hand to
the parameter. Derive the list of such segments from the router's own registrations, and escape a link to such a name
rather than refuse it.

## 1035. url.URL.EscapedPath ignores a RawPath holding a raw |, ^, backtick, {, }, < or > and escapes the decoded path afresh, so each %2F became a separator: the UI's dot-segment refusal, and the branch's first request log and return address, judged a different path from the one chi routed (fixed on this branch; on main since 910123c3, 2026-11-08, in dotsegments.go, merged in #138; the class of 438 and 1009)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-08. Go's `EscapedPath` returns `RawPath` only when it is a valid escaping of
`Path` (`validEncoded`); otherwise it escapes `Path` again, in which each `%2F` has become a `/`. chi routes on
`RawPath` whenever it is set, and served the right device. Measured: a Go client given `/devices/a%2Fb|c` sends
`/devices/a/b%7Cc`. Three sites read `EscapedPath` and so judged a different path from chi's: the UI's dot-segment
refusal (`internal/ui/web/dotsegments.go`, on main from #138), and this branch's first request log (`c0f86091`) and
return address (`27b1351b`).

**Root cause.** The class of 438 and 1009: a check made on one form of a path while the action uses another.
`EscapedPath` reads as "the path as sent", and it is that except in the case its doc names.

**Why 438 and 1009 did not prevent it.** Both say to decide on the bytes the far side reads. Each site here took
`EscapedPath` for those bytes, which it is for every path a Go client sends. No test sent a path holding such a raw
byte, which another client can send.

**Fix.** `8462a125`. `api.SentPath` (`internal/api/pathparam.go`) returns `RawPath` when the request had one, with only
the raw bytes a valid escaping cannot hold percent-encoded, and otherwise `EscapedPath`. It is always a valid escaping,
with chi's segments, that decodes to `Path`. The request log, the dot-segment refusal and the return address use it,
and the archtest's allowlist names it in place of their own reads. Tests, red on the old code:
`TestSentPath_IsWhatChiMatchedAndAValidEscaping` (`internal/api/pathparam_internal_test.go`),
`TestRawBytePath_IsReadAsChiSplitsIt` (`internal/ui/web/rawpath_test.go`), and new rows in
`TestRequestLog_RecordsThePathAsSent` and `TestSafeReturn_CannotBeRedirectedOffOrigin`.

**Lesson.** Read the exceptions in the doc of an accessor named for the form you want. Code that must agree with a
router reads what the router reads, and its test sends a path a Go client would not.

## 1036. pleiades inventory sync printed each quarantined and conflicted device's name and reason raw from the upstream source, so a crafted Catalyst Center hostname or AWS tag could send ANSI or direction-override sequences to the operator's terminal (fixed on this branch; on main since ad1ff164, 2026-08-06; a repeat of 257, 619 and 1028; LESSONS 266)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-08, while adding the refused outcome to the sync review list.
`printReconciliation` (`cmd/pleiades/inventory.go`) printed `res.Name` and `res.Reason` with `%s`. Both are the
upstream source's text: a device's hostname, or a software type inside a quarantine's reason.

**Security.** Low severity. An attacker needs control of a name or a classified field in a source the operator syncs
(a Catalyst Center hostname, an AWS tag). It gets control sequences onto the operator's terminal: a line rewritten or
hidden, or text shown in another order. The bytes reaching the output were shown by the test on the old code; no
terminal was attacked. Changelog: `changelog/sync-report-escapes-upstream-text.security.md`.

**Root cause.** The list was written with the sync port itself, before any rule on printing remote text.

**Why 257, 619, 1028 and LESSONS 266 did not prevent it.** Each fix quoted the text at the place that printed it, and
no sweep went back over printers that already existed. This one is older than all of them.

**Fix.** `b0db594b`. Each name is printed through `strconv.Quote`, which escapes a control character, a direction
override and invalid UTF-8 and shows an empty name as `""`, and each reason through `termsafe.EscapeLine`. Test, red on
the old code: `TestPrintReconciliation_EscapesWhatTheUpstreamWrote` (`cmd/pleiades/inventory_names_test.go`). The same
class is still open in the CLI's error print (1043).

**Lesson.** As 266. When a rule on printing remote text is written, sweep the printers that already exist, not only
the new one.

**Class.** C1 (delimiter injection into a terminal; CWE-150)
**Portable.** yes: any CLI report that prints names or reasons read from an inventory source it does not control
**Detector.** table-test names and reasons holding ESC, U+202E and invalid UTF-8 through each report printer, and
assert the output holds none of them raw; see ~/vuln-corpus/README.md

## 1037. TestDeviceHandler_PercentEncodedControlsArriveEncoded pinned 1013's defect as chi's behavior, asserting that a handler receives "%0a", "%0d" and "%2f" still escaped (fixed on this branch; on main since 5387aaa8, 2026-08-07; a repeat in kind of 751; LESSONS 213)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-08, when 1013's fix turned the test red. It asserted that a lowercase escape
reaches the handler as three characters, and called that a property of chi. It was a property of the request: a
lowercase escape differs from Go's default encoding, so the request had a RawPath, and chi recorded the value still
escaped (1012). `%00`, which matches the default encoding, arrived decoded. So `edge%0a-01` was looked up as a name no
client escaping in upper case could have created.

**Root cause.** The expected value was what the code did, not what the handler should act on.

**Why 751 and LESSONS 213 did not prevent it.** The test is older than both, and nothing reads old tests again against a
newer rule. It was found only because the fix it pinned against was made.

**Fix.** `bdba8259`. Rewritten as `TestDeviceHandler_PercentEncodedControlsAreDecodedAndRefused`
(`internal/api/devices_test.go`): every escape is decoded once, however the client spelled it, and the name guard
refuses an escaped newline exactly as it refuses a raw one.

**Lesson.** As 751: a test that pins a third party's behavior says why that behavior is the intended one, and is held
by a second case that contradicts the lazy answer (here, the same escape in upper case).

## 1038. The first TestOnlyPathParamReadsARoutedValue was narrower than its rule: it judged "chi routes this package" by an import of chi in the same directory, though chi sets each value still escaped through r.SetPathValue, and it missed a copied URL, a helper taking a *url.URL, RequestURI, RoutePath and a split EscapedPath (fixed before push, a repeat of 1017 and 194; LESSONS 114, 273 and 343)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, 2026-11-08, before push. `38cd196f`'s test said it refused every other
way to read a routed value, and held only packages that import chi. chi v5.4.0's `Mux.routeHTTP` (`mux.go` line 487)
calls `r.SetPathValue(key, value)` with the value it recorded, still escaped, so `r.PathValue` in a package with no
chi import, mounted under chi, reads escaped text. It also matched syntax, so `u := r.URL; u.Path` and a helper taking
a `*url.URL` passed, and `RequestURI`, `RoutePath` and `strings.Split(r.URL.EscapedPath(), "/")` were not held.

**Root cause.** The test decided which code its rule covers by a proxy, an import, rather than by what the runtime does,
and it matched spellings rather than types.

**Why 1017, 194, LESSONS 114, 273 and 343 did not prevent it.** 1017 was found the same day, on #138, in the UI's path
guard; its fix widened that guard's spellings, and this test was written fresh for a new rule, again from the incident.
273 and 343 say to read the property, not a proxy for it. The import looked like the property ("chi routes this code")
until chi's own source was read.

**Fix.** `3a952e13`, with `8462a125`. The test type-checks, with go/types over compiled export data, every package under
`internal/api`, `internal/ui` and `cmd/controller` (`routedRoots`, `internal/archtest/routed_types_test.go`). In every
non-test file of the module it refuses chi's `URLParam`, `URLParamFromCtx`, `URLParams` and `RouteCtxKey` outside
`internal/api/pathparam.go`. In the routed packages it refuses, by type, a read of a `*url.URL`'s `Path`, `RawPath`,
`EscapedPath` or `RequestURI`, an `*http.Request`'s `RequestURI` or `PathValue`, and a `*chi.Context`'s `RoutePath`,
except at the sites `allowedReads` names, each with its reason; an entry nothing reads fails. Reflection and a URL
turned into text first are not held, and the test's doc and `pathparam.go`'s say so. Tests of the test:
`TestTypedReadsFindsEveryWay`, `TestRoutedValueReadsFindsEveryWay` and `TestIsRoutedCoversEachRoot`
(`internal/archtest/routed_value_test.go`).

**Lesson.** As 273 and 343, applied to a rule's scope: decide which code a rule covers from what the runtime does (here,
which handlers chi sets a value for), not from an import that usually goes with it.

## 1039. TestDeviceCreate_RefusesANameNoURLCarries passed with the create handler's name guard removed, since the store's guard refused the same names and mapped to the same 400 (fixed before push, a repeat in kind of 1016; LESSONS 135 and 213)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-08, before push. `8948dfb0` added a name guard to the API's create handler
and a test posting `""`, `.` and `..`. The inventory stores refuse the same names (`ca679684`), and that refusal maps to
400 too, so the test passed with the handler's guard removed.

**Root cause.** LESSONS 135's class: two identical guards in a row, so removing the first changes no outcome.

**Why 1016 and LESSONS 135 did not prevent it.** 1016 was on the branch before this one (#138). Its rule, run each new
test with its fix removed, is applied by hand, and it was not applied here before review.

**Fix.** `06aad2ab`. The test runs against a store stub (`unreachableStore`, `internal/api/devices_names_test.go`) that
fails the test if the handler reaches it, so only the handler's guard can pass it.
`TestDeviceCreate_MapsTheStoresNameRefusalTo400` holds the store's refusal to 400 on its own.

**Lesson.** As 135: to pin the earlier of two identical guards, make the later one fail loudly when it is reached.

## 1040. The record-name rule was first put in a new pkg/recordname, public SDK surface, because internal/facts was said to import no internal package, a habit no record gave a reason for (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-08, before push. `c900b43b` moved `view.Addressable` into a new
`pkg/recordname`, so that the inventory stores, the API, the CLI, sync and `internal/facts` could share it. `pkg/` is
the surface a Collection compiles against, which the planned split of first-party Collections will freeze, and no
Collection uses the rule. The only reason given was a comment saying `internal/facts` imports no internal package.
Nothing gave a reason for that, and no plan moves the facts package out of the module; `7bee73af` had only reworded a
note about it.

**Root cause.** An unwritten constraint was obeyed as if it had a reason, and what obeying it cost (a public package)
was not weighed.

**Fix.** `9924bfe3`. The package is `internal/recordname`. `internal/facts` imports it, and its comment now says only
what is true: it takes `internal/redact`'s two checks from its caller rather than importing that package.

**Lesson.** Before adding to `pkg/`, name the caller outside `internal/` that needs it. A constraint with no recorded
reason is asked about before it is obeyed.

## 1041. Text the branch wrote claimed more than the code did: docs/09 said every other record is addressed by numeric id, a sentence said each segment is decoded once however a client spells its escapes, Reconcile's Reason doc left out refusals, and a gosec waiver cited the removed view.Addressable (fixed before push, a repeat of 571, 789 and 1029)

**Symptom.** Found in review on this branch, 2026-11-08, before push.
- `docs/09-control-plane-and-api.md` said every record but a device is addressed by numeric id. Runbook ids and
  capability names are addressed by name too.
- "Decodes each segment once, however a client spells its escapes" left out the case where Go drops a RawPath that is
  not a valid escaping (1035).
- The doc of `syncplugin`'s `Reason` did not mention the new refused outcome.
- `gosec-waivers.json`'s waiver for `Handler.redirect` cited `view.Addressable`, which `c900b43b` removed.

**Root cause.** 228's class: sentences written to the plan, or left in place while the code under them moved.

**Why 571, 789 and 1029 did not prevent it.** Their rule is still checked only by a review. 1029 was written earlier the
same day, on #139.

**Fix.** `1063049f`: the docs name each record addressed by name and the dropped-RawPath case, `Reason`'s doc names
refusals, and the waiver names `recordname`.

**Lesson.** As 1029: before review, reread each sentence the branch added against the code it describes, and search
the records and waivers for each name the branch removed.

## 1042. An agent ran git stash push -- <path> on a committed file with no changes, which saved nothing and made no stash entry, and its git stash pop then popped and dropped the repository's only stash, the owner's parked GNS3 work, which the handoff said never to drop (recovered the same session; the class of 433)

**Symptom.** On this branch, 2026-11-08, in an agent's worktree. A writer set a committed, unchanged file aside with
`git stash push -- <path>`. With nothing to save, git made no entry. The `git stash pop` after it took the entry on top
of the list, which was `stash@{0}`, the owner's GNS3 link suspend and capture work (`e0362a27`, "On
lab-captures-129b: gns3 link suspend and capture (back burner, 2026-10-25)"), and dropped it. The handoff said never
to drop that stash.

**Recovery.** The commit was found among the repository's unreachable objects and stored again with `git stash store`
under its original message. Nothing was lost. The owner later parked the GNS3 work deliberately, and it is saved in
`~/pleiades-gns`; the stash list is now empty.

**Root cause.** The stash list is one list for the whole repository, shared by every worktree, and `pop` takes the entry
on top, not the one the same process pushed. A push that saves nothing pushes no entry, so the pop took the next one
down.

**Why 433 and LESSONS 268 did not prevent it.** Both name shared branch refs only. Nothing named the stash list as
shared, and the handoff's "never drop it" was a note to readers, not a guard.

**Fix.** A rule for agents (LESSONS 423).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 423: never use git stash to set a file aside in an agent's worktree; copy it aside and restore it
with git checkout.

## 1043. cmd/pleiades/main.go prints a command's error with %v, and some Reconcile errors carry an upstream name raw ("classifying %s", "building %s", "rebuilding %s"), so a crafted upstream name can still reach the operator's terminal unescaped (open: passed to a later CLI pull request; the error print on main since 94ef873c, 2026-08-04, and the Reconcile errors since ad1ff164, 2026-08-06; the class of 1036)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-08, by reading; not run. `cmd/pleiades/main.go` prints errors with `%v` at
lines 93 and 131. `internal/inventory/syncplugin/reconcile.go` wraps `raw.Name`, the upstream source's name, with `%s`
at lines 164, 239 and 290. An error from those paths reaches the terminal at line 131 with the name as written.

**Security.** Low severity, the same as 1036: an attacker who controls a name in a synced source could put control
sequences on the operator's terminal when a classify or build step fails. Reasoned from the code, not measured.

**Status.** Open. Passed to a later CLI pull request (task 14).

**Lesson.** Pending the fix. As 1036: escape a remote system's text where it is printed, including inside an error.

**Resolved 2026-11-09 (fixed on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, `289fbbdf` and `23d89779`; a repeat of 257, 619, 1028 and
1036; LESSONS 266).** Shown on the old code by a test through the real command line: a Catalyst Center device renamed with
an ANSI escape and U+202E, synced, reached stderr raw. The reach was wider than the three messages named above. Sync and
inventory errors carried device names and IDs from a sync source unquoted through `syncplugin.Reconcile`, both
repositories, `internal/inventory/factory.go`, `internal/inventory/create.go` and `internal/inventory/record/`. A newline
in a name could start a forged `pleiades:` line on stderr, which an escape at the print site does not stop (1064).

Two layers now. Where each error is built, the 61 verbs that carry a name or ID use `%q`, so a name prints quoted with
every control character escaped and cannot start a line. Where it is printed, `printError` and `printHelpAnswer`
(`cmd/pleiades/main.go`) pass the text through `termsafe.Escape`, which leaves plain text, tabs and newlines alone and
escapes what a terminal acts on. Tests, shown red on the old code: `TestReconcile_QuotesTheUpstreamNameInEveryError`
(`internal/inventory/syncplugin/reconcile_quoting_test.go`), which stops Reconcile at each of its eight naming steps;
`TestRun_EscapesAnUpstreamNameInACommandsError` and `TestRun_QuotesAnUpstreamNameInAFailedSave`
(`cmd/pleiades/cli_error_escape_test.go`), which sync crafted names through the command line, the second into a
read-only project so the save fails, and assert no line of stderr begins with the forged text; and
`TestPrintError_EscapesWhatATerminalActsOn` (`cmd/pleiades/print_error_test.go`), which holds the print-site layer on its
own (1065). Changelog: `changelog/cli-error-escapes-upstream-text.security.md`.

**Why 257, 619, 1028 and 1036 did not prevent it.** Each quoted remote text at the printer its symptom showed. An
error is built far from where it is printed, and no sweep followed names through the errors that wrap them. The first
fix on this branch repeated that once more (1063).

Still open: a name holding a control character is accepted at creation (1068).

**Class.** C1 (delimiter injection into a terminal; CWE-150; a forged line is CWE-117's shape on stderr)
**Portable.** yes: any CLI whose errors name records read from a source it does not control
**Detector.** sync a name holding ESC, U+202E and a newline followed by a fake program line, make each step that names
it fail, and assert stderr holds none of them raw and no line begins with the fake text; see ~/vuln-corpus/README.md

## 1044. Suspected, from reading only: the UI devices view's Update saves the item Bind built with a new random id, and the ent store's Save looks its row up by id, so editing a device in the web UI against a real store probably fails (open, unverified; on main since 9de3c7fe, 2026-08-11)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-08, by reading; not run. `writer.Update`
(`internal/ui/resources/devices/devices.go`, line 131) ignores its `id` and calls `repo.Save(ctx, item)` with the item
the form's `Bind` built. Read, `Bind` builds that item with a new random id, and the ent repository's `Save` looks its
row up by id, so the save would find no row. No test has shown it.

**Status.** Open, unverified (task 15). The next step is a test that edits a seeded device through the UI over the real
ent repository.

**Lesson.** Pending.

**Resolved 2026-11-09 (fixed on `fix/ui-device-edit`, `6db5b4d5`, with `5f38ecda` and `7b958c25`). Reproduced, and the
failure was not the one guessed; a repeat of 261.** Run through the real UI handler (`web.New` with the real router,
the ent session store, CSRF and admission) over `inventory.NewEntRepository` on SQLite, and over the file store, an edit
of a device's tags answered 303, the success redirect, and stored nothing: the tags stayed as they were, the version
stayed 0, and no revision was recorded. It was not a 500 or a version conflict. The view's `Bind` built the item through
`factory.Build` with a fresh id and version 0, so its `BaseVersion()` equaled its `Version()`, and both stores' `Save`
return nil for "nothing changed" before they look the row up. The lookup by the new id that the symptom above guessed
at was never reached. The edit form also offered `name` and `type`, which neither store's `Save` writes and the stored
type column cannot change.

**Why 261 did not prevent it.** 261 was this defect on the API's PATCH: an item at the version it was loaded at, and a
`Save` that read it as unchanged. Its fix (`record.Base.ChangeTags`) and its lesson (test a write path that ends in that
optimization against the real repository) were applied to the API handler only. Nothing applied them to the UI's
writer, and the UI conformance suite's fake repository hid it: its `Save` returned nil and kept nothing, and it handed
out stored items by pointer, so no read-back in that suite could show the loss (1053).

**Fix.** `writer.Update` (`internal/ui/resources/devices/ports.go`) reads the stored device with `GetByName`, applies the
change through `ChangeTags` and saves that device, so its id, state, source, properties and history are kept, the
version goes up and a revision is recorded. `inventory.ErrVersionConflict` answers 422 on the form and keeps what was
typed. `name` and `type` are `Immutable` (111), so the edit form no longer offers them. Tests, each shown red on the old
code: `TestEditingADeviceUpdatesTheStoredRecord` (ent), `TestEditingADeviceUpdatesTheFileStore`,
`TestAnEditThatLosesARaceIsRefusedAndKeepsTheOtherWrite`, `TestAnEditFormOffersOnlyWhatAnEditCanChange` and
`TestEditingADeviceKeepsItsPropertiesAndState` (`internal/ui/resources/devices/edit_test.go`), and the e2e
`TestUI_FullCRUDRoundTrip` (`tests/e2e/ui_test.go`), which now has an edit step, passes against real PostgreSQL and
fails against the old view (1057).

**Limits, by design.** The edit form carries no version, so a form opened before another change still overwrites the
tags when submitted: last writer wins, as the API's PATCH does without `If-Match`. Only a race between the server's own
read and its save is refused. Neither store can rename a device, so the name stays fixed.

**Lesson.** As 261, and for the suite as well as the code: a write that ends in "unchanged version means nothing to
save" is proven only by reading the record back from a real store, and a fake standing in for that store must keep its
contract (LESSONS 424).

## 1045. The toybox chmod test downloaded toybox 0.8.13 from landley.net on every run, so a CI containers shard failed when that server timed out, with nothing in the repository changed (fixed on this branch; on main since 17d17f8b, 2026-09-28)

**Symptom.** 2026-11-08, a CI run of PR #135, the converter's (run 42506735140, `containers (3)`, at `d963453c`):
`internal/catalog/file`'s `TestToyboxChmod_FiveDigitModesMeanWhatTheySay` failed at `toybox_chmod_test.go:80` with
`downloading toybox 0.8.13: Get "https://landley.net/toybox/downloads/binaries/0.8.13/toybox-x86_64": dial tcp
<ip>:443: i/o timeout`, and the run was rerun. `tools/failures` records it as a real failure that only Actions saw, in a
package pr-check did not test at that commit.

**Root cause.** `fetchToybox` fetched the pinned build from the toybox project's own server every time the test ran,
and failed the test on any download error so that a skip would not read as a pass. The pin (version and SHA-256) fixed
the bytes, not their availability: every container run depended on a third party's server answering during the run.
CI has cached its container images since Phase 118 (LESSONS 262), and nothing did the same for a file a test fetches
for itself.

**Earlier entries.** No earlier entry records a test failing because a publisher's server did not answer. The nearest
are 917 (a fixture's `apk add` from Alpine's moving index) and 966 (rolling image tags), where a third-party source
changed what a test got rather than failing to answer. This is new in kind for files a test downloads.

**Fix.** `6adebb59`, `25134a51`, `dd1ec192`. `internal/testsupport/pins.go` holds every file a test downloads as a
`testsupport.Pin` (`ToyboxChmod`), and `testsupport.Download` serves it from a cache whose file names are the SHA-256
(`PLEIADES_TEST_DOWNLOADS` in CI, `os.UserCacheDir()/pleiades-test-downloads` locally), checking the digest on every
use. A bad cached copy is discarded and fetched again. A changed upstream file fails, whichever way the bytes arrived,
and is never cached. With a cold cache and no network the test skips as `needs toybox`, or fails where
`PLEIADES_TEST_REQUIRE` names toybox, as the containers, branch-containers and nightly jobs now do. The containers jobs
restore and save the directory through `actions/cache`; nightly only restores it. Tests:
`TestFetchPinned_CacheWorksWithTheNetworkGone`, `TestFetchPinned_CorruptCacheIsDiscardedAndRefetched`,
`TestFetchPinned_WrongChecksumFromTheNetworkIsRefusedAndNotCached`, `TestDownload_UnavailableFailsWhenTheRunRequiresIt`.

**Lesson.** A pin fixes a download's bytes, not its availability. A file a test fetches comes from a cache named by its
digest and checked on every use, and a CI job that counts on the test requires its need, so a cold cache during an
outage fails rather than quietly shrinking the run (CI_LESSONS 30).

## 1046. TestProcess_LeavesNoGoroutinesBehind took its goleak snapshot as soon as Connect returned, before the in-process test server had started its own DiscardRequests goroutine, so that goroutine read as a leak on fast-macos (a repeat of 169) (fixed on this branch; on main since 662ffb17, 2026-09-23)

**Symptom.** PR #138, run 42545199991, `fast-macos (3)`, on the test's third repeat: `pkg/remoteexec`'s
`TestProcess_LeavesNoGoroutinesBehind` reported a leaked goroutine. It passed on rerun.

**Root cause.** The test took `goleak.IgnoreCurrent()` right after `Connect`, which returns when the client's handshake
does. The in-process server's `serveConn` (`pkg/remoteexec/remoteexectest/server.go`) starts `go
cryptossh.DiscardRequests(reqs)` only after its own side of the handshake (line 370 at this commit), on its own
schedule. When the server reached that line after the snapshot, its goroutine, which lives as long as the connection,
was missing from the baseline, and goleak reported it as the test's leak. A slow runner widens the window.

**Why 169 did not prevent it.** 169 is the same class: a goleak baseline taken before everything it should ignore had
started. Its fix took the test's own snapshot after its own setup and after a full dial-and-close cycle, and its lesson
said to take the snapshot after the test's own setup. This test did take its own snapshot after its own setup, as the
client saw it. Nothing said that the far side finishes its setup on another goroutine, or that the round trip in 169's
fix was what made the snapshot safe, and no sweep of goleak snapshots followed it.

**Fix.** `241d4a86`. One `conn.Run("true")` before the snapshot. The server accepts a session only inside its channel
loop, after line 370, so once the command returns the goroutine already exists. This is ordered by program order, not
by timing. `DiscardRequests` is not ignored by name, since that would also hide a real leak of the same goroutine on the
client side. Shown red with a temporary 300 ms sleep before line 370, which gave the CI failure's signature; with the
sleep still in place the fixed test passed 5 of 5, and `-count=30` under `-race` passed.

**Lesson.** A goleak snapshot is taken after a round trip with the far side, not when the connecting call returns: the
return proves the caller's side is set up, and the other side's goroutines start on their own schedule (CI_LESSONS
31).

## 1047. need.Require ignored a name in PLEIADES_TEST_REQUIRE that no test needs, so a typo or a renamed need turned a CI requirement off and the job stayed green (fixed on this branch; on main since dd0346ce, 2026-09-29; the class of LESSONS 417 and FAILURE_PATTERNS 930)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch. `required` only reported whether the list named the need being asked about, so a
name no `Require` call used matched nothing and said nothing. A job listing `docekr` for `docker`, or a need still
listed under its old name after a rename, required nothing: every test that should have failed for the missing tool
skipped, and the job stayed green.

**Root cause.** The list was read only to answer "is this need required?", never checked as a whole, and there was no
registry to check it against: each need existed only as a string literal at its `Require` calls.

**Fix.** `e42a6cbe`. `need.Names` registers every need as a constant (`need.Toybox`, `need.RefusingPort` and the rest),
and `Require` fails at its first call when the variable lists a name that is neither in `Names` nor `all`
(`TestRequire_UnknownNameInEnvFails`). `TestEveryRequireCallNamesAKnownNeed` parses every Go file in the module and
checks each `Require` call whose need is a string literal against `Names`; it fails if it finds none of three known
calls, so a walk that sees nothing cannot pass. `TestCIRequireListsOnlyKnownNeeds` parses `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s
lists. Assembling the registry by parsing every Go file found seven names a text search had missed: "a CML
controller", docker-desktop, landlock, landlock-scoping, linux, pty and timeout.

**Limits.** The module walk reads string literals only. A need passed as a constant is held to `Names` by the compiler
only when the constant comes from `need`, as `refusing.Need` now does.

**Earlier entries.** LESSONS 417 (a scanner's silence is not a pass) and 930 (a filter naming a family alone passed the
typo refusal and matched nothing) are this class: a name that matches nothing reads as success. The seven missed names
are the case LESSONS 157 and 273 already name: a search written from what one call looks like finds the calls that
look like it, and a guard over a list reads the code, not a sign of it. The repository's rule to answer questions about
Go code with the language server or the syntax tree, not a text search, covers it, so no new lesson was written.

**Lesson.** A list that turns checks on is checked against the names its readers know, so a name that matches nothing
fails instead of turning a check off (CI_LESSONS 32).

## 1048. testsupport.Download's verdict had no test: all six of the cache's first tests called fetchPinned, so the branch that fails on a changed checksum and the one that skips or fails on an outage could each be deleted with every test green (fixed before push; a repeat in kind of 1016 and 1039; LESSONS 158 and 213)

**Symptom.** fp-reviewer, on this branch, before push. `6adebb59` added six tests of the download cache. Each called
the internal `fetchPinned`, which returns an error. None called `Download`, which turns that error into the test's
verdict: `Fatalf` on a changed checksum, and `Require` (a skip, or a failure where the run requires the need) on an
outage. Deleting either branch left every test green.

**Root cause.** The tests were written against the function that does the work, and the decision a caller sees sat one
level up with no test. LESSONS 158's second half says a skip needs a control of its own; the outage skip had none.

**Why 1016, 1039 and LESSONS 213 did not prevent it.** Their rule, run each new test with its fix removed, is applied
by hand, and it was not applied to `Download` before review.

**Fix.** `dd1ec192`. `TestDownload_ChecksumMismatchFailsTheTest`, `TestDownload_UnavailableSkipsNamingTheNeed` and
`TestDownload_UnavailableFailsWhenTheRunRequiresIt` call `Download` itself; each was shown red by removing its branch.

**Lesson.** As 1016: a test of a verdict calls the function that reaches the verdict. A test one level down proves the
parts, not the decision.

## 1049. The CI download cache was keyed on pins.go, the list of what should be cached, not on what the entry holds, and it is saved only on a miss, so an incomplete entry would have been a permanent hit that never refilled (fixed before push; the shard case is a written rule, not a guard)

**Symptom.** fp-reviewer, on this branch, before push. `6adebb59` keyed the containers jobs' download cache on
`hashFiles('internal/testsupport/pins.go')` and saved `.ci/downloads` only when the restore missed. Two ways to save an
incomplete entry under that key:
- A test binary killed mid-download leaves a `.download-*` temporary file in the directory, and the save step runs under
  `always()`. `@actions/glob` matches dotfiles, so the leftover is saved, with or without the real file.
- Every shard restores the same key, and the first to miss saves only what it downloaded. A second pin used only in
  another shard is missing from that entry, and that shard downloads it on every run and never saves it.

Either way every later run hits the key and nothing saves again until pins.go changes.

**Root cause.** The key named what the entry should hold, and nothing checked that it did. The image cache beside it is
keyed on each shard's own image list and saved only after every image in that list is pulled, so its key does describe
its contents.

**Earlier entries.** None of this class. 127 is the opposite error: a key holding a value that changes by itself, so a
good entry is thrown away on a schedule nobody chose. LESSONS 374 is about cached predictions of state, not CI caches.

**Fix.** `dd1ec192` makes the temporary file in the cache directory's parent, so the directory holds only digest-named
files (`TestNewTempFile_IsOutsideTheCacheDirectory`, `TestFetchPinned_CacheDirectoryHoldsOnlyTheDigestNamedFile`).
`a971dc8d` adds to pins.go that a pin used in a different shard from an earlier one needs the shard number in the key.
That second case is a rule written beside the key, not a guard; today one test uses the one pin.

**Lesson.** A cache key derived from the list of what should be cached, not from what the entry holds, makes an
incomplete entry a permanent hit. Save an entry only when it holds everything its key names, or key it on what it holds
(CI_LESSONS 33).

## 1050. A relative PLEIADES_TEST_DOWNLOADS was used as given, so each test package wrote a download cache into its own directory inside the module tree (fixed before push; the class of 53 and 463)

**Symptom.** fp-reviewer, on this branch, before push. `go test` runs each package in that package's directory, so a
relative value named a different directory for each package, every one of them under the module tree. A mutation run
left a stray `relative/dir/<digest>` file in the tree.

**Root cause.** The value was used as the cache directory with no check that it was absolute.

**Fix.** `dd1ec192`. A relative value is refused with `ErrRelativeDownloadsDir` (`TestDownloadsDir_RelativeEnvIsRefused`,
`TestDownload_RelativeEnvAndBadPinFail`).

**Lesson.** As 463: a directory a test writes to is absolute, or it lands in the module tree, where other tests read.

## 1051. Download's messages named the wrong cause three ways: a malformed pin read as "the published file changed", a machine with no cache directory as "not cached and cannot be fetched" though no fetch was tried, and a body over 16 MiB as a changed checksum (fixed before push; in kind of 126 and 492)

**Symptom.** fp-reviewer, on this branch, before push.
- A pin's SHA256 became the cached file's name with no check of its form. An uppercase or truncated digest can never
  match, so it failed as a changed upstream file.
- With no cache directory, the message said the file was not cached and could not be fetched, when no fetch had been
  tried.
- A body over the 16 MiB read limit was cut at the limit, its digest then did not match, and it was reported as a
  changed checksum.

**Security.** vuln-corpus's sweep flagged the digest used as a file name as its class C4. It is not reachable: the pin
is a constant in the source, not input. Reasoned from the code.

**Root cause.** Each case was reported by the last check that failed, not by the first thing that was wrong.

**Fix.** `dd1ec192`. `ErrBadPin` is raised before any fetch when the SHA256 is not 64 lowercase hex characters, which
also keeps the file name inside the directory (`TestFetchPinned_RefusesAMalformedDigest`). With no cache directory,
`Download` fetches without caching and logs that (`TestDownload_NoCacheDirectoryFetchesWithoutCaching`,
`TestFetchPinned_EmptyDirMeansNoCache`). A body over the limit is `ErrDownloadTooLarge`
(`TestFetchPinned_BodyOverTheLimitIsTooLargeNotAChecksumError`, `TestDownload_OversizedBodyFailsAsTooLarge`).

**Lesson.** As 126 and 492: a refusal names the first thing that was wrong. Check a value's form before using it, and
report a limit as the limit.

## 1052. Two ci.yml comments said a test whose download is missing skips, above a step that requires toybox, where it fails (fixed before push; a repeat of 1029 and 1041, the class of 228)

**Symptom.** fp-reviewer, on this branch, before push. `25134a51` set `PLEIADES_TEST_REQUIRE: toybox` on the containers
step, and the comments above the download cache steps still said the test skips when the file is neither cached nor
fetchable.

**Why 1029 and 1041 did not prevent it.** Their rule, reread each sentence the branch added against the code it
describes, is still checked only by review. A comment written one commit before the behavior under it changed was not
reread.

**Fix.** `a971dc8d` rewords both: the test skips in a run that does not require the need and fails in one that does,
and the step below requires toybox.

**Lesson.** As 1041: before review, reread each sentence the branch added against the code it describes, including
comments in workflow files.

## 1053. The UI conformance suite's fakes were more permissive than the stores they stand for: the device fake's Save answered nil and kept nothing, its reads handed out the stored item by pointer, and the device retire and inventory delete fakes answered nil for a record that was not stored (fixed on this branch; on main since 9de3c7fe, 2026-08-11, and the inventory delete fake since 46d6f734, 2026-09-13; a repeat in kind of 261)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/ui-device-edit`, 2026-11-09, while reproducing 1044. `internal/ui/resources/harness_test.go`'s
`fakeRepository.Save` was `return nil`: it stored nothing, so an edit that wrote nothing passed every test in the
suite. Its `GetByName` returned the stored item itself, so a caller's change to that item in memory reached the fixture
with no `Save` at all, which no real store allows. `fakeRepository.Retire` and `fakeSetStore.Delete` answered nil for
any name or id, so in the suite a delete of a device or an inventory that was not stored answered 303, the success
