redirect, where the real stores return `inventory.ErrItemNotFound` and `inventory.ErrSetNotFound` (1058).

**Root cause.** The fakes were written to let each view's handler run, not to keep the stores' contract. A fake that
accepts every write and answers every lookup can only make a test pass more often than the real store would, and the
suite never read a record back from the fake after a write.

**Why 261 did not prevent it.** 261's handler tests used a stub repository that recorded any `Save` call, and its lesson
said such a path must be tested against the real repository. The fix there replaced the API handler's test, not the
other fakes of the same repository; this suite's fake predates 261 and nothing swept it.

**Fix.** `5f38ecda` and `b5c39653`. `GetByName` returns a copy rebuilt through the factory from the stored record,
version and history included (`copyItem`). `Save` stores the item, conditional on the stored version as the real
repositories are, and answers `ErrVersionConflict` on a mismatch. `Retire` and `fakeSetStore.Delete` return the real
stores' not-found errors for a record that is not stored, and `Delete` really removes. The tests that depend on them are
1044's and 1058's.

**Lesson.** A fake for a store keeps the store's contract: it copies on read, stores on save under the same version
check, and returns the store's own not-found errors. A fake more permissive than its store hides exactly the failures
the store would show (LESSONS 424).

## 1054. PATCH /inventory/devices/{name} answered 200 while ignoring name and type, so a rename or a type change stored nothing and said it had worked (fixed on this branch; on main since ea2fc4fd, 2026-08-10; a repeat of 111 and 261)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/ui-device-edit`, 2026-11-09. `deviceWriteRequest` (`internal/api/devices.go`) decodes
`name` and `type` for create and update alike, and `DeviceHandler.Update` never read either. A body changing either one
answered 200 with the record unchanged. Neither store's `Save` writes the name, and the stored type column cannot
change.

**Root cause.** One request type serves create and update, and the update path read only the fields it could apply.
Nothing refused the rest.

**Why 111 and 261 did not prevent it.** 111 was the same "accepted and ignored" shape in the UI's edit forms, and its fix,
`view.Field.Immutable`, lives in the UI's view declarations; no sweep held the API's write types to it. 261 fixed the
two fields its symptom showed, state and tags, and left the request type's other two fields unread.

**Fix.** `239aaa6b`. `Update` compares each of `name` and `type` in the body byte for byte against the stored record. A
differing value is refused with 400 naming the field. An echo of the stored value is accepted, so a client that sends
the record back with one other field changed still works. The route's description in `internal/apispec/apispec.go` says
so, and the generated OpenAPI documents were regenerated. Test, shown red on the old code:
`TestDeviceUpdate_ANameOrTypeChangeIsRefusedAndAnEchoIsAccepted` (`internal/api/devices_fixed_fields_test.go`). This is
a breaking change for a client that relied on a differing value being dropped, and its changelog fragment says so.

**Lesson.** As 111: a write path that cannot apply a field it decodes refuses a value that differs from the stored one,
rather than answering success. A request type shared by create and update needs its update half checked field by
field.

## 1055. Nine other PATCH endpoints answer success while ignoring fields their body can carry: announcements, bindings, contacts, credential types, credentials, inventories, projects, teams and templates (open: task 17; a repeat of 111, 261 and 1054)

**Symptom.** Found by a sweep of the PATCH handlers on `fix/ui-device-edit`, 2026-11-09, after 1054. Each of the nine
endpoints named in the title decodes at least one field that its update then ignores, so a request changing that field
answers success and stores nothing for it. The fields each one ignores are held in task 17 and are not listed here. The
templates endpoint's `kind`, `definition` and `inventory` are ignored on update by design (its `templateWriteDTO` doc
comment), which is the same shape whatever its reason.

**Root cause.** As 1054: a request type shared by create and update, and an update that reads only what it can apply.

**Status.** Open. Passed to task 17. When each was introduced has not been traced.

**Lesson.** Pending the fix. 1054's rule applies to each: refuse a differing value of a field the update cannot apply.

**Note 2026-11-09 (`fix/template-patch-partial`, `e82caa70`).** Templates leave this entry's list. A `kind`,
`definition` or `inventory` that differs from the stored one is now refused with 400 naming the field, and an echo is
accepted, as 1054 does for devices (1069). The entry stays open, task 17, for the other eight: announcements, bindings,
contacts, credential types, credentials, inventories, projects and teams. The sweep on that branch also found seven of
those (all but bindings), and organizations, to be full replaces, the other shape, recorded as 1075.

**Note 2026-11-09 (`fix/patch-access-partial`, `93db918f`, with `1f51e3d8` for the shared helpers).** Teams, contacts
and role bindings leave this entry's list. Each PATCH now refuses, with 400 naming the field, a value that differs from
the stored one for a field no update can change: a team's `organization`; a contact's `organization` and `team`; a
binding's `team`, `scope_type` and `scope_id`. The stored value sent back is accepted. Until then each was decoded and
ignored, so a re-point answered 200 and changed nothing. `TestAccessPatch_FixedFieldsAreRefusedUnlessEchoed`
(`internal/api/access_patch_test.go`) holds each one, and `TestAccess_BindingUpdateCannotRepointAGrant`
(`internal/api/access_test.go`) now expects 400 for a re-point. The refusal is a breaking change, and its changelog
fragment says so. The entry stays open, task 17, for five: announcements, credential types, credentials, inventories
and projects. The same branch made the four access routes partial updates (1075's note).

**Note 2026-11-09 (`fix/patch-projects-partial`, `862a5aad`).** Projects leave this entry's list. A PATCH's
`organization` was decoded and ignored, so a re-point answered 200 and changed nothing. It is now refused with 400
naming the field when it differs from the stored one, and the stored value sent back is accepted.
`TestProjectPatch_TheOrganizationIsFixed` (`internal/api/projects_patch_test.go`) holds it. The refusal is a breaking
change, and its changelog fragment says so. The same branch made the project PATCH a partial update (1075's note). The
entry stays open, task 17, for four: announcements, credential types, credentials and inventories.

**Note 2026-11-09 (`fix/patch-credentials-partial`, `7c3fed71`).** Credentials and credential types leave this entry's
list. A credential PATCH's `credential_type` and `organization`, and a credential type PATCH's `namespace` and
`organization`, were decoded and ignored, so a change answered 200 and stored nothing. Each is now refused with 400
naming the field when it differs from the stored one, and the stored value sent back is accepted.
`TestCredentialPatch_RefusesAChangedTypeOrOrganization` and
`TestCredentialTypePatch_RefusesAChangedNamespaceOrOrganization` (`internal/api`) hold it. The refusal is a breaking
change, and its changelog fragment says so. The same branch made both routes partial updates (1075's note). The entry
stays open, task 17, for two: announcements and inventories.

**Resolved 2026-11-10 (`fix/patch-inventories-announcements`, `a9d76653` for inventories, `2e2f3481` for
announcements).** The last two leave this entry's list, which closes it. Each PATCH decoded an `organization` and
ignored it, so a different organization answered 200 and changed nothing. `inventoryPatchDTO`
(`internal/api/inventories_patch.go`) and `announcementPatchDTO` (`internal/api/announcements_patch.go`), on the shared
helpers in `internal/api/patch.go`, now refuse with 400 naming the field an `organization` that differs from the stored
one, and accept the stored value sent back (0 for a system-wide announcement). Tests:
`TestInventoryPatch_RefusesWhatItCannotApply`, `TestInventoryPatch_AcceptsTheStoredOrganizationAsAnEcho`,
`TestAnnouncementPatch_RefusesWhatItCannotApply` and `TestAnnouncementPatch_AcceptsTheStoredOrganizationAsAnEcho`
(`internal/api`), red on the old handlers. The refusal is a breaking change, and its changelog fragment says so. The
same branch made both routes partial updates (1075's note).

## 1056. PATCH /templates/{id} replaces a template's editable half from the body, so a client that omits survey deletes the survey, omitting defaults, prompts or required_capabilities blanks them, and omitting allow_simultaneous writes false (open, read in code and not reproduced: task 16; on main since 5dbc35bc, 2026-08-12; a repeat in kind of 103)

**Symptom.** Found by reading on `fix/ui-device-edit`, 2026-11-09; not run. `TemplateHandler.Update`
(`internal/api/templates.go`, lines 388 to 417) checks that the template exists and then calls `h.templates.Update`
with a `launch.Template` built only from the body: `Name`, `Description`, `Defaults`, `Prompts`, `Survey`,
`AllowSimultaneous` and `RequiredCaps`. A field the body leaves out arrives as its zero value. Read, that deletes a
survey's questions, blanks the defaults, prompts and required capabilities, and writes `allow_simultaneous: false`. The
method's own doc comment says it "replaces a template's editable half", behind a route documented as PATCH. If the
reading holds, an ordinary partial PATCH loses data.

**Why 103 did not prevent it.** 103's fix landed in the same commit, `5dbc35bc`. It turned the teams' and inventories'
membership lists into pointers, and its lesson (LESSONS 98) says PATCH means partial and a field whose absence differs
from its emptiness needs three states. The fix and the rule were applied to the list fields its symptom showed; the
template handler, written beside them, takes plain values and a map, and nothing held every PATCH handler to the rule.

**Status.** Open, unverified (task 16). The next step is a test that seeds a template with a survey, defaults and
`allow_simultaneous: true`, sends a PATCH naming only its description through the real router and store, and reads the
template back.

**Lesson.** Pending the fix. LESSONS 98 applies to every field of a PATCH body, not only to lists.

**Resolved 2026-11-09 (fixed on `fix/template-patch-partial`, `e82caa70`, with `67c752aa` for the route text).
Reproduced, and worse than read.** Run through the real router over the ent store on SQLite, `PATCH {"name":
"renamed"}` on a full template answered 200 and erased the description, the defaults `{forks: 5, limit: edge-*}`, the
prompts `[limit forks]` and the required capabilities `[ssh apt]`. It set `allow_simultaneous` from true to false, and
it deleted both survey questions and set the survey's `enabled` to false. A PATCH without `name` was refused with 400 "a
template needs a name", so no real partial PATCH could succeed at all. The full replace also hid a check: a stored
default that the kind no longer declares was wiped by the good data the body carried, so it was never refused.

**Fix.** `TemplateHandler.Update` decodes `templatePatchDTO` (`internal/api/templates_patch.go`), which tracks presence
with one pointer per field, as `deviceWriteRequest` and `scheduleWriteDTO` do. It folds the fields the body names over
the stored template and hands the merged template to the store, which validates it whole, so a kept default the kind
no longer declares is now refused. The survey is partial in its own right: `enabled` and `questions` are each kept when
left out, and a survey is cleared with `{"enabled": false, "questions": []}`. Other fields are cleared per field with
`""`, `{}` or `[]`. A JSON `null` on one of the template's own fields, or on `survey.enabled` or `survey.questions`, is
refused with 400 naming the field; a null inside a question decodes as a create decodes it. The strict decode is
repeated inside the custom unmarshalers, since `decodeJSON`'s `DisallowUnknownFields` does not reach into one, so an
unknown key is still a malformed body. This matches AWX, whose PATCH is partial. Tests, shown red on the old handler:
`TestTemplateAPI_PatchKeepsEveryFieldItDoesNotName`, `TestTemplateAPI_PatchClearsAFieldSentEmpty`,
`TestTemplateAPI_PatchRefusesNull`, `TestTemplateAPI_PatchRefusesABodyThatIsNotAnObjectOfKnownFields` and
`TestTemplateAPI_PatchValidatesTheMergedTemplate` (`internal/api/templates_patch_test.go`). The refusal of a null is a
breaking change, and its changelog fragment says so. The same branch refuses a changed kind, definition or inventory
(1069) and two store bounds that answered 500 (1070, 1071).

**Limits, unchanged.** Concurrent PATCHes are last-writer-wins: there is no version check, so of two at once the second
covers the first for every field. A template edit does not re-run a schedule's Preflight. Eight other PATCH handlers are
full replaces in the same way (1075, open).

**Lesson.** As LESSONS 98, for every field of a PATCH body: track presence per field and fold the body over the stored
record, and validate the merged record, not only the fields the body names.

## 1057. TestUI_FullCRUDRoundTrip's doc comment said it drove create, read, edit and delete through the rendered pages, and the test had no edit step (fixed on this branch; on main since 9de3c7fe, 2026-08-11; the class of 228, 1029 and 1041)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/ui-device-edit`, 2026-11-09, while resolving 1044. `tests/e2e/ui_test.go`'s
`TestUI_FullCRUDRoundTrip` created a device, read it back and retired it. Its doc comment named an edit as well. The one
end-to-end test of the UI's writes against real PostgreSQL therefore never edited anything, and a reader of its comment
had no reason to look for 1044 there.

**Root cause.** The comment named the steps the test was meant to have, not the steps it had.

**Why 228, 1029 and 1041 did not prevent it.** Their rule is to reread each sentence a branch adds against the code it
describes before review. This sentence was old, and no check reads a test's doc comment against its body.

**Fix.** `7b958c25`. The test now opens the device's edit form, posts new tags with that form's own CSRF token, expects
303, and reads the tags back from the detail page. It passes against real PostgreSQL and fails against the old view.

**Lesson.** A test's doc comment that lists the steps it covers is coverage a reader trusts. Read it against the test's
body as a claim, as 1029 and 1041 say of any other text.

## 1058. An edit or a delete of a record that was not stored answered 500 on every writable UI view, as though the server were broken (fixed on this branch; on main since 9de3c7fe, 2026-08-11)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/ui-device-edit`, 2026-11-09, while writing 1044's tests. The UI handler
(`internal/ui/web/resources.go`) answered every error from a view's `Update` or `Delete` with `serverError`, so editing
or deleting a record someone else had removed answered 500 on all twelve writable views. Credentials and templates
answered 400 on the edit instead, because their edit forms build their fields from the stored record and failed there.
In the conformance suite, a delete of a missing device or inventory answered 303, because the fakes answered nil (1053).

**Root cause.** The handler had no way to tell "not stored" from a fault. Each write port returned its store's own
not-found error, and the handler imports no store, so it could not test for any of them.

**Earlier entries.** A search of the index for a missing record answered as a server fault, by symptom and by cause,
found no earlier entry.

**Fix.** `c63f7e1f` and `b5c39653`. `view.ErrNotFound` and `view.WrapNotFound(err, storeNotFound)`
(`internal/ui/view/bind.go`): each of the twelve writable views (contacts, credentials, credential types, devices,
grants, inventories, organizations, projects, schedules, teams, templates and users) wraps its store's not-found sentinel,
and the handler's update, delete and form-resolving paths answer it with 404, as the edit form for an unreadable record
already did. Tests, shown red on the old code: `TestViewConformance_AMissingRecordIsNotFound`
(`internal/ui/resources/missing_record_test.go`), which also fails if the set of writable views drifts from the set it
checks; `TestWrapNotFound` (`internal/ui/view/wrapnotfound_test.go`); and `TestEditingAMissingDeviceIsNotFound`
(`internal/ui/resources/devices/edit_test.go`). The review checked that no other error maps to 404 and that the new 404
gives no signal of a record's existence across organizations.

**Lesson.** A handler that imports no store needs one sentinel of its own for "not stored", which each port wraps, or
every missing record reads as a server fault. Test it over the whole set of views, so a view added later cannot skip it.

## 1059. About 30 hand-kept lists of each command's bool flags in cmd/pleiades duplicated its FlagSet, and run's list left out --fail-on-rescue, so in run, adhoc and rollback that flag took the next argument as its value (fixed on this branch; the gap on main since c9824c1f, 2026-10-20, and the lists since 90cdb0c7, 2026-08-05; a repeat of 50; the class of LESSONS 114 and 273)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, 2026-11-09. `pleiades run --fail-on-rescue runbooks/x.yaml` read
`runbooks/x.yaml` as the value of `--fail-on-rescue` and then found no runbook. The same held for `adhoc` and
`rollback`, which shared run's flags (`addRunFlags`) and its list.

**Root cause.** The shared splitter (`splitPositional` and `splitPositionals`, `cmd/pleiades/addhost.go`) took a
`map[string]bool` naming the flags that take no value. Each command kept its own map beside its FlagSet, about 30 of
them, and nothing held a map equal to its FlagSet. `runBoolFlags` (`cmd/pleiades/run.go`) named `verbose`, `v`,
`persist-connections` and `json`. `--fail-on-rescue` was added to `addRunFlags` in `c9824c1f` and never to the map. A
check of every other map against its FlagSet found no other drift.

**Earlier entries.** The splitter exists because of 4 (stdlib `flag` stops at the first positional). 50 found it
swallowing a value after a bool flag, and its fix added the hand-kept lists. 598 found an unknown flag swallowing the
positional, and 663 a lone `-` read as a flag. All four are the same splitter guessing what a token is.

**Why 50 did not prevent it.** 50's fix was this defect's means: it kept the splitter's guess and gave each caller a
list to correct it, a second copy of what the FlagSet already knows. LESSONS 114 and 273 say a hand-kept list beside
the truth drifts and a guard reads the property the list stands for; nothing read the FlagSet here.

**Fix.** `71614896`. `parseArgs`, `parseOneArg` and `parseCheckedArgs` (`cmd/pleiades/args.go`) take the command's
FlagSet and ask each flag's Value for `IsBoolFlag`, as the flag package does, so `fs.Bool`, `fs.BoolVar`, `fs.BoolFunc`
and any bool `flag.Value` count. Every hand map is removed. Tests, shown red: `TestEveryCommandSplitsItsOwnBoolFlags`
(`cmd/pleiades/args_test.go`) drives every splitting command through its real FlagSet with each bool flag before the
positionals (and after them since `e09aba0b`); `TestNoCommandPassesAHandKeptBoolFlagList` (`cmd/pleiades/args_guard_test.go`) fails on a call
passing `args` beside a non-empty `map[string]bool`; and `TestEverySplittingCommandIsInTheTable` follows the package's
call graph and fails on a function that calls the parser and that no command in the test's table reaches.

**Review.** A review of the branch proposed replacing the splitter with spf13/pflag. That would change the syntax the
CLI accepts: pflag reads `-json` as the shorthands `-j -s -o -n`. Its named edge cases, `-vxf` and `--set arg=-value`,
were probed against a copy of the splitter and stdlib `flag`, and both already behaved correctly. The real gaps were
1060 and 598's open half. LESSONS 50, 392 and 419 already say to check a review's remedy and claims before acting.

**Lesson.** As 114 and 273: when one value already says what a list would, read that value. A splitter reads which
flags are boolean from the FlagSet it splits for.

## 1060. "--" was read as a value flag named "", so it swallowed the next argument instead of ending the flags (fixed on this branch; on main since 57138643, 2026-08-04; a repeat of 663)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, 2026-11-09. `pleiades remove-host -- -web1` passed `["--", "-web1"]`
to the FlagSet, so a command that read only the positionals never saw `-web1`. The flag package ends the flags at
`--`; the splitter did not.

**Root cause.** The splitter read any token starting with `-` as a flag, and a flag it did not know as boolean took the
next token. `--` starts with `-`, and its name is empty.

**Why 663 did not prevent it.** 663's fix made a lone `-` a positional. Its lesson listed `--` among the word shapes a
hand-written splitter is tested against, and no test was written for it.

**Fix.** `90a0473b`. `splitArgs` (`cmd/pleiades/args.go`) drops `--` and returns every token after it as a positional,
so `fs.Parse` always consumes all of the flag tokens. The leftover-argument checks in remove-host, remove-credential,
add-secret, validate and forge migrate-playbook, and doc's append of `fs.Args`, could no longer fire and are removed.
Tests, shown red: the `--` cases of `TestSplitArgs_ReadsBoolFlagsFromTheFlagSet` (`cmd/pleiades/args_test.go`), and
`TestEveryCommandSplitsItsOwnBoolFlags`, which gives each command's last positional after `--` with a leading `-`.

**Lesson.** As 663: a word shape a lesson names gets its test in the same change.

## 1061. import awx-credential-types read its export through fs.Arg(0) with stdlib ordering, so a flag after the export (x.json --quiet) was counted as a second argument and failed with a usage error (fixed on this branch; on main since b32b5eb0, 2026-08-14; a repeat of 4)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, 2026-11-09. `pleiades import awx-credential-types export.json --quiet`
stopped parsing at `export.json`, left `--quiet` as an argument, and failed with a usage error. Every other command
with a positional accepts flags after it.

**Root cause.** The command was written after 4's fix with plain `fs.Parse(args)` and `fs.Arg(0)`, which stop at the
first positional.

**Why 4 did not prevent it.** 4's fix was a splitter for add-host. A command written later had to choose to call it,
and nothing found one that did not.

**Fix.** `e09aba0b`. The command takes its argument through `parseArgs` and is in the test's command table
(`splitCommands`). `TestEveryCommandSplitsItsOwnBoolFlags` now also places each bool flag after the positionals. Its
`--help` and `-h` are pinned in the help golden (1062) and unchanged. One output changed on purpose: `--help` after the
export now prints the flags, as `add-host web1 --help` does, where it printed the usage error.

**Limit.** `TestEverySplittingCommandIsInTheTable` finds functions that call the shared parser. A new command that
never calls it, and reads its positional through `fs.Arg`, is not found by that test.

**Lesson.** As 4: run each command with a flag after its positional. A shared parser that a command must choose to
call is held by a test over every command, not by the parser.

## 1062. The first version of the parser changed --help output for every command, adding the flag package's "Usage of X:" list, against the owner's decision of 2026-10-22 that a bare --help stays as designed (fixed before push)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, 2026-11-09, before push. Parsing the flags before counting the
positionals (598's lesson) sent a bare `--help` to the flag package, so add-host, adhoc, rollback and the others
printed its "Usage of" list of flags instead of their own usage line. A help request after the positionals printed the
usage line too. A golden generated from origin/main's own code failed 47 lines against this version.

**Root cause.** The old splitter checked the positional count before the flags parsed, and that ordering was what
produced each command's help answer. Moving the flag parse first fixed 598 and changed help as a side effect. No test
pinned the help text, so nothing showed it.

**Earlier entries.** A search by symptom found 562 and 648, which fixed help's exit status. None covers output changed
as a side effect of a shared change.

**Fix.** `18c3bf1f`. `parseCheckedArgs` (`cmd/pleiades/args.go`) takes a command's positional check, and for a help
request alone runs it before the flags parse, as the old splitter did. Every other flag error still comes before the
positional count. `TestHelpOutputIsUnchanged` (`cmd/pleiades/help_golden_test.go`) runs 95 command lines (every
command's `--help` and `-h`, nested commands, and help after positionals) through the CLI's own `run` and compares exit
status, stdout and stderr byte for byte with `cmd/pleiades/testdata/help_golden.json`, which was written by running
origin/main's `cmd/pleiades`.

**Lesson.** Before changing code every command shares, pin each command's output from the base branch's own code, so
each difference is one someone decided (LESSONS 425).

## 1063. The first quoting of upstream names fixed only Reconcile's own messages; the inner errors it wraps (the Save path's version conflict and write errors, factory.go, create.go) still carried the name raw (fixed before push; LESSONS 244)

**Symptom.** Found by fp-reviewer on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, 2026-11-09, before push. The branch's first fix for 1043
quoted the name in `syncplugin.Reconcile`'s own messages. Several of those wrap an inner error from the inventory
package that names the same device with `%s`: the Save path's version conflict and write errors,
`internal/inventory/factory.go` line 52, and `internal/inventory/create.go` lines 44 and 48. So a newline in a name
could still forge a line of stderr when a later sync hit a save conflict.

**Root cause.** The fix was applied to the messages the entry named, not to every error on the path from the name to
the print.

**Why LESSONS 244 did not prevent it.** 244 says to check the sibling path of a guarded one. Here the sibling was the
wrapped error inside the guarded one, and the first fix did not follow the wrap.

**Fix.** `23d89779`. Every error in `internal/inventory` and `internal/inventory/record` that names a device or carries
its ID uses `%q`: the file and ent repositories' get, create, save, retire and remove errors, the read-only repository's
refusals, the factory, group variables and discovery rules. Tests, shown red: `TestReconcile_QuotesTheUpstreamNameInEveryError`
(`internal/inventory/syncplugin/reconcile_quoting_test.go`) stops Reconcile at each of its eight naming steps over a
real file repository and asserts the error holds the name quoted and no newline; `TestRun_QuotesAnUpstreamNameInAFailedSave`
(`cmd/pleiades/cli_error_escape_test.go`) syncs a crafted name into a read-only project so the file repository's save
fails, and asserts no line of stderr begins with the forged text.

**Lesson.** As 244: when an error is made safe, follow every error it wraps to where that one is built.

## 1064. The first escape of CLI errors used termsafe.Escape at the print site only, which keeps newlines, so a device name holding a newline could still start a forged "pleiades:" line on stderr (fixed before push; the class of 1036)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, 2026-11-09, before push. `289fbbdf` printed every command error
through `termsafe.Escape`. That escapes ANSI sequences and direction overrides, and by design keeps tab and newline so
an error of several lines still reads as lines. A sync source naming a device `sw2` followed by a newline and
`pleiades: approved` still produced a stderr line that read like the CLI's own.

**Root cause.** The print site cannot tell a newline the program wrote from one a remote system wrote. `EscapeLine`,
which escapes newlines too, would break every multi-line error. Only the place that builds the error knows which part
is a remote name.

**Why 1036 did not prevent it.** 1036 printed a name with `strconv.Quote` and a reason with `EscapeLine`, each at the
place it was printed, where the printer knew what each value was. An error's text reaches `main` as one string, and the
first fix escaped it there with the function that keeps lines.

**Fix.** `23d89779`, with 1063's: each name or ID is quoted with `%q` where the error is built, and `printError`'s
escape stays as the second layer. `TestRun_EscapesAnUpstreamNameInACommandsError` and
`TestRun_QuotesAnUpstreamNameInAFailedSave` (`cmd/pleiades/cli_error_escape_test.go`) sync a name holding a newline and
a fake `pleiades:` line through the command line and assert no line of stderr begins with it.

**Lesson.** As 266, with one addition: escape a remote value where its boundaries are known. A print site that sees one
joined string can stop terminal sequences but cannot stop a forged line.

## 1065. printError's escape was untested: with names quoted at the source, removing it changed nothing in any test (fixed before push; a repeat of 1016 and 1039; LESSONS 135)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, 2026-11-09, before push. Once 1063 and 1064 quoted every name where the
error is built, the CLI tests that synced a crafted name passed with `printError`'s `termsafe.Escape` removed. The
second layer had no test of its own.

**Root cause.** LESSONS 135's class: two guards in a row, so the later one hides whether the earlier one works, and
here the earlier one hid the later.

**Why 1016, 1039 and LESSONS 135 did not prevent it.** 1039's rule, make one guard fail loudly to pin the other, is
applied by hand, and it was applied here only when the mutation was tried.

**Fix.** `18c3bf1f`. `TestPrintError_EscapesWhatATerminalActsOn` (`cmd/pleiades/print_error_test.go`) calls
`printError` and `printHelpAnswer` directly with an error holding a raw ANSI escape and a raw U+202E, and asserts both
reach stderr escaped.

**Lesson.** As 135: a guard kept as a second layer gets a test that reaches it with the first layer absent.

## 1066. Three comments claimed more than the code (a test comment named the wrong test, a count said 99 where the golden held 93, and args.go said the bool test "cannot disagree" with the flags), and the table guard special-cased reviewFlags by name (fixed before push; a repeat of 571 and 1029)

**Symptom.** Found in review on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, 2026-11-09, before push. A test comment named a test other
than the one it described. A comment counted 99 command lines where the golden held 93. The `cmd/pleiades/args.go`
package comment said the bool test read from the FlagSet "cannot disagree" with the command's flags, but an undefined
`-h` is read as taking a value, so `add-host -h web1` takes `web1` as its value. `TestEverySplittingCommandIsInTheTable`
also accepted `reviewFlags` through a line naming that one helper and its three callers.

**Root cause.** Each sentence was written from intent, not reread against the code. The guard's special case was
written against the one helper that failed it (LESSONS 114).

**Why 571 and 1029 did not prevent it.** Their rule, reread each sentence a branch adds against the code before review,
is applied by hand, and it was applied here in review rather than before it.

**Fix.** `18c3bf1f`. The comments were corrected. The package comment now says how `-h` and `-help` differ from the
flag package and why help output is unchanged anyway. The guard follows the package's call graph, so any helper a
command in the table reaches is covered, with no name written in.

**Lesson.** As 571 and 1029, and as LESSONS 114 for the guard: state a guard's rule as a predicate, not a list of the
cases that failed it.

## 1067. A writer's wait loop, while pgrep -f 'monitor.py run'; do sleep N; done, never ended, because pgrep -f matched the loop's own bash -c command line; it ran 33 minutes after the gate ended (open, as 689 is: no guard catches a self-matching pgrep -f; a repeat of 153 and 689)

**Symptom.** 2026-11-09, on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`. A writing agent told to pause while a gate ran waited with
`while pgrep -f 'monitor.py run'; do sleep N; done`. The loop kept running 33 minutes after the gate had ended. A
tooling mistake, not a product defect.

**Root cause.** `pgrep -f` matches whole command lines, and the shell running the loop held the pattern in its own. The
brief that told writers to pause while `pgrep -f 'monitor.py run'` finds a gate handed them the pattern in that form.

**Why 153 and 689 did not prevent it.** 153 found this exact loop, and its fix was a lesson only. 689 found the same
match killing an agent's shell, and is still open because the guard hook refuses `pkill -f` and `killall` and not
`pgrep -f`. The brief was written without either, and passed the hazard to every agent that followed it.

**Fix.** The bracket form, `pgrep -f '[m]onitor.py run'`, which matches the real process and not a command line that
holds the bracketed text. No guard enforces it.

**Lesson.** As 153: a wait loop whose predicate can match the loop never ends. A brief that hands another agent a
command hands it that command's hazards, so write the safe form there.

## 1068. recordname.Check accepts a device name holding a control character such as a newline, so quoting each error is the only layer between a crafted name and a forged line (open: task 18)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/cli-flag-splitting`, 2026-11-09, while fixing 1043. `recordname.Check`
(`internal/recordname/recordname.go`) refuses only `""`, `.` and `..`. A device name holding a newline, an escape or a
direction override is stored, from a sync source or any other create path, and every error and printer that names it
must quote it (1043, 1063, 1064).

**Root cause.** The name rule was written for addressability in a URL (1011), not for what a name may hold.

**Status.** Open, task 18: refuse such a name at creation, so the quoting on this branch becomes the second layer. When
device creation first accepted one has not been traced; `recordname.Check` is on main since `c900b43b`, 2026-11-08.

**Lesson.** Pending the fix.

**Fixed (2026-11-09, `64329eb1`, branch `fix/name-control-chars`, task 18).** `internal/recordname/shown.go` refuses a
name holding invalid UTF-8, a C0 control, DEL, a C1 control, a direction control, U+2028 or U+2029, U+00AD, U+200B,
U+2060, U+FEFF or a tag character. The control codes, line breaks and direction controls are refused through
`termsafe.CheckLine`; `hidden` adds the rest as fixed code-point ranges, none read from Go's Unicode tables, so the
answer does not change with a Go release (LESSONS 415). Only creation refuses. A device already stored under such a name
is still updated by a sync (`storedUnder`, `internal/inventory/syncplugin/reconcile.go`), still written back to a hosts file
(`refuseNewUnusable`, `internal/inventory/yaml_plugin.go`, refuses only such a name the file did not hold before), and still
replaced by a kubeconfig import with replace (`internal/api/devices_kubeconfig.go`, `7d79abf6`;
`cmd/pleiades/importkubeconfig.go`, `19c82f5c`). The quoting from 1043, 1063 and 1064 stays, as the second layer.
Evidence: `internal/recordname/recordname_shown_test.go`, `internal/inventory/syncplugin/reconcile_stored_names_test.go`,
`internal/api/devices_stored_names_test.go` and `cmd/pleiades/names_shown_test.go`. The fix's own defects are 1078,
1079 and 1080; the set it refuses is open to the owner as 1081.

**Lesson (on the fix).** A name rule covers what the name may hold as well as whether a URL can carry it, because the
name is printed wherever the record is named. A rule that tightens what may be stored runs where the value is created,
not where a stored value is read or updated, so a record made under an older rule stays reachable (LESSONS 415, 422).

## 1069. PATCH /templates/{id} answered 200 for a kind, definition or inventory that differed from the stored one, and stored nothing for it (fixed on this branch; on main since 5dbc35bc, 2026-08-12; a repeat of 111, 261 and 1054)

**Symptom.** Fixed on `fix/template-patch-partial`, 2026-11-09, while fixing 1056; 1055 had listed it. The PATCH body
decoded `kind`, `definition` and `inventory`, and the update never applied them, since the store carries all three
forward from storage. A request asking to re-point a template answered 200 and changed nothing.

**Root cause.** As 1054: one request type, `templateWriteDTO`, served create and update, and the update read only what
it could apply. Its doc comment called the ignoring deliberate. Nothing refused a value that differed.

**Why 111, 261 and 1054 did not prevent it.** It was known, not missed. 1054's fix was applied to the device endpoint
only. The sweep after it found this endpoint and eight others and passed them to task 17 as 1055, open.

**Fix.** `e82caa70`. `templatePatchDTO.fixedFieldRefusal` (`internal/api/templates_patch.go`) compares each of the three
with the stored template, the definition trimmed because it is stored trimmed. A differing value is refused with 400
naming the field. An echo of the stored value is accepted, as the device PATCH accepts one. Test, shown red on the old
handler: `TestTemplateAPI_PatchRefusesAChangeToAFixedField` (`internal/api/templates_patch_test.go`). The route's
description in `internal/apispec/template_endpoints.go` says so (`67c752aa`). A client that relied on a differing value
being dropped now gets a 400.

**Lesson.** As 1054.

## 1070. A survey question with no label answered 500 on create, PUT /templates/{id}/survey and PATCH, because the database's NotEmpty refused it while Survey.Validate did not; a label of spaces alone was accepted and stored (fixed on this branch; on main since 5dbc35bc, 2026-08-12; a repeat in kind of 974)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/template-patch-partial`, 2026-11-09. A question with an empty `label` passed
`launch.Survey.Validate` and failed at the insert, where `survey_question.label` is `NotEmpty()`
(`internal/ent/schema/survey_question.go`). Each of the three write paths answered 500 "internal error". A label of
spaces alone passed both checks and was stored, so the launch form would ask a question with nothing to read.

**Root cause.** A store constraint the validator in front of it did not mirror. The handler does not map the store's
validation error, so it reached the caller as a fault rather than as a refusal.

**Earlier entries.** A search of the index and the archive for a store bound that the layer before it does not check,
by symptom (a 500 on a write) and by cause (an ent `NotEmpty` or `MaxLen`), found 974 as the nearest: an order source
longer than its column's `MaxLen(256)` failed ent's validator inside the facts consumer. 267 and 1058 are 500s from
other causes (a foreign key, a missing record).

**Why 974 did not prevent it.** 974's fix and lesson covered one new column fed from a batch, and asked where that bound
is refused before the consumer meets it. Nothing holds a domain validator to the ent schema's validators, so the rule
never reached the API's write paths.

**Fix.** `034e4050`. `Survey.Validate` (`internal/launch/survey.go`) refuses a label that is empty or only spaces with
400, naming the question by its variable. Test, shown red on the old code:
`TestTemplateAPI_RefusesAQuestionWithNoLabelOnEveryWritePath` (`internal/api/templates_store_limits_test.go`), which
drives create, PUT /survey and PATCH. The route descriptions name the refusal (`3f9ee50f`).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 426.

## 1071. A template name over 253 bytes answered 500 on create and PATCH, because the launchable row the store copies it into is MaxLen(253) and Template.Validate had no bound (fixed on this branch; on main since b044f0c2, 2026-09-20; a sibling of 1070, a repeat in kind of 974)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/template-patch-partial`, 2026-11-09, beside 1070. The template row's `name` is `NotEmpty()`
only. The store also writes the name into the template's `launchables` row in the same transaction, and that column is
`MaxLen(253)` (`internal/ent/schema/launchable.go`). A longer name passed `Template.Validate`, failed at that insert,
and answered 500.

**Root cause.** As 1070. The bound came with the launchable row in `b044f0c2` (Phase 21's C1 seam), on a table other
than the template's own, so a reader of the template schema would not see it.

**Why 974 did not prevent it.** As for 1070.

**Fix.** `034e4050`. `launch.MaxNameBytes` is 253, and `Template.Validate` (`internal/launch/template.go`) refuses a
trimmed name longer than that, in bytes, with 400. `TestMaxNameBytes_IsTheLaunchableRowsOwnBound`
(`internal/launch/template_test.go`) calls ent's generated `launchable.NameValidator` at the bound and one past it, so
the constant cannot drift from the schema unseen. Test, shown red on the old code:
`TestTemplateAPI_RefusesANameLongerThanTheLaunchableRowHolds` (`internal/api/templates_store_limits_test.go`).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 426. A project's name has the same bound and is suspected of the same 500 (1076).

## 1072. Two of the branch's first PATCH tests passed with their protection removed, because the new label rule refused their unlabelled questions before the rule under test ran, and the survey refusal table had the same masking, seen only as a coverage drop (fixed before push; a repeat of 1016, 1039 and 1048; LESSONS 213 and 261)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/template-patch-partial`, 2026-11-09, before push. The "an unknown question field" case of
`TestTemplateAPI_PatchRefusesABodyThatIsNotAnObjectOfKnownFields` and the "a survey nobody could answer" case of
`TestTemplateAPI_PatchValidatesTheMergedTemplate` (`internal/api/templates_patch_test.go`) sent questions with no
label. Once 1070's rule existed, each body was refused for its missing label, a 400 like the one each case expected,
so each passed with the strict decode or the duplicate-variable rule removed. The survey refusal table the branch
extended with its two label cases, `TestSurvey_RefusesWhatNobodyCouldAnswerCorrectly` (`internal/launch/template_test.go`,
older than the branch), had the same masking: its questions had no labels, so every case failed on the new rule first. That showed only as a coverage drop in
`internal/launch`, from 91.5 to 90.6 percent.

**Root cause.** A new refusal that runs before older ones, and test data it refuses. The tests checked a status, or
that some error came back, rather than which rule refused.

**Why 1016, 1039, 1048 and LESSONS 261 did not prevent it.** LESSONS 261 is this rule: after adding a refusal, confirm
each negative test near it still fails for its own reason. 1016, 1039 and 1048 are the same check, a test seen to fail
with its protection removed. All are applied by hand, and here they were applied after the coverage number moved, not
when the rule was added.

**Fix.** Before push. Every question in those tests has a label, and each case asserts its own rule's message: the
malformed-body refusal for the strict decode, "both write to" for the duplicate-variable rule, and in the survey table
each case's own message.

**Lesson.** As LESSONS 261, which covers it: when a refusal is added, read every test table whose data it could refuse,
and make each case assert its own message. No new lesson.

## 1073. The first test of the fixed-field refusal sent the template's stored inventory id, so it could not see whether a changed inventory was ignored or refused (fixed before push; the class of 1016; LESSONS 213)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/template-patch-partial`, 2026-11-09, before push. The "ignored fields" case written for 1069
sent an `inventory` equal to the stored one. With the refusal removed, the body was still an accepted echo, so the case
passed either way for the inventory.

**Root cause.** The test data matched the stored value it was meant to differ from.

**Why 1016 did not prevent it.** Its rule, see the test fail with the protection removed, is applied by hand.

**Fix.** Before push. `TestTemplateAPI_PatchRefusesAChangeToAFixedField` sends a second inventory's id (`f.invB`) for the
"a different inventory" case, and a separate case checks that an echo of the stored values is accepted.

**Lesson.** As LESSONS 213.

## 1074. Text the branch wrote claimed more than the code did: that a client can send a template back as it reads it, that an empty value clears every field, that null is refused everywhere, and that inventoryWriteDTO tracks presence with a pointer per field (fixed before push; a repeat of 228, 571, 1029 and 1041)

**Symptom.** Found in review on `fix/template-patch-partial`, 2026-11-09, before push. Four claims in the branch's
comments and route text were wrong:

- that a client can send the whole record back with one field changed: a GET body carries read-only fields, which the
  strict decode refuses as unknown;
- that an empty value clears every field: an empty name is refused, and `"survey": {}` keeps the survey;
- that a null is refused everywhere: a null inside a question is accepted, read as that field's zero value;
- that `inventoryWriteDTO` tracks presence with a pointer per field, as a precedent: its name and description are plain
  strings.

**Root cause.** Each sentence was written from intent, not reread against the code.

**Why 228, 571, 1029 and 1041 did not prevent it.** Their rule, reread each sentence a branch adds against the code
before review, is applied by hand, and here it was applied in review.

**Fix.** Before push. `internal/api/templates_patch.go` cites `deviceWriteRequest` and `scheduleWriteDTO` as the
precedent, says how each field is cleared, that a name may not be blank and that `"survey": {}` keeps both survey
fields, and that the fields inside a question decode as a create decodes them. The route's description
(`internal/apispec/template_endpoints.go`) says unknown fields are refused, so a GET body cannot be sent back as it is.

**Lesson.** As 571 and 1029.

## 1075. Eight more PATCH handlers are full replaces, as 1056 was: organizations, teams, inventories, contacts, announcements, credential types, credentials and projects each write a field the body leaves out as empty (open: task 17; the class of 1056; a repeat in kind of 103)

**Symptom.** Found by a sweep of the PATCH handlers on `fix/template-patch-partial`, 2026-11-09, after 1056. No test on
this branch reproduces them. A body that leaves a field out writes that field's zero value:

- organizations blank `classification`, `change_window`, `freeze_reason`, `cost_centre`, `ticket_key` and `cmdb_id`,
  and set `frozen` to false. The review found nothing in dispatch that reads `frozen`, so this is data loss, not a lifted
  guard;
- teams, inventories, contacts, announcements and credential types blank what is left out; for inventories, a PATCH
  naming only the membership blanks the name and the description;
- credentials blank `external`, the record's secret references;
- projects set `credential` to 0, which unbinds the project's credential.

**Root cause.** As 1056: the update builds the record from the body alone, so absent reads as empty.

**Why 1056 and LESSONS 98 did not prevent it.** 1056's fix covered templates only. LESSONS 98 says a PATCH needs three
states for a field whose absence differs from its emptiness, and nothing holds every PATCH handler to it.

**Status.** Open, task 17. This is a sibling entry rather than an extension of 1055, because 1055 is the other shape: a
field the body sends is ignored, where here a field the body leaves out is erased, and the fix differs (a pointer per
field folded over the stored record, as `templatePatchDTO` does). Task 17 holds both. When each was introduced has not
been traced.

**Lesson.** Pending the fix. LESSONS 98 applies to every field of every PATCH body.

**Note 2026-11-09 (`fix/patch-access-partial`, `93db918f`, with `1f51e3d8` for the shared helpers and `7bc22e7d` for
the route text).** Organizations, teams and contacts leave this entry's list. Role bindings were a full replace too,
which the sweep's list missed: a PATCH naming only a grant's role sent its effect empty and was refused. Each of the
four routes, `PATCH /organizations|teams|contacts|bindings/{id}`, now reads the stored record and folds one pointer per
field over it (`internal/api/access_patch.go`, with the decode and refusal helpers it shares with the template PATCH in
`internal/api/patch.go`). A JSON `null` on any of a resource's own fields is refused with 400 naming the field. A field
no update can change is refused when it differs and accepted as an echo (1055's note). The merged record goes to the
unchanged store method, so the store's own checks run on what would be saved: the contact one-channel rule, the guard
on the last system-scope grant, the classification and duplicate names. The UI's edit forms call the store directly
with full records and are unchanged. Tests, shown red on the old handlers, in `internal/api/access_patch_test.go`:
`TestAccessPatch_OrganizationKeepsWhatItDoesNotName` (a PATCH naming only the name came back with every other field
empty and `frozen` false), `TestAccessPatch_OrganizationIsValidatedWhole`, `TestAccessPatch_TeamKeepsWhatItDoesNotName`,
`TestAccessPatch_ContactKeepsWhatItDoesNotName`, `TestAccessPatch_ContactIsValidatedWhole`,
`TestAccessPatch_BindingKeepsWhatItDoesNotName`, `TestAccessPatch_RefusesNull`,
`TestAccessPatch_RefusesABodyThatIsNotAnObjectOfKnownFields` and `TestAccessPatch_FixedFieldsAreRefusedUnlessEchoed`.
The refusal of a null is a breaking change, and its changelog fragment says so.

An empty PATCH `{}`, or one that only echoes fixed fields, now answers 200, writes the stored record back and records
an "updated" activity entry (`internal/access/audited_store.go`), as the template PATCH already did. That is accepted.
Concurrent PATCHes are last-writer-wins, now for the fields a body leaves out as well (1085, open).

The entry stays open, task 17, for five: inventories, announcements, credential types, credentials and projects. The
inventory and announcement write schemas the OpenAPI document now publishes (1084) still describe a full-replace body,
which is accurate until those routes are fixed.

**Note 2026-11-09 (`fix/patch-projects-partial`, `862a5aad`).** Projects leave this entry's list. The full replace did
more than the sweep listed: a PATCH that left out `credential` unbound the project (0 ran `ClearCredential`), and one
that left out `scm_type` turned a manual or archive project into git. `PATCH /projects/{id}`
(`internal/api/projects_patch.go`) now reads the stored project and folds one pointer per field over it. `"credential": 0`
unbinds explicitly. A JSON `null` on any field is refused with 400 naming it. The project as it would be saved is

`TestProjectPatch_RefusesNull`, `TestProjectPatch_RefusesABodyThatIsNotAnObjectOfKnownFields` and
`TestProjectPatch_TheOrganizationIsFixed`. The refusal of a null is a breaking change, and its changelog fragment says

showed replaced the stored one (1087). The entry stays open, task 17, for four: inventories, announcements, credential
types and credentials.

**Note 2026-11-09 (`fix/patch-credentials-partial`, `7c3fed71`, with `50319b68` for the fold under the type lock).**
Credentials and credential types leave this entry's list. The full replace did more than the sweep listed. A credential
PATCH that did not name `external` erased every external secret reference the credential held: data loss that saved

pointer per field over the stored record. The store runs the fold inside its own transaction, under the type row's

`TestCredentialPatch_KeepsWhatItDoesNotName`, `TestCredentialPatch_ReplacesExternalWholeWhenNamed`,
`TestCredentialPatch_RefusesNull`, `TestCredentialPatch_RefusesABodyThatIsNotAnObjectOfKnownFields`,
`TestCredentialPatch_IsValidatedWhole`, `TestCredentialPatch_NeverShowsASecret`,
`TestCredentialTypePatch_KeepsWhatItDoesNotName`, `TestCredentialTypePatch_ReplacesInputsAndInjectorsWhole`,
`TestCredentialTypePatch_IsValidatedWhole`, `TestCredentialTypePatch_RefusesNull` and
`TestCredentialTypePatch_RefusesABodyThatIsNotAnObjectOfKnownFields`. The refusal of a null is a breaking change, and

`PATCH /inventories/{id}` and `PATCH /announcements/{id}` now fold one pointer per field over the stored record

## 1076. Suspected: a project name over 253 bytes answers 500, as a template's did (open, suspected from reading; a sibling of 1071)

**Symptom.** Found by reading on `fix/template-patch-partial`, 2026-11-09; not run. `project.name` is `MaxLen(253)`
(`internal/ent/schema/project.go`), and a bounded search of `internal/project` and `internal/api/projects.go` found no
length check before the store. If that holds, a longer name fails ent's validator at the insert and answers 500, as
1071 did.

**Status.** Open, unverified. The next step is a test that creates and renames a project with a 254-byte name through
the real router and store.

**Lesson.** Pending. LESSONS 426 says what a fix would hold.

**Resolution 2026-11-09 (`fix/patch-projects-partial`, `6fa14dac`).** Confirmed and fixed. Proven red through the real
router and ent store: nine 500s, from four over-long creates (name, description, `scm_url`, `scm_branch`), a
127-character name of two-byte characters (254 bytes), and four full-body PATCHes. The bounds were wider than the name:
`internal/project/bounds.go` holds name 253, description 1024, `scm_url` 2048 and `scm_branch` 255 bytes, measured after
trimming, and `project.CheckLengths` refuses an over-long field with 400 naming the field before the store, on create
and PATCH. One source feeds the API's check, the UI form's `MaxLen` and the OpenAPI text (`c68a7b07`).
`TestFieldBounds_AreTheDatabasesOwn` holds the four equal to the generated ent validators, as LESSONS 426 asks. The UI
form already refused over-long values through `view.Validate`; it now reads the same bounds. Other tests:
`TestCheckLengths_NamesTheFirstFieldOverItsBound` (`internal/project`),
`TestProjects_RefuseAFieldLongerThanTheDatabaseHolds` (`internal/api`),
`TestProjectsView_RefusesAFieldLongerThanTheDatabaseHolds` (`internal/ui/resources`). The same branch refuses a NUL in
the same four fields (1092).

## 1078. Closing a create path to a crafted name broke three tests that stored the name through that path to reach an error, so every case ended "Reconcile succeeded" (fixed before push; a repeat in kind of 42; LESSONS 43)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/name-control-chars`, 2026-11-09, after rebasing onto #143. Three tests failed:
`TestReconcile_QuotesTheUpstreamNameInEveryError` (`internal/inventory/syncplugin/reconcile_quoting_test.go`), and
`TestRun_EscapesAnUpstreamNameInACommandsError` and `TestRun_QuotesAnUpstreamNameInAFailedSave`
(`cmd/pleiades/cli_error_escape_test.go`). Each stored a crafted name (a newline, an ANSI escape, a right-to-left
override) through a sync, then drove an error that names it. The new rule (1068) refuses such a name at the sync, so no
case reached its error and each ended "Reconcile succeeded". The rebase itself applied cleanly apart from
`cmd/pleiades/importkubeconfig.go`; running the affected tests afterwards is what found them.

**Root cause.** The tests used the create path as their way into the store. A rule that closes that path for the input
also closes the tests' only route to the state they assert on, and nothing ties the rule's change to the tests that
relied on the old path.

**Why 42 and LESSONS 43 did not prevent it.** 42 is this shape: a new fail-closed startup check broke an older test
that started the binary without the new variable. LESSONS 43 was written for that case, a required environment
variable and the tests that spawn the binary, so it names spawn sites and environment lists. It does not say that any
new refusal breaks every test that reached its state through the refused input, which is the general form (LESSONS 114:
a rule written against the incident's literal).

**Fix.** Before push. Steps that need a stored device seed the crafted name the way an older release could have stored
it: a hand-written `hosts.yaml`, or the inventory file renamed as text after a first sync, since `EncodeHosts` refuses
adding such a name. Steps that only create use a name the rule allows that `%q` still changes (`web1" scripted:
approved`), and each also checks that the raw name never appears beside its quoted form. The CLI test now skips on
Windows and as root for both rows, because it reaches its error through a read-only directory's save failure; that
loses the end-to-end proof there. `print_error_test.go` still covers `printError`'s escape on every platform.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 427.

## 1079. Moving a store lookup ahead of a validation, so a stored cluster under a refused name could be replaced, sent a NUL name to the database and would have answered 500 on PostgreSQL where main answered 400 (fixed before push; a repeat of 371 and 919, through the same dialect gap)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent on `fix/name-control-chars`, 2026-11-09, reasoned from 371's measurement.
To let `ImportKubeconfig` (`internal/api/devices_kubeconfig.go`) replace a cluster stored under a name the new rule
refuses, the branch moved `GetByName` ahead of `refuseUnusableName` and dropped main's
`strings.ContainsAny(req.Name, "\x00\r\n")`, there since `d5011ea7` (2026-10-14). A name holding NUL then reached the
store's query. On PostgreSQL, lib/pq sends a NUL in a text parameter and the server refuses it, so the request would
have answered 500 "internal error" with an ERROR log, where main answered 400. On SQLite the lookup just matches no row,
so the SQLite-backed tests passed.

**Root cause.** Reordering a guard and a lookup changed what the lookup is given. The removed check was doing two jobs:
refusing a name no URL can carry, and keeping a value no PostgreSQL row can hold away from the query.

**Why 371 and 919 did not prevent it.** Both say a NUL that reaches a PostgreSQL query is an error, not a miss, and both
fixed it at their own site (sign-in, the facts and journal consumers). Neither leaves a check that every lookup is
given a value its dialect can hold, and the branch's tests ran on SQLite. Here the guard existed on main and was
removed for a different reason, so nothing new was missing a guard; an old guard lost one of its jobs.

**Fix.** Before push, in `7d79abf6`. A name holding NUL is refused with the reason before the lookup, since no
PostgreSQL row can hold one, so no stored cluster can be under it. CR and LF stay allowed past that point, so a cluster
stored under a name holding one can still be replaced. `TestImportKubeconfig_RefusesANULNameBeforeTheStore`
(`internal/api/devices_kubeconfig_test.go`) uses a repository that answers a NUL as lib/pq does; written first, it
answered 500 before the fix.

**Lesson.** As 371: whether a value is legal differs by database. When a change moves a lookup ahead of a check, list
each job the check did and keep the ones the lookup still needs, here a value the production dialect can hold.

## 1080. API text said a create refuses only "." and "..", and the five device {name} routes said a name "contains a control character" where deviceName refuses only NUL, CR and LF (fixed on this branch; the {name} text on main since fda1792d, 2026-09-24, or earlier; the class of 228, 1029, 1041 and 1074)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/name-control-chars`, 2026-11-09. Two kinds of stale text in `internal/apispec/apispec.go`:

- the 400 descriptions of CreateDevice and ImportKubeconfig said a name of "." or ".." is unusable, and nothing else.
  That was true on main and became false when 1068's fix refused more;
- the 400 descriptions of the five `{name}` routes (get, facts, fact chain, delete, onboard) said "name is empty, too
  long, or contains a control character". `deviceName` (`internal/api/devices.go`) refuses only an empty, too long or
  undecodable name, or one holding NUL, CR or LF. It did the same at `fda1792d`, so that text was not true when written
  there; whether an earlier version made it true has not been traced.

**Root cause.** As 1074: route text written from intent and not reread against the code, and text that described a rule
the branch then changed.

**Why 228, 1029, 1041 and 1074 did not prevent it.** Their rule, reread each sentence against the code, is applied by
hand, and nothing compares a route's error text with the check that answers it.

**Fix.** `00db02de`. Both kinds are corrected, and `docs/reference/schemas/openapi.json` and
`internal/api/wellknown/openapi.json` regenerated.

**Lesson.** As 1029. When a change alters what a check refuses, search the route table for each route that check
answers, and reread its error text.

## 1081. The name rule refuses U+00AD, U+200B, U+2060 and U+FEFF because each shows as nothing, and passes other characters that show as nothing (fixed on fix/name-control-chars by the owner's decision of 2026-11-09: the rule reads Go's unicode tables at creation only; a sibling of 905; LESSONS 114)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent on `fix/name-control-chars`, 2026-11-09 (its finding F2); reasoned, not run.
`hidden` (`internal/recordname/shown.go`) refuses four characters by name because a reader cannot see them. Others a
reader cannot see pass: U+034F, U+115F, U+1160, U+17B4 to U+17B5, U+180E, U+2061 to U+2064, U+206A to U+206F, U+3164,
U+FFA0, U+FFF9 to U+FFFB, U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, and U+1D173 to U+1D17A. A device name holding one would print as a
different name, or as another device's name.

**Root cause.** The list was built from the characters the decided rule named, not from the property the rule exists
for. 905 is the same gap in the source check, which was closed with Unicode's Default_Ignorable property; the name rule
deliberately reads no Go Unicode table (LESSONS 415, FAILURE_PATTERNS 1003), so it cannot reuse that answer and needs the
ranges written out.

**Status.** Open, for the owner, until 2026-11-09.

**Fixed (2026-11-09, `07f25792`, branch `fix/name-control-chars`).** The owner decided the rule should name the
property, not the examples, and read it from Go's standard `unicode` tables rather than `golang.org/x/text/secure/precis`
(whose API is still marked unstable, whose `Identifier` profile refuses the ASCII space names already use, and whose
`Freeform` profile passes U+2800). `recordname.ShowsAsItself`, asked by `Check` and by `facts.ValidKey`, refuses after
`termsafe.CheckLine`: `unicode.Cc`, `Cf`, `Cs`, `Co`, `Other_Default_Ignorable_Code_Point`, `Variation_Selector`,
`Noncharacter_Code_Point`, `Zl`, `Zp`, every `Zs` but U+0020, U+2800 (the blank braille pattern, filed as a symbol), and a
name of spaces alone. A real U+FFFD stays allowed (932). The cost, owner-accepted: the zero width joiner and non-joiner and
the variation selectors are now refused, so a Persian name spelled with the non-joiner or an emoji in its color form must
be written without it (`TestCheck_RefusesTheJoinersAndSelectorsRealNamesCanHold` pins this). Reading Go's tables here is
safe for the reason LESSONS 415 gives and 1003 lacked: only a create asks the rule, so a Go upgrade can refuse a new name
and never a stored one. Checking that claim found 1083. Evidence: `internal/recordname/recordname_shown_test.go` (both
edges of every range and the neighbour kept), `internal/facts/key_names_test.go` (every code point to U+10FFFF).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 114: a guard written against the examples is not a guard against the rule. A rule may read a table a
release can grow only where nothing reading a stored value asks it; check every reference of the rule before widening.

## 1082. A test list built with rg inside a git rebase -x script came out empty, because the script's PATH had no rg, so go test -run matched no test and reported ok with "no tests to run" (open, as 374 is: nothing fails a -run that matches no test; a repeat in kind of 374)

**Symptom.** On `fix/name-control-chars`, 2026-11-09. A script run by `git rebase -x` built its `go test -run` pattern
from a list of test names made with `rg`. `rg` is on the agent's PATH, not on the PATH a script started by git gets, so
the list was empty. `go test` printed "no tests to run" and reported ok for each commit. Once noticed, each commit
touching `cmd/pleiades` (the rule commit, the import-kubeconfig fix and the tip, before the rebase onto #144) was re-run with a name
pattern and `-v`, counting the passes (75, 77 and 77 tests), and all passed.

**Root cause.** Two things that each fail silently: a command substitution whose command is not found yields an empty
string, and `go test -run` with a pattern that matches nothing is a pass.

**Why 374 did not prevent it.** 374's lesson is to read `-v` output when a new test does not appear. It is a check made
by hand, and a script reading only the exit status cannot make it.

**Status.** Open, as a practice rather than a guard. A script that builds a test list should use commands it can be
sure of (an absolute path, or `go test -list`), stop on an empty list, and treat "no tests to run" as a failure.

**Lesson.** As 374. A pass from `go test -run` proves something only when the run names the tests it ran.

## 1083. The fact history route held the {key} it was asked to read to facts.ValidKey, the rule a new fact's key is held to, so a key stored before that rule grew would answer 400 at its own address (fixed before push; a repeat of 988 and 1003)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/name-control-chars`, 2026-11-09, by listing `facts.ValidKey`'s references (gopls) before
making it ask `recordname.ShowsAsItself`. `DeviceHandler.FactHistory` (`internal/api/device_facts.go`) refused any
`{key}` `ValidKey` refused. Until then `ValidKey` added only "." and ".." to the reader's `wellFormedKey`, neither of
which a URL carries, so nothing showed. Once `ValidKey` read Go's unicode tables, a fact stored under a key holding
U+3164 (printable, so well formed) became unreadable by `GET /inventory/devices/{name}/facts/{key}`, and a Go upgrade
could have done the same to any stored key.

**Root cause.** A reader asked the creation rule. `ValidKey`'s own doc said a reader holds a stored key to
`wellFormedKey`, but `wellFormedKey` was unexported, so the route outside the package had only `ValidKey` to call.

**Why 988 and 1003 did not prevent it.** Each fixed the readers it found (the fact stores' Collection identity, the
Crawl journal's strict reader) and stated the rule; nothing lists which callers of a creation rule are readers, and a
route looking up a stored record by a caller's text is a reader that does not look like one.

**Fix.** `facts.ReadableKey`, exported, is the reader's rule (`wellFormedKey`); the route asks it. RED first:
`TestDeviceFactHistory_ReadsAKeyANewFactMayNotTake` (`internal/api/device_facts_test.go`) answered 400 before the
fix and 200 after.

**Lesson.** As LESSONS 415. When a creation rule exists, export the reader's rule beside it, so a reader outside the
package is never left with only the creation rule to call.

## 1084. Fourteen endpoints declared a request schema with no RequestContentType, so the OpenAPI document never published the body they take, and TestOpenAPIPaths_EveryDeclaredRequestSchemaIsPublished skipped each of them (fixed on this branch; on main since 5dbc35bc, 2026-08-12; a repeat of 116; LESSONS 114; the class of 1038)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent on `fix/patch-access-partial`, 2026-11-09. Ten access routes in
`internal/apispec/access_endpoints.go` (organization, team, contact, user and binding create and update) and four in
`internal/apispec/apispec.go` (inventory and announcement create and update) set `RequestSchema` and left
`RequestContentType` empty. `openAPIRequestBody` (`tools/gendocs/openapi.go`) returns nil when the content type is
empty, so none of the fourteen had a request body in `docs/reference/schemas/openapi.json` or
`internal/api/wellknown/openapi.json`. The field-level contract of those bodies existed only in Go. A client generated
from the document could not tell what to send to create an organization or edit a grant.

**Root cause.** The generator needs two fields to publish a body, and the declarations set one. The guard written for
this generator read only endpoints that set both: its loop skipped any endpoint with an empty content type or an empty
schema, so an endpoint with a schema and no content type was outside it.

**Why 116 did not prevent it.** The guard was written in `18fcb6394` (2026-08-13, Phase 22b) for this exact shape: its
doc comment names FAILURE_PATTERNS 116, after more than twenty endpoints declared a content type and a schema that the
generator never emitted. It was written against that incident's literal, both fields declared and nothing emitted,
rather than against its own name, every declared schema published (LESSONS 114). The fourteen schemas date from
`5dbc35bc`, one day before the guard, so the guard never covered them. As in 1038, the test was narrower than its
name, and nothing checked the test against the declarations it skipped.

**Fix.** `3a898605`. The guard now fails an endpoint that declares a schema with no content type; it failed with
exactly these fourteen before the fix. Each of the fourteen sets `application/json`, and both OpenAPI documents were
regenerated. The inventory and announcement write schemas now published describe a full-replace body, which is what
those routes still do (1075, open).

The first `make pr-check` on the branch (7c8b26c0) stopped at `schema-compat`: publishing a body the v0.3.0 document did
not describe reads as `request-body-added-required` on ten of the routes, though each always required its body. The
writer had run gendocs and the apispec tests but not `make schema-compat`. Fixed by
`changelog/openapi-request-bodies.breaking.md`, naming each token, folded into the commit that published the bodies.

**Lesson.** As LESSONS 114: a guard that skips an input skips it on purpose, so each `continue` in a guard's loop is a
claim to check against its name. A skip for a half-made declaration hides the defect the guard exists to find.

## 1085. A partial PATCH reads the stored record, folds the body over it and writes every column, with no compare-and-swap, so a PATCH naming only a name that races an edit setting frozen writes frozen back to false (open; low severity while nothing reads frozen; a repeat in kind of 45 and 135)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent on `fix/patch-access-partial`, 2026-11-09, by reading; not run. The access
PATCH handlers (`internal/api/access_patch.go`) read the stored record, apply the fields the body names and send the
whole merged record to the store. `entStore.UpdateOrganization` (`internal/access/ent_store.go`) sets every column. A
PATCH `{"name":"x"}` that reads the record before a UI edit, or a second PATCH, sets `frozen: true` and writes after it
puts `frozen=false` back, with the old `freeze_reason` and `ticket_key`. The same holds for every partial PATCH: teams,
contacts, bindings, and templates since 1056's fix.

**Root cause.** A read-modify-write with no version check. A field the body did not name is written from a read that
another writer may have overtaken. Before the partial PATCH, a body's empty fields were written whatever the stored
record held, which lost more; the partial PATCH narrowed the loss to a race, and did not close it.

**Why 45 and 135 did not prevent it.** 45 fixed one write, the key rotation's, with the compare-and-swap
`entRepository.Save` already used for devices; 135 fixed a provenance file. Neither made a version check a property of
every store write. The access and template stores have no version column, and the template PATCH's own spec text and
changelog already said "last-writer-wins" as a limit, without a pattern to track it.

**Status.** Open. Low severity today: the review found no dispatcher, scheduler or guard that reads `frozen` or the
other change-management fields, so a lost freeze lifts nothing that is enforced. That changes once anything enforces
a freeze. The code (`internal/api/access_patch.go`), the route text (`internal/apispec/access_endpoints.go`) and the
changelog say last-writer-wins. Two fixes were named: a field mask in the store, so an update writes only the fields
the body named, or a precondition on `updated_at` (every one of these schemas has it, through `TimestampMixin`), so a
write over a newer record is refused.

**Lesson.** Pending the fix. A partial update that writes the whole record is a read-modify-write, and it needs a
version check or a field mask, as a store write did in 45.

**Note 2026-11-09 (`fix/patch-credentials-partial`, `50319b68`).** Credentials and credential types no longer read
before they write. Their PATCH and PUT handlers, and the web UI's credential and credential type forms and input and
injector controls, hand the store a fold, and the store runs it over the record it reads under the type row's write
lock, inside the write's own transaction (`UpdateCredentialWith`, `UpdateTypeWith`). So a field the body does not name
is written from the record as it stands under that lock, not from an earlier read. On these routes the race was not
low severity: a stale read written back restored a secret reference a type edit had deleted (1100). Two concurrent
PATCHes naming the same field are still last-writer-wins, as the changelog says. The entry stays open for the other
partial PATCHes: organizations, teams, contacts, bindings, templates and projects.

**Note 2026-11-10 (`fix/patch-inventories-announcements`, `a74957af`).** The inventory and announcement PATCH routes no
longer read before they write: the store runs the body's fold over the row it reads under a lock, inside the write's
transaction (1112). On the inventory route the race was not low severity either, since an inventory is a grant surface
(97) and a lost write could undo a device's removal. Two gaps stay, and the entry stays open for them as well as for
the routes listed above. The web UI's inventory edit form (`internal/ui/resources/inventories/inventories.go`, the
`writer.Update` method) still calls `Update` with a full submission rendered earlier, so a stale form puts back a
member a PATCH removed after the form was drawn. And an API PATCH naming a full member list built from a stale GET does
the same, since a named list replaces the stored one whole. Neither has a version token (no `If-Match`, no version
column). Whether to add one is the owner's decision. The changelog and the route text say that a named list replaces
the stored one and that there is no version check (1115).

**Note 2026-11-10 (`feat/inventory-version`, not yet committed).** Both inventory gaps the note above names are
closed on this branch. A PATCH naming a full member list needs an `If-Match` holding the inventory's current ETag, judged
under the row lock (1140), and the web UI's inventory edit form carries what it was opened with and merges each element
under the row lock (1141). The entry stays open for the other partial PATCHes listed above, and for two more whole-list
writes from an earlier read with no version: team membership (`PATCH /teams/{id}`'s `users`, and the UI teams form's
users lookup) and the UI template form's credentials lookup.

## 1086. A code-writing agent ran git stash push --keep-index and git stash pop to test a commit alone, which LESSONS 423 forbids, because the rule was in the records, the handoff and memory but not in the agent's brief (open: nothing holds an agent's brief to the rule; nothing was lost; a repeat of 1042)

**Symptom.** On `fix/patch-access-partial`, 2026-11-09. To test one commit by itself, a code-writing agent set its
other changes aside with `git stash push --keep-index` and restored them with `git stash pop`. That is the command
pair 1042 lost the owner's stash with. This time the stash list held nothing else, and it was checked empty after, so
nothing was lost. The follow-up brief forbade git stash, and the agent then tested the commit with `git rebase -x`.

**Root cause.** The rule reached the main thread and never reached the agent. LESSONS 423, the handoff and the
session's memory each say not to use git stash. A code-writing agent is briefed by the main thread and reads none of
them. The first brief did not say it.

**Why 1042 and LESSONS 423 did not prevent it.** Their fix was a rule for agents, written where the main thread reads
it. 1042 itself said a handoff note protects a stash only from a reader, not from a command; the same holds for the
rule, which protects the stash list only from an agent that is told it.

**Status.** Open. Each brief to a code-writing agent now has to name the rule, and nothing checks that it does. A
guard that refuses `git stash` in an agent's shell would hold it whatever the brief says.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 423, with its note of 2026-11-09: a brief to a code-writing agent states the rule, and names the
way to test a commit alone (`git rebase -x`, or a copy set aside and restored with `git checkout`).

## 1087. Sending back the scm_url a project's GET showed replaced the stored URL with its redacted form, through PATCH /projects/{id} and through the UI's edit form, which prefills that text (fixed on this branch; on main; a repeat in kind of 580)

**Symptom.** Found by the writer on `fix/patch-projects-partial`, 2026-11-09. `GET /projects/{id}`, the list and the UI
show a stored `scm_url` that may carry a credential through `project.RedactedSourceURL`: the userinfo replaced, or the
URL withheld whole. The UI's edit form prefills its URL control with that same text, and a client that edits a project
by reading it, changing one field and sending the body back sends it too. The write took the text it was sent as the
new URL. For a manual or archive project, whose source main's store did not check (1088), the redacted text was saved
and the real URL was lost.

**Root cause.** The read path redacts, and the write path did not know the redacted form when it came back. As in 580,
nothing asked whether the value being written was a masked copy of the stored one.

**Why 580 did not prevent it.** 580's fix is `net.frr.config` refusing its own mask's marker, a rule for one method's
data. The project redaction came later, in 458's fix (`f5512ff5`, 2026-10-14), as a read rule with no write rule
beside it, and nothing ties a redacting read to the write that takes its output back.

**Shown red first.** The first versions of `TestProjectPatch_AnEchoedRedactedURLNeverReplacesTheStoredOne` (real router and ent store) and `TestProjectsView_SavingTheEditFormNeverReplacesAStoredURLItShowsRedacted` (the UI form), then named for keeping the stored URL, found it replaced by `https://redacted@example.invalid/legacy.git`. Once 1088 refused a stored credential URL on every save, both were rewritten to expect that refusal with the stored URL unchanged.

**Fix.** `862a5aad` (the API) and `d8f39e06` (the UI form). `project.KeepEchoedSourceURL`
(`internal/project/secret_url.go`): a submitted value equal to `RedactedSourceURL(stored)` keeps the stored URL; any
other value is the new URL and goes through the source checks. The project as it would be saved is still checked
whole, so a stored URL that carries a credential is kept by the echo and then refused on save until it is changed
(1088). Tests: `TestKeepEchoedSourceURL_KeepsTheStoredURLOnlyForWhatItRedactsTo` (`internal/project`),
