  (`job:read`, `template:read`; rollback is 1135), `launch_template` and `check_template` (`template:read`),
  `onboard_device`, `grant_capability` and `revoke_capability` (`inventory:read`), `set_template_credentials`
  (`credential:read`, `template:read`, so three scopes with its write scope) and `import_kubeconfig` (`inventory:write`,
  `inventory:read`; 1138). Review on the branch added `create_project` and `update_project` (`credential:read`; 1137) and
  the schedule path (1136).
- Each route's reads are an explicit table, `requiredReads` in `internal/apispec/patch_scopes_test.go`.
  `TestAlsoScopes_EveryDeclaringRouteRefusesAMissingScope` (`internal/api/patch_scopes_test.go`) drops each declared
  scope in turn for all 36 routes that declare one, and checks the `Allow` header for the three-scope `PUT`.
  `TestAffordances_RequireEveryFurtherScope` (`internal/ui/web/also_scopes_internal_test.go`) was measured red when the
  loop read only the first position: Relaunch was offered without `template:read`.
- `changelog/action-routes-need-read-scopes.breaking.md` names the change.

**Known limits, updated.** A route now records one authorization Decision per scope, so a three-scope route records
three, still with no route or request id to tie them together. `auth.AllScopes()` (`internal/auth/rolescopes.go`) still
leaves out `ScopeAccessRead`, `ScopeSettingsRead` and `ScopeSettingsWrite`.

**Still open.** Creates and forms that name another resource without its read scope: 1139.

## 1120. The inventory member check answers 400 for an id that does not exist, 403 for another organization's and 200 for one's own, so a token holding inventory:write can learn which device and group ids exist (open: owner decision; on main as 409, 403 and 200; reasoned, not run as an oracle test; the class of 1096)

**Symptom.** Reasoned on `fix/patch-inventories-announcements`, 2026-11-10. Ids are sequential. A caller holding
`inventory:write` can PATCH its own inventory's member list with a guessed id and read the answer: 400 "does not
exist" (1111's `ErrUnknownMember`), 403 for a member in another organization, 200 for its own. On main the first case
answered 409 (the constraint error read as a taken name), so the oracle was there before this branch; the branch
changed its wording, not its substance.

**Root cause.** Two refusals that tell different callers different things about records they may not read.

**Status.** Open, for the owner: whether to merge "does not exist" and "another organization's" into one 400.
Per-organization authorization (98's notes) would narrow who can ask.

**Lesson.** Pending the decision. As 1096: a refusal tells a caller nothing about a record they could not read.

**Resolution, in part, 2026-11-10 (`fix/inventory-member-checks`, `a78ffdf4`).** Owner decision 2026-11-10: merge the
two answers. `POST /inventories` and `PATCH /inventories/{id}` now answer a group or device of another organization (or
a group holding one) with the same 400 and text as one that does not exist: "one or more of the groups or devices do
not exist or cannot be added to this inventory" (`memberRefusal`, `internal/api/inventories.go`). `checkMembers` runs
every check before it returns and joins both sentinels (`errors.Join`), so the order of the checks does not show which
failed first; the queries' cost still differs a little with what they match. Measured red, then green:
`TestInventoryMembers_ForeignAnswersLikeUnknown` (`internal/api/inventories_patch_test.go`). The OpenAPI document drops
the 403.

**Still open.** The claim-refuter agent refuted that the probe is closed. Without per-organization authorization (98)
a caller holding `inventory:write` can still map ids and their owners:
- `POST /inventories` naming another organization answers 201 for a member that organization owns and 400 otherwise.
- `PATCH /inventories/{id}` with `{}` on any inventory returns its member ids (the class of 1119).
- The GET routes are not filtered by organization.
- The UI's membership chooser (`ListMembers`) lists every organization's devices and groups.
- The UI answers an unknown member 422 (`view.Validate`) and a foreign one 500 (the store's refusal; 1121), so the UI
  still tells the two apart.
- `POST /inventory/kubeconfig-imports` with replace answers 409 "belongs to another organization" for a cluster name.

The changelog fragment (`changelog/inventory-member-one-refusal.breaking.md`) says the change removes the difference
between the two answers only, and does not make ids private.

**See also, 2026-11-10.** 1139 records the wider class found on `fix/action-route-read-scopes`: creates, forms and
refusals across the API and the UI that name, list or count another store's records to a caller without its read scope,
existence answers for referenced ids among them. It is a separate entry because most of it is about read scopes, not
member ids.

## 1121. The web UI answers every inventory store refusal to an edit with a 500, as though the server were broken (open; on main; reasoned, not run; the class of 1058)

**Symptom.** Reasoned on `fix/patch-inventories-announcements`, 2026-11-10, from `internal/ui/web/resources.go`'s update
handler. The handler turns `view.ErrNotFound` into a 404 and any other error from the view's `Update` into a server
error page. The inventory view's writer (`internal/ui/resources/inventories/inventories.go`) passes the store's errors
through unmapped, so a store refusal the form's own checks do not catch first (a taken name, an unknown member, a NUL)
renders as a 500, not as a refusal beside the field. The create path was not traced. The branch's new typed errors (1111, 1113) make the mapping possible; the branch did not
add it.

**Root cause.** As 1058: the UI's generic handler knows one store error, not found, and the view maps nothing else.

**Status.** Open.

**Lesson.** Pending the fix. As 1058: a refusal the caller can correct is shown as one, beside the field it concerns.

**Note 2026-11-10 (`fix/inventory-member-checks`).** Still open. The claim-refuter agent reported that the inventory
form answers an unknown member 422, from the view's own `Validate`, before the store is reached, so the symptom above
is narrower for that case: an unknown member is a refusal beside the field, and a member of another organization, which
only the store refuses, is the 500. The two answers differ, so the UI also tells an unknown id from another
organization's (1120's note). Mapping the store's `ErrCrossTenantMember` and `ErrUnknownMember` to one refusal would
close both.

**Resolution 2026-11-10 (`feat/inventory-version`, not yet committed).** Fixed as 1147. The inventories writer's
`asFault` maps an unknown member, another organization's member, a taken name and a NUL to fixed-text field errors, one
sentence for both member refusals (`TestAsFault_TheStoreRefusalsTheFormShows`). Whether the form's own `Validate` still
answers an id it does not offer differently, as the note above reported, was not checked.

## 1122. PR 149's coverage job failed although every test passed, because the new container package internal/storage/rowlocktest had no recorded time in durations.json (fixed on the branch; a repeat of 745)

**Symptom.** PR 149 (`fix/patch-inventories-announcements`), run 42836825606, 2026-11-10: every test job passed, and
the `coverage` job failed in 19 seconds at `make coverage-measured`. The floor check passed ("none below their
recorded floor" bar the four LocalStack packages CI never checks); the next command, `testgate -durations-check
.coverage/containers*.json`, printed that `internal/storage/rowlocktest` had no time in `tools/testgate/durations.json`
and exited 1. The local `make pr-check` passed, and `make branch-containers` passed.

**Root cause.** As 745: a branch adding a container package must add its time to `durations.json`, and nothing in the
commit that adds the package asks for it. 745's time was caught by a local pr-check run with containers on. This
time pr-check left container packages to Actions (its default since FAILURE_PATTERNS 755), so with no
`.coverage/pr/containers.json` its `durations` step never ran, and the CI `coverage` job, which reads the shards'
records, was the first to see the package. `branch-containers` runs the package's tests but not the durations check.

**Fix.** Added `"internal/storage/rowlocktest": 4,` (the measured time) to `tools/testgate/durations.json`, folded
into the commit that adds the package.

**Lesson.** A branch that adds a package to `DOCKER_DEPENDENT_PACKAGES` adds its `durations.json` line in the same
commit. Until a check enforces it (prscope or commitgate could flag a listed package with no time), add it by hand
whenever the Makefile's container list grows.

## 1123. A source URL's query or fragment was refused only as a literal "?" or "#", so a signature written behind "%3F", "%23", a double encoding, a fullwidth percent sign or a Unicode lookalike was stored in plain text and shown raw, even in the redacted form; the branch's first fix, a longer list, still missed nine forms (fixed on this branch; on main since #147; a repeat of 1089 and 458; LESSONS 190 and 375; vuln-corpus C13, as 354)

**Symptom.** Found by an outside review (Fable 5.2, through the API) on `fix/source-url-encoded-query`, 2026-11-10.
1089's allowlist refuses any query or fragment in a project's source URL, since one may carry a credential (a SAS
`sig`, an S3 signature, a token). `hasQueryOrFragment` (`internal/project/secret_url.go`) looked for the characters `?`
and `#` only. A URL holding the same signature behind `%3F` or `%23`, or behind a Unicode lookalike of either, passed,
was stored as written for a manual or archive project, and was shown raw by `GET /projects/{id}`, the list and the UI.
Measured red: `RedactedSourceURL("https://svc:pw@host/r.git%3Fsig=hunter2")` returned
`https://redacted@host/r.git%3Fsig=hunter2`. The password was cut out and the signature beside it was shown.

The branch's first fix added a list: `%3f`, `%23`, U+FF1F, U+FE56, U+FF03, U+FE5F and their percent encodings. Both
review passes (the fp-reviewer agent, and the claim-refuter agent with a Python scan of every code point NFKC maps to
`?`, `#`, `@` or `%`) found shapes it still missed: U+FE16 and U+2047 to U+2049, which NFKC also turns into `?`; double
encodings (`%253F`, `%2523`, and `%2540` for the sibling `@` list, `hasAtLookalike`); and the fullwidth and small
percent signs (U+FF05, U+FE6A), which turn any escape into a lookalike of one. That was caught before push.

**Root cause.** The check compared the raw text with a list of the forms a forbidden character can take. A reader along
the way (a browser, a proxy, a server, a log viewer) may decode or normalize the URL before it acts on it, so the
character the rule forbids can appear in any form that becomes it. A list names the forms someone thought of.

**Why 1089's fix did not hold.** 1089 replaced a list of credential shapes with an allowlist, as LESSONS 190 advises,
but the allowlist's own terms (`?`, `#`, `@`) were still read from the raw text, and its `@` rule was again a list
(`%40`, U+FF20, U+FE6B and their encodings). So the allowlist moved the denylist down one level, from shapes of
credentials to shapes of three characters. Each fix in this family, 458's, 1089's three passes, and this branch's
first, extended a list, and each next review found a form the list lacked. LESSONS 375 says to stop after the second
review of a family and change what the check reads; the first fix here was the family's fifth patch of a list. The
same class is vuln-corpus C13's entry for 354, where an escaper doubled only the ASCII apostrophe and missed the
typographic quotes PowerShell also reads as one.

**Fix.** `972493c9`. `revealed` (`internal/project/url_reveal.go`) reads a URL as a reader could come to read it: NFKC
(`golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm`, now a direct requirement in `go.mod`) and then a lenient percent decode, which
decodes every well-formed `%XX` and leaves any other `%`, repeated until the text stops changing, at most eight rounds.
Text that has not settled by then is treated as carrying `?`, `#` and `@`. `hasQueryOrFragment` and `hasAtLookalike`
ask it, so `HasEmbeddedSecret`, `RefuseEmbeddedSecret` and `RedactedSourceURL` refuse such a URL on write and withhold
it whole on read. Tests: `TestRevealed_SettlesOrSaysItDidNot` and `TestPercentDecoded_DecodesOnlyWellFormedEscapes`
(`internal/project/url_reveal_internal_test.go`), the rows added to `internal/project/source_secret_test.go`, and
`TestProjects_ASourceURLMayCarryNoQueryOrFragment` (`internal/api`).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 431. Check a character's ban on the text as a reader could come to read it, not on a list of the
forms it may take.

## 1124. The project store held every edit to the source rules, so a project stored with a URL a later rule refuses (a credential, or a source the deployment's policy now refuses) could not be renamed or described until its URL changed (fixed on this branch; on main since #147 by design, reversed by owner decision 2026-11-10; a repeat in kind of 1114 and 1103; LESSONS 415 and 422)

**Symptom.** On main, the project store's `Update` (`internal/project/ent_store.go`) ran `checkSource` on the project
as it would be saved, on every edit. A project stored before a rule existed (a credential in its URL, which 1088 and
1089 began to refuse, or a source a deployment's policy came to refuse) answered an edit of its name or description
with the source refusal, for a URL the caller had not sent. This was deliberate: 1088's fix says "its next save is
refused until its URL changes". The owner decided on 2026-11-10 that only creation refuses a stored value.

**Root cause.** A rule that tightens what may be stored was held to a field the edit kept, read from storage and
written back, so the rule acted on stored data (LESSONS 415 and 422).

**Why 1114 did not prevent it.** 1114, fixed earlier the same day, is the same mistake: the inventory store's new
blank-name rule held a stored name to a rule newer than it. Its fix (`checkSetText`, `checkText`) was scoped to the two
stores its branch touched. The project rule was not an oversight but a recorded design (1088), so a sweep for the
mistake would not have read it as one; it changed only when the owner decided.

**Fix.** `8e24dc6a`. `checkSourceChange` runs every source rule only when the edit changes the URL or the project
becomes git (1125). An echo of the redacted or withheld URL (`KeepEchoedSourceURL`, 1087) keeps the stored URL and now
saves. The UI harness's fake store (`fakeProjectStore.Update`, `internal/ui/resources/harness_test.go`) applies the
same rule, and the API and UI tests that pinned the old refusal pin the new one
(`internal/api/projects_patch_test.go`, `internal/ui/resources/projects_edit_test.go`). Tests:
`TestStore_AStoredCredentialInTheURLIsReadableAndKeptByAnEditThatLeavesIt` and
`TestStore_ASourceThePolicyNowRefusesIsKeptByAnEditThatLeavesIt` (`internal/project`).

**Lesson.** As 1114, LESSONS 415 and 422. When the owner reverses a recorded design, its entry gets a note (1088's
now has one).

## 1125. The first checkSourceChange skipped the embedded-secret refusal when an edit changed only the type, so turning a manual project whose stored URL carries a password into a git one would have saved, and its next sync dialed with the password (fixed before push; caught in review; a repeat in kind of 1022; LESSONS 421)

**Symptom.** Found by both review passes (the fp-reviewer and claim-refuter agents) on `fix/source-url-encoded-query`,
2026-11-10, reasoned from the code; not run before the fix. The first version of 1124's fix ran the source rules only
when the URL changed. `PATCH {"scm_type":"git"}` on a manual project stored before 1088's rule, whose URL carries a
password, left the URL unchanged, so no rule ran. The project would have saved as git, and its next sync would have
sent the password to the host.

**Root cause.** A rule was moved under "only when the value changed", and the change that mattered was in another
field. For a manual project the URL is only stored; for a git project it is dialed. The type changed what the URL is
used for while the URL stayed the same.

**Why 1022 and LESSONS 421 did not prevent it.** 421 says a rule that must hold in every case does not run inside the
branch a comparison opens, and to list the cases with nothing to compare. Here the comparison had both values and found
them equal. The missed case was not a missing input but a second field that changes what the compared value does, and
421's rule does not name it.

**Fix.** Before push, in `8e24dc6a`. `checkSourceChange` treats a project becoming git as a change of URL and runs every
rule (`becomesGit`, `internal/project/ent_store.go`). Test: `TestStore_TurningAProjectGitHoldsItsStoredURLToEveryRule`
(`internal/project/source_secret_test.go`).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 432.

## 1126. The project store's Update read the stored URL to decide whether its rules run, with no lock, so on PostgreSQL an edit could write back a credential URL another edit had just replaced, unchecked as unchanged (fixed before push; a repeat of 1112 and 1100; LESSONS 429)

**Symptom.** Found by the writer on `fix/source-url-encoded-query`, 2026-11-10, before push. 1124's fix made `Update`
read the stored type and URL and compare them with the project to be saved. With no row lock, on PostgreSQL's read
committed: edit A read a project whose stored URL carries a credential; edit B replaced that URL with a clean one and
committed; A, whose project still held the old URL, compared it with what it had read, found it unchanged, skipped
every rule, and wrote the credential URL back.

**Root cause.** As 1112 and 1100: a read whose result decides the write, taken outside the write's lock. Here the read
decided whether a rule runs, not only what is written.

**Why 1112 and 1100 did not prevent it.** The writer had recorded 1112 and LESSONS 429 on the previous branch the same
day. Their fixes added locks to the stores those branches changed. Before this branch the project `Update` wrote the
record without reading it, so it had nothing to lock. The read was added by this branch, in a change about which rules
run, and nothing flags a store read inside an update that is not under the row lock.

**Fix.** Before push, in `8e24dc6a`. `Update` writes `updated_at` first in its transaction, which takes the row lock as
the inventory and announcement stores do, and reads the stored record after it. Tests:
`TestProjectEditsNeverInterleave_PostgreSQL` (`internal/storage/rowlocktest/project.go` and `postgres_test.go`) and
`TestStore_EditsOfOneProjectNeverInterleave_SQLite` (`internal/project/ent_store_lock_test.go`). Measured with the lock
removed: the PostgreSQL test reports "after both edits the stored URL carries the credential again", and the SQLite test
fails with "database is locked".

**Lesson.** As 1100 and LESSONS 429. A read added to an update to decide which rules run is a read the write depends
on, and goes under the lock with the rest.

## 1127. The withheld placeholder "(withheld: the URL carries a credential)" passed RefuseEmbeddedSecret, so a stale UI form, whose URL had changed since it was shown, saved the placeholder as a manual project's source URL (fixed on this branch; on main; a repeat in kind of 1087 and 580)

**Symptom.** Found by the fp-reviewer agent on `fix/source-url-encoded-query`, 2026-11-10, reasoned from the code. The
UI's edit form prefills a URL that may carry a credential with the text `RedactedSourceURL` shows, which for a URL
whose userinfo it cannot cut out cleanly is the fixed placeholder. `KeepEchoedSourceURL` (1087) keeps the stored URL only when the submitted text equals
what the stored URL redacts to now. If the URL changed after the form was rendered, the placeholder no longer matched,
was taken as a new URL, and passed `RefuseEmbeddedSecret`, which looks for `@`, `?` and `#` and finds none. For a
manual project, which no source policy checks, the placeholder was saved as the source.

**Root cause.** The write recognized the read's mask only as the echo of the current stored value. The mask's own text
was not refused as a value.

**Why 1087's fix did not hold.** 1087 cited 580, whose fix refuses the mask's own marker, and chose instead to recognize
the exact text the read showed for the stored URL. That holds only while the stored URL has not changed since the read.
609 had already shown, for `net.ios.config`, that a masked placeholder must be refused wherever it can come back.

**Fix.** `8e24dc6a`. `RefuseEmbeddedSecret` refuses the placeholder text. Test:
`TestStore_RefusesTheWithheldPlaceholderAsAURL` (`internal/project/source_secret_test.go`).

**Lesson.** As 580 and 609: a write behind a redacting read refuses the mask's own text, besides keeping the stored
value for an exact echo.

## 1128. A sync error stored before this branch's rules kept the signature it quoted, and the API's sync_error, the UI's project row and the UI's sync history showed it raw, because a stored error was scrubbed only when stored, by that release's rules (fixed on this branch; on main; the class of 1090)

**Symptom.** Found by the claim-refuter agent on `fix/source-url-encoded-query`, 2026-11-10, reasoned from the code;
the fix is tested. 1090's `scrubURL` (`internal/project/git.go`) withholds a sync's transport error when the URL may
carry a credential, and runs once, when the error is stored. A sync of a URL holding `%3Fsig=...`, recorded before
1123's rule, was stored with the signature in its text, since the rule of that release did not flag the URL. Every
reader returned the stored text: `sync_error` in the API, the UI's project row, and the UI's sync history.

**Root cause.** A mask was applied only by the writer, so stored text kept the rules of the release that wrote it.

**Fix.** `ab9b4804`. `project.ShownSyncError` applies `scrubURL` again when an error is shown, against the project's
current URL. The readers call it: `internal/api/projects.go`, `internal/ui/resources/projects/projects.go` and
`internal/ui/resources/projects/history.go`. Tests: `TestShownSyncError_WithholdsAnErrorAnOlderReleaseStored`
(`internal/project`) and `TestProjects_AStoredSyncErrorIsCheckedAgainWhenShown` (`internal/api`).

Known limit: an error recorded against an earlier URL is judged by the current one, so an error from a URL since
replaced by a clean one is shown as stored.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 433.

## 1129. `head -25 FILE | rg PATTERN < /dev/null` searched the whole working tree instead of the pipe and printed 38 MB, because the redirect replaced the pipe as rg's input (open, as a practice; a repeat of 1118, the case LESSONS 430's second half names)

**Symptom.** On `fix/source-url-encoded-query`, 2026-11-10. The writer ran `head -25 FILE | rg PATTERN < /dev/null`.
The redirect, not the pipe, became rg's standard input; rg, given no path and no input to read, searched the working
directory and printed 38 MB.

**Root cause.** As 1118 and LESSONS 430: rg reads stdin or the working directory depending on whether it has a path and
what its stdin is, and `< /dev/null` on the reader of a pipe takes the pipe away.

**Why 1118 and LESSONS 430 did not prevent it.** 430 was written the same day by the records-keeper agent and names
this exact case in its second half: put `< /dev/null` on a command that must not read input, never on the reader of a
pipe. The habit carried from it was its first half alone, "add `< /dev/null`", applied to every rg. A rule with two
halves was remembered as one. Nothing checks for it: the session's command guard asks for bounded rg output, not for
where its input comes from.

**Fix.** None in code. The practice is 430's whole rule. A guard could refuse `| rg ... < /dev/null`, which is never
what a writer means; that is not built.

**Lesson.** As LESSONS 430. A habit drawn from a rule keeps its exceptions or it repeats the failure the rule recorded.

## 1130. A job launched against one organization's inventory dispatched to another organization's device, because a member the inventory held could later move into that organization and dispatch read the stored membership with no organization filter; the branch's first fix filtered only SetsForDevice, which nothing in production calls (fixed on this branch; on main; the first fix caught in review before push; a repeat of 97; LESSONS 191, 244 and 434)

**Symptom.** Found on `fix/inventory-member-checks`, 2026-11-10. An inventory may hold an unowned device and a group.
Both can change after the inventory took them in: `inventory.AssignDeviceOrganization` puts an unowned device in an
organization (a kubeconfig import with replace does), and a group the inventory holds can later gain another
organization's device. The stored membership kept them. Dispatch (`internal/dispatch/worker.go`'s `targetSelector`,
then `inventory.Set.Selector`, then the ent repository's `GetGroup` in `internal/inventory/ent_repository.go`) read
that membership as stored. So a job launched against organization A's inventory, by hand or on a schedule, dispatched
to organization B's device with that device's own stored credential. Measured red:
`TestSetSelector_NeverStreamsAMemberOfAnotherOrganization` (`internal/inventory/ent_set_store_members_test.go`)
streamed `[grouped loose own unowned]`, want `[own unowned]`.

The branch's first version put the drift filter only into `SetsForDevice`. That is the resolver the design names as
what fills `ScopeTarget.InventoryIDs`, but nothing in production calls it (gopls: only tests), and nothing in
production fills `ScopeTarget.InventoryIDs` (98's note of 2026-11-10). Dispatch, the reader that acts on the
membership, was unchanged. The claim-refuter and fp-reviewer agents found this independently, before push.

**Root cause.** 97's fix checks membership once, when it is written. The facts that check reads (a device's
organization, a group's devices) can change after the write, and no reader that acts on the membership checked them
again. The first fix then guarded the reader the design named rather than the reader that runs.

**Why 97's fix did not hold.** 97 said the write "is the only place it can be stopped - by the time the resolver sees
the containment it is a fact". That holds only while the members' organizations never change, and two code paths
change them. LESSONS 191 already says a gate checked only when a record is authored is a lint, and to check it where
the thing happens; 97 predates the paths that move a device, and nobody went back to it when they were added. The
first fix then missed LESSONS 244: of two readers of the same membership (device to inventories, and inventory to
devices), it guarded one. As in 1091, whose lesson says 456's fix reached "the one lookup it found", the guard went to
the lookup the writer was looking at.

**Fix.** On this branch, in `266e0f8c`. `pkg/inventory.Membership.OrganizationID` carries the collection's
organization, `Set.Selector` (`internal/inventory/set.go`) fills it, and `GetGroup` keeps only that organization's
devices and unowned ones. A drifted member stays in the stored membership and no job reaches it. `SetsForDevice`
(`internal/inventory/ent_set_store.go`) also answers a device that belongs to an organization only with that
organization's inventories. Tests: `TestSetSelector_NeverStreamsAMemberOfAnotherOrganization` and
`TestEntSetStore_SetsForDeviceSkipsAnotherOrganizationsInventory`.

**Known limits.** Reasoned, not run.
- `SetsForDevice` reads the device and the inventories in two statements, so a device moved between them is answered
  once by its old organization's inventories. It has no production caller; its comment says so.
- `Create` checks members and then inserts outside a transaction, so a concurrent `AssignDeviceOrganization` can slip
  a foreign member into a new inventory. This was there before the branch and is not fixed; dispatch now filters such a
  member out, and an update does not check it again (1132).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 434.

## 1131. A code comment, the OpenAPI text and the security changelog fragment said a drifted inventory member grants nothing, which was false until dispatch filtered it (fixed before push; caught in review with 1130; a repeat of 1115 and 1074)

**Symptom.** On `fix/inventory-member-checks`, 2026-11-10, before push. The branch's first version filtered a drifted
member out of `SetsForDevice` only (1130) and said, in three places, that such a member "grants nothing": a code
comment, the OpenAPI text and the security changelog fragment. A job launched against the inventory still reached the
member, with its own stored credential, so the claim was false. The review that found 1130 (the claim-refuter and
fp-reviewer agents) showed it.

**Root cause.** The claim was written from the one reader the fix changed, not from every reader that acts on the
membership.

**Why 1115 and 1074 did not prevent it.** 1115 was recorded the same day for the same store: a claim written from the
fix's own test rather than from every writer of the field. This is its mirror, every reader rather than every writer.
Their class has no check for a comment's claim before review, and the review pass that refutes claims is again what
caught it.

**Fix.** Before push, in the fixups folded into `266e0f8c` and `a78ffdf4`. The dispatch filter made the claim true
(1130), and the text now says what each reader does: `SetsForDevice`'s comment points at `Set.Selector`, and
`changelog/inventory-member-drift.security.md` says a drifted member stays stored and no job reaches it.

**Lesson.** As 1115 and LESSONS 434: a claim that something "grants nothing" is a claim about every reader that acts on
it. List them by reference before writing it.

## 1132. An inventory update checked every member it held, not only those it added, so a member that had since moved into another organization blocked every edit that kept it, a rename included (fixed on this branch; on main; a repeat of 1114 and 1124; LESSONS 415 and 422)

**Symptom.** On `fix/inventory-member-checks`, 2026-11-10, from the code. `UpdateWith`
(`internal/inventory/ent_set_store_update.go`), which `Update` and the API PATCH both reach, ran the tenancy check over
every member of the saved list. A member stored when it was allowed, and since drifted (1130), was refused on every
later edit that kept it, including a rename or the removal of some other member. The drift itself still reached the
other organization through dispatch (1130), so the refusal blocked the owner and protected nothing.

**Root cause.** As 1114: a write held data it was keeping, not changing, to a rule. Here the rule was old (97), and the
stored data it read (the member's organization) changed after the member was stored.

**Why 1114 and 1124 did not prevent it.** 1114's fix, on the previous branch for this same store, moved the text rules
(`checkSetText`) to the fields an update changes. The membership check on the same update was not read against that
lesson. 1124, the project store's case the same day, was framed as a rule newer than the stored value; here the rule was
unchanged and its input moved, which neither title names.

**Fix.** On this branch, in `266e0f8c`. `UpdateWith` checks only the members the update adds (`addedIDs`). Re-adding a
drifted member is still refused. `checkMembers` runs every check before it returns and joins each sentinel that applies
(`errors.Join`), so the API can answer both with one sentence (1120). Test:
`TestEntSetStore_AnUpdateChecksOnlyTheMembersItAdds` (`internal/inventory/ent_set_store_members_test.go`).

**Lesson.** As 1114 and LESSONS 415 and 422: a write checks what it adds. A member it keeps is stored data, and a rule
whose input can change after storage is enforced where the data is acted on (LESSONS 434), not by blocking every later
edit.

## 1133. The web UI read records in process and gated each page only on its endpoint's first scope, so after the branch's first fix a session holding inventory:write alone still opened /ui/inventories/1/edit (200) and saved it (303) while the API refused the same token (fixed before push; caught in review; on main as part of 1119; a repeat of 1130; LESSONS 244, 363 and 434)

**Symptom.** On `fix/patch-needs-read-and-write`, 2026-11-10, before push. The branch's first version put the second
scope (1119) into the API router only: `api.Route.AlsoScope`, enforced by a second `RequireScope` before the handler.
The web UI does not serve its pages through that router. It reads records in process, and it checked only
`apispec.Endpoint.Scope`: in `internal/ui/web/resources.go` (`resolve`, the record actions and the row actions) and, for
the controls it offers, in `internal/ui/view/view.go` (`Descriptor.Candidates`). So a JWT holding `inventory:write`
alone, signed in at `/ui`, opened `/ui/inventories/1/edit` (measured 200), which shows the stored record, and saved it
(303). The JSON API answered the same token 403. The claim-refuter and fp-reviewer agents found it by reading the code,
and it was then measured.

**Root cause.** One rule, declared once and enforced in two places, was added to one of them. The router is where a
scope rule lives for the JSON API, so the first version listed the router's routes and stopped there. The UI's readers
reach the stores without passing through the router.

**Why 1130's fix did not hold.** 1130 and LESSONS 434, recorded the same day, say to list every reader that acts on the
data from the production call graph before calling a grant closed. They were written for a tenancy rule on stored
membership. This branch's rule was framed as a route rule, so its places were taken from the route table rather than
from the readers of the record. LESSONS 244 (a guard on one of two sibling paths) and 363 (every route a mechanism
takes, tier included) name the same class. None of them was applied to the UI as a second reader of the same records.

**Fix.** On this branch, in `0882d90b`. `web.permitsEndpoint` (`internal/ui/web/handler.go`) checks an endpoint's
`Scope` and, when it declares one, its `AlsoScope`; `resolve`, the record actions and the row actions call it.
`view.Descriptor.AlsoCandidates` (`internal/ui/view/view.go`) offers the second scope's affordances to the generator, so
a caller holding both scopes still sees the control. As in 100 and 220, a gated relation needs a place in the candidate
set as well as in the gate, and only the gate fails loudly without it. Both tiers read the one declaration,
`apispec.Endpoint.AlsoScope`. Tests: `TestUI_AWriteScopeAloneCannotOpenAnEditForm`
(`internal/ui/resources/write_only_session_test.go`), which fails with the second scope removed, and
`TestDescriptor_AlsoCandidatesOffersEverySecondScope` (`internal/ui/view/alsocandidates_test.go`).

**Lesson.** As LESSONS 434, for any rule and not only tenancy: a rule placed in the router covers only the callers that
pass through the router. List the readers of the record from the store up (the UI reads in process), not the router's
route table. LESSONS 435 has the rest. The same class is vuln-corpus finding C10_auto-roboto_2026-11-07 (two tiers
enforcing one rule drift apart).

## 1134. The branch's first fix required the read scope on PATCH and PUT only, chosen by HTTP method, but seven write-scoped POSTs also answer with the stored record, and its guard test forbade a second scope on any POST under a comment saying only PATCH and PUT answer with a folded record (fixed before push; caught in review with 1133; on main as part of 1119; a repeat in kind of 1089, and of 1115 and 1131 for the comment; LESSONS 155 and 157)

**Symptom.** On `fix/patch-needs-read-and-write`, 2026-11-10, before push. The first version gave every PATCH and PUT
endpoint the read scope as its `AlsoScope` and left every POST alone. Seven POSTs a write scope reaches answer with the
record they act on, so a write-only token could still read it: `copy_template` returns the whole template,
`sync_project` and `cancel_project_sync` return the project, `attest_organization` and `attest_team` return the
organization or the team, `test_credential_type` returns the stored injectors, and `create_template_config`'s refusals
judge the body against the stored survey. The guard test (`internal/apispec/patch_scopes_test.go`) failed any POST that
declared an `AlsoScope`, and its comment said only PATCH and PUT answer with a folded record, which was false. The review
that found 1133 found these by reading the handlers.

**Root cause.** What a route shows a caller is decided by what its handler answers with, and the first version decided
it by the verb. The guard test was written from the same premise, so it would have refused the fix.

**Why 1089 and LESSONS 155 and 157 did not prevent it.** 1089 was a list of credential shapes that missed members of its
class, and LESSONS 155 and 157 say to enumerate a class by what the code does rather than by the instance in hand. Here
the instance was 1119's `PATCH {}`. Selecting by method looked like a class, because it is a complete filter over the
route table. It is complete for the verb, not for the property the rule is about. As in 1115 and 1131, the comment
stated the premise as a fact, and nothing checked it before review.

**Fix.** On this branch, in `0882d90b`. The seven POSTs declare `AlsoScope`, so 25 endpoints do: 13 PATCH, 5 PUT and 7
POST. The guard test names the seven in `recordAnsweringPosts`, holds each of the 25 to the read scope of its write
scope, and fails any other endpoint that declares one; its comment now says what it checks.
`TestAlsoScope_EveryDeclaringRouteRefusesTheFirstScopeAlone` (`internal/api/patch_scopes_test.go`) mounts all 25
through the real router and refuses each one to its first scope alone. The OpenAPI document lists both scopes, and
`changelog/patch-needs-read-and-write.breaking.md` names the 25 scope additions schema-compat reports as breaking.

**Known limits.** From the repository. `recordAnsweringPosts` is kept by hand, so a POST added later that answers with a
stored record passes the guard until someone adds it to the list. DELETE and the routes whose scope is not a `*:write`
scope (`runbook:execute`, `inventory:onboard`, `inventory:assert`) are outside the rule; 1119's note of 2026-11-10 lists
what they still show.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 435.

## 1135. The branch's first version gave POST /jobs/{id}/rollback only job:read, though a rollback reads the job's template and names a bound credential in a refusal exactly as a relaunch does, which got job:read and template:read; the guard test's table of reads held the gap in place (fixed before push; caught in review; a repeat of 939, and of 1134's class; LESSONS 244, 363 and 436)

**Symptom.** On `fix/action-route-read-scopes`, 2026-11-10, before push. Owner decision 2026-11-10: an action route
needs the read scope of each record it reads (1119's open list). The branch's first version wrote each route's reads
into a table in the guard test (`requiredReads`, `internal/apispec/patch_scopes_test.go`). It gave `relaunch_job`
`job:read` and `template:read`, and `rollback_job` `job:read` alone. `Dispatcher.Rollback`
(`internal/api/dispatcher_rollback.go`) reads the job's template and calls `refuseUnrepeatableCredentials`
(`internal/api/dispatcher.go`) on it, as a relaunch does, and that refusal names the bound credential. So a token
holding `runbook:execute` and `job:read` without `template:read` could still have the template read for it, and a bound
credential's name answered back. The guard test holds every route to the table, so it passed. The fp-reviewer and
claim-refuter agents found it by reading the handlers.

**Root cause.** The table was written route by route, and a rollback was given the reads of a job action (the job)
rather than the reads of the code it shares with relaunch. 1119's open note named cancel, relaunch and launch, and not
rollback, so nothing pointed at the template read inside it.

**Why 939 and 1134 did not prevent it.** 939 found that the rollback route is a second door into a job that applies the
template's rules by hand (it calls `refuseUnrepeatableCredentials` itself), and its lesson says to list the routes that
create a job (launch, saved configuration, schedule, relaunch, rollback, check) when a launch field is added. It was
written for a launch field, and this branch's rule was a scope rule, so the list was taken from 1119's note instead.
1134 is a guard test written from an incomplete premise, which then holds the gap in. Here the premise was one row of
the table rather than a filter by verb, and the test held it in the same way.

**Fix.** On this branch, in `8a3449d3`. `rollback_job` (`internal/apispec/template_endpoints.go`) declares `job:read`
and `template:read` in `AlsoScopes`, and the table says the same.
`TestAlsoScopes_EveryDeclaringRouteRefusesAMissingScope` (`internal/api/patch_scopes_test.go`) drops each declared scope
in turn, for all 36 routes that declare one, rollback included.

**Known limits.** From the repository. The table is still kept by hand, as LESSONS 435 says of `recordAnsweringPosts`: a
route whose handler starts to read another record passes the guard until its row changes.

**Lesson.** Routes that call the same helper read what the helper reads: take each route's reads from the code it calls,
and give routes sharing a helper the same rows. LESSONS 436 has the rule for a second path to one effect.

## 1136. A schedule's write was gated only on the one launch scope its target's type declares, so after this branch's first version a token refused POST /templates/{id}/launch for want of template:read could still schedule that template to run unattended, read its name back, and have the schedule's preflight refusals name its bound credentials (fixed before push; caught in review; a repeat of 268, and of 1133; LESSONS 134, 435 and 436)

**Symptom.** On `fix/action-route-read-scopes`, 2026-11-10, before push. The branch's first version gave
`launch_template` `template:read` beside `runbook:execute`, and `sync_project` already needed `project:read` beside
`project:write` (1134). A schedule's write is gated by `launchable.Reach.Admits` (`internal/launchable/reach.go`), which
the schedule store calls at the write and the UI picker calls when it decides what to offer (268). `Admits` checked only
`launchable.Descriptor.LaunchScope`. So a token holding `schedule:write` and `runbook:execute` without `template:read`,
refused the launch route by hand, could still create a schedule that runs the template repeatedly. The schedule's answer
names its target, and its preflight refusals call `refuseUnrepeatableCredentials` (`internal/api/dispatcher_launchable.go`),
which names a bound credential (1135). The same held for a project without `project:read`. The fp-reviewer and
claim-refuter agents found it by reading the code.

**Root cause.** A second way to make a run kept a copy of the launch route's scope rather than reading the route's
declaration, and the copy had room for one scope, as `Route.AlsoScope` once did. When the route gained a read scope,
nothing on the schedule side could say so.

**Why 268 and 1133 did not hold.** 268's fix made each launchable type declare the scope needed to launch it, and
`TestBuiltins_DeclareTheScopeTheirOwnRouteRequires` (`internal/launchable/types/builtins_test.go`) held that one scope
equal to the route's one scope. Its rule is that a mechanism causing work later checks the permission to do that work
now. It was right, and the permission it encoded was one scope, so it held only while the route needed one. 1133 found
that the UI reads the same records outside the router; the schedule store is another such reader, through `launchable`,
and this branch's list of places did not include it.

**Fix.** On this branch, in `8a3449d3`. `launchable.Descriptor.ReadScopes` (`internal/launchable/launchable.go`) names
the read scopes a type's own launch route requires (`job_template`: `template:read`; `project`: `project:read`), and
`Reach.Admits` requires each one. `TestBuiltins_DeclareTheScopeTheirOwnRouteRequires` holds them to the routes'
`AlsoScopes`. `TestReach_Admits` (`internal/launchable/launchable_test.go`) and
`TestSchedules_WritingOneNeedsPermissionToLaunchWhatItLaunches` (`internal/api/schedules_launchable_test.go`) gained cases
for a caller missing a read scope.

**Known limits.** From the repository. `TestBuiltins_DeclareTheScopeTheirOwnRouteRequires` restates the routes' scopes in
its own map rather than reading `apispec`, deliberately, so the package does not depend on the route table; a scope added
to `LaunchTemplate` or `SyncProject` later passes it until someone edits the map too. A schedule is authorized when it is
written and not judged again when it fires (`Reach`'s doc comment), so a schedule written before this branch by a token
without the read scope keeps firing.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 436.

## 1137. POST /projects and PATCH /projects/{id} read the credential they bind, and checkCredential's three answers told a caller without credential:read which organization owns a credential id and whether it can authenticate a clone (fixed before push; caught in review; a repeat in kind of 1091 and 1096; LESSONS 435)

**Symptom.** On `fix/action-route-read-scopes`, 2026-11-10, before push. `ProjectHandler.checkCredential`
(`internal/api/projects.go`) lists every credential and answers in one of three ways: 400 "no credential with that id in
this project's organization" for a missing id or another organization's, 400 "not a source control credential" for one
of the organization that cannot authenticate a clone, and success otherwise. The caller chooses the project's
organization (the function's own comment says so, 98). So by trying organizations, a token holding `project:write`
without `credential:read` could learn which organization owns a credential id and whether it is a git credential. The
routes needed `project:write`, and `PATCH` also `project:read` (1119). The fp-reviewer and claim-refuter agents found it
by reading the handlers.

**Root cause.** A refusal that judges the body against a stored record shows that record, and the record here belongs to
another store, whose read scope the route did not require.

**Why 1091, 1096 and LESSONS 435 did not prevent it.** 1091 answered another organization's credential exactly as a
missing one, and 1096 took names out of refusals. Both worked on what one answer says. While the caller can choose the
organization, the merged answer still tells the owner by trial, and the kind refusal is a third answer. LESSONS 435 lists
"a refusal that judges the body against one" among what a route shows, but this branch's first version took its list
from 1119's open note, which named action routes.

**Fix.** On this branch, in `8a3449d3`. `create_project` declares `credential:read`, and `update_project` declares
`project:read` and `credential:read` (`internal/apispec/project_endpoints.go`), with the same rows in `requiredReads`.

**Known limits.** From the repository. A caller holding `credential:read` still gets the three answers, which is
information that scope can read. Keeping a caller to its own organization waits on per-organization authorization (98).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 435, with its whole list: sweep every handler for refusals that judge the body against another
store's record, not only the routes an open note names.

## 1138. POST /inventory/kubeconfig-imports checked inventory:write in its handler only, so the OpenAPI document, the OPTIONS Allow header and _links offered it to a token the handler then refused (fixed before push; caught in review; the class of 1106 and 1131)

**Symptom.** On `fix/action-route-read-scopes`, 2026-11-10, before push. `import_kubeconfig`
(`internal/apispec/apispec.go`) declared `credential:write` only. `DeviceHandler.ImportKubeconfig`
(`internal/api/devices_kubeconfig.go`) refused a caller without `inventory:write` with 403 "a kubeconfig import writes a
device, which needs inventory:write". The OpenAPI document, the `Allow` header and `_links` are built from the
declaration, so each said less than the code required, and a client following them was refused. The fp-reviewer and
claim-refuter agents found it.

**Root cause.** A route needing two scopes could declare one (`Route.AlsoScope` held a single scope, and that one was
wanted for the read), so the second was checked by hand inside the handler, where the contract cannot see it.

**Why 1106 and 1131 did not prevent it.** Both are text claiming something the code does not do, found and fixed one
claim at a time. Here the claim is generated from the declaration, so the declaration was the text that was wrong, and
no check compared it with the handler's own scope test.

**Fix.** On this branch, in `8a3449d3`. `import_kubeconfig` declares `inventory:write` and `inventory:read` in
`AlsoScopes` beside `credential:write`. The handler's check stays as a second line for a handler mounted another way,
with a comment saying so. `TestAlsoScopes_EveryDeclaringRouteRefusesAMissingScope` drops each of the three in turn.

**Known limits.** From the repository. Nothing finds another handler that checks a scope its route does not declare.

**Lesson.** A scope a handler checks for itself belongs in its route's declaration, so the contract built from it says
the same. When a declaration cannot say it, widen the declaration rather than checking in the handler.

## 1139. Creates, create and edit forms, and some refusals name, list or count another store's records to a caller holding no read scope for them (open: owner decision; on main; reasoned by the claim-refuter agent, not run; the class of 1119, 1120 and 1096)

**Symptom.** Reasoned by the claim-refuter agent on `fix/action-route-read-scopes`, 2026-11-10, from the code; not run.
- The web UI's create and edit forms list other stores' records with no read check. A `project:write` session sees every
  git credential's name, type and organization, across organizations; `template:write` sees every inventory and
  organization; `access:write` every user's email; the grant forms list team names.
- `POST /templates` answers with the named inventory's name and organization, and refuses on an unknown runbook.
- `POST /bindings` answers with device, inventory and group names.
- `POST /credentials` answers with the type's name, namespace and kind.
- `DELETE /credential-types/{id}` answers 409 naming the type and counting its credentials, and a template or project
  `DELETE` answers 409 showing a schedule.
- Creates answer differently for a referenced id that exists and one that does not (teams, inventories, contacts; a user
  create tells whether an email exists; a kubeconfig import names an existing credential).
- Launch and rollback show one bit about the runbook without `runbook:read`.
- The claim-refuter's list also named the schedule form listing every launchable and `POST /schedules` answering with its
  target's name. Both were listed with the review of the branch's first version, before 1136's fix, which now requires
  the target's read scope at the write and in the picker. Whether anything is left there is not checked.

**Root cause.** A create or a form that names another resource reads that resource under the creating scope alone, as
1119's write routes once answered with their own record. The owner's decision of 2026-11-10 covers routes that read
records of their own resource and action routes; creates that name another resource were left out of it.

**Status.** Open, for the owner. The owner decided on 2026-11-10 to leave the `DELETE` 204 and 404 as they are (1119).
Per-organization authorization (98) would narrow the cross-organization part of each item.

**Lesson.** Pending the decision. As 1096: a response names only what the caller sent or may read.

## 1140. A PATCH /inventories/{id} naming groups or devices replaced that list whole with no version check, so a client that read the inventory before another update removed a device put it back, re-granting it to every team the inventory is shared with (fixed on this branch; on main; the gap 1112 and 1085 recorded as open; LESSONS 429 and 437)

**Symptom.** On main, and recorded as open in 1112's status and 1085's note of 2026-11-10. The inventory PATCH folds the
body under the row lock (1112), but a body that names `groups` or `devices` sets that list to what it holds. A client
that read the inventory, then lost a race with an update that removed a device, sent back the list it had read, and the
device came back. An inventory is a grant surface (97), so the device was granted again to every team the inventory is
shared with. `TestInventoryPatch_AStaleCopyCannotRevertARevocation` (`internal/api/inventories_precondition_test.go`)
is that sequence.

**Root cause.** As LESSONS 429: a lock around a fold protects only what the fold reads under it. A list the caller read
earlier and sends whole was never read under the lock, and nothing told the store which state the caller had seen.

**Why 1112 did not prevent it.** 1112 fixed what the lock can reach, a field the body does not name. It said in its own
status that a full list from a stale GET still replaces the stored one, and left the version token to the owner.

**Fix.** On this branch (`feat/inventory-version`), not yet committed. The inventory has an ent `version` column
(`internal/ent/schema/inventory.go`; migrations `sqlite/0046_inventory_version.sql` and
`postgres/0043_inventory_version.sql`). `UpdateWith` bumps it with `AddVersion(1)` in the write that commits, never in
`lockSet`, which takes the lock (`internal/inventory/ent_set_store_update.go`;
`internal/inventory/ent_set_store_version_test.go`). `GET`, `POST` and `PATCH` send an `ETag`. The `If-Match` header is
judged inside the store's fold, under the row lock, so a write that commits between the read and the lock is seen
(`TestInventoryPatch_IfMatchIsJudgedUnderTheLock`). A PATCH that names a list without `If-Match` is refused with 428. An
`If-Match` that is not exactly the current tag is refused with 412: `*`, a weak tag, a list and a header sent on two
lines are each refused (`TestInventoryPatch_IfMatchMustNameTheCurrentTagExactly`). A missing inventory is a 404 before
either refusal. The tag also covers the content (1144). The breaking fragment is `changelog/inventory-if-match.breaking.md`.

**Known limits.** From the repository. A PATCH that names neither list needs no `If-Match`, and two such PATCHes naming
the same field are still last-writer-wins. Team membership (`PATCH /teams/{id}`'s `users`) has the same whole-list shape
and no version; 1085 stays open for it. The compatibility check cannot see this change (1146).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 437.

## 1141. The web UI's inventory edit form replaced the whole inventory with what it was opened with, so saving a description fix after another writer removed a device re-granted it (fixed on this branch; on main; the gap 1112 and 1085 recorded as open; LESSONS 429 and 438)

**Symptom.** On main, and recorded as open in 1112's status and 1085's note of 2026-11-10. The inventories view's writer
(`internal/ui/resources/inventories/inventories.go`) called `Update` with the whole submission. The form held every
device and group it was drawn with, so an operator who opened the form, waited while an API client removed a device,
then saved a description fix put the device back.

**Root cause.** The form sent its whole state, and the writer had no way to tell what the operator changed from what the
form had only carried along. As 1140, the list was read before the lock and written whole after it.

**Why 1112 did not prevent it.** As 1140: the lock covers only what the fold reads under it, and 1112 left this path
open by name.

**Fix.** On this branch, not yet committed. A generic `view.Field.KeepsOriginal` (`internal/ui/view/field.go`) has the
form carry what it was opened with as hidden `_original.<name>` inputs. A lookup's originals are filtered to the options
it offers. Originals are accepted only on an edit and only for declared fields, and are refused on a password field, a
`RefusedValue` field and an immutable one. `Values.Original`, `Values.OriginalSelected` and `Values.Unchanged` read them;
`Validate` skips a field left as the form showed it, so a stored value past a later limit does not block another edit
(`TestUIEdit_AStoredLongNameDoesNotBlockAnotherEdit`). The inventories writer saves through `UpdateWith` with a
three-way merge per element (`internal/ui/resources/inventories/merge.go`): a member the form deselected is removed, one
it selected is added, and every other change made since stays. A text field both writers changed is refused beside the
field with a fixed text, and a refused edit redisplays the submitted originals, so resubmitting it is refused again
(`TestUIEdit_AFieldChangedUnderneathIsRefusedAndStaysRefused`). Tests: `internal/ui/resources/inventories_merge_test.go`,
`internal/ui/resources/inventories/merge_internal_test.go` (on the real ent store) and
`internal/ui/view/originals_internal_test.go`. The fragment is `changelog/ui-inventory-edit-merge.fixed.md`.

**Known limits.** From the review on this branch. Team membership (`PATCH /teams/{id}`'s `users`, and the UI teams form's users
lookup) and the UI template form's credentials lookup still write a list whole from an earlier read. These are likely
1085's class, and 1085 stays open for them.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 438.

## 1142. A refused create or edit in the web UI redisplayed only the first selection of a multiple-choice control, so saving the redisplayed form again silently deselected the rest (fixed on this branch; on main; a repeat in kind of 226)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch. When a create or an edit was refused, the form was drawn again
from the submission. `formValues` (`internal/ui/web/resources.go`) read each field with `Values.Get`, which returns the
first value only. A multi-select with two devices selected came back with one, and an operator who fixed the refused
field and saved again dropped the other with no sign of it. The same held in every view with a multi-select.

**Root cause.** A list was read through an accessor that returns one value.

**Why 226 did not prevent it.** 226 fixed where an edit form's existing values come from when it opens (the prefill),
and its test asserted the stored values were selected on the first draw. The refused form's redisplay is a different
path, and nothing asserted what it shows.

**Fix.** On this branch, not yet committed. `formValues` joins every selected value.
`TestUIEdit_AFieldChangedUnderneathIsRefusedAndStaysRefused` asserts that both devices come back on the refused form.

**Lesson.** As 226: a control that shows nothing selected and a control that holds nothing render the same, so a test
asserts what is selected on every path that draws the form, a refused submission included.

## 1143. ent's generated SQLite migration for an added column rebuilt the inventories table, which drops its sqlite_sequence row, so a deleted inventory's id would be handed out again and a role binding still scoped to it would grant the new inventory, possibly in another organization (fixed before push; a repeat in kind of 266; LESSONS 439; open: bindings are not removed when an inventory is deleted, owner question)

**Symptom.** On this branch, before commit. ent generated the version column's SQLite migration as a table rebuild:
create `new_inventories`, copy the rows, drop `inventories`, rename. Dropping the table drops its `sqlite_sequence` row,
so the next id is one past the highest id still held, not past the highest ever handed out. Measured with Python's
`sqlite3`: after the rebuild, the id of a deleted inventory (3) was handed out again. `role_binding.scope_id` has no
foreign key, and `SetStore.Delete` leaves inventory-scoped bindings in place. So a binding scoped to the deleted
inventory would grant the new inventory that took its id, which may belong to another organization.

**Root cause.** The generator writes a SQLite column change as a rebuild, and a rebuild resets AUTOINCREMENT. A
reference without a foreign key re-attaches to the reused id without any error.

**Why 266 did not prevent it.** 266 fixed the foreign-key side of a rebuild (the `PRAGMA` that never took effect), and
its upgrade test (`internal/ent/migrate/upgrade_internal_test.go`) migrates populated databases and checks that rows and
their children survive. Neither asked what a rebuild does to the sequence.

**Fix.** On this branch, not yet committed. `sqlite/0046_inventory_version.sql` is hand-written as one `ALTER TABLE ...
ADD COLUMN`, which keeps the table, its sequence and its rows. `TestSQLiteMigrations_ARebuildKeepsItsSequence`
(`internal/ent/migrate/sequence_guard_internal_test.go`) refuses any SQLite migration from 0046 on that rebuilds a table
and does not write `sqlite_sequence`.

**Known limits.** From the repository. Older rebuilds (0003, 0007 and 0022 among them) had the same effect and are left
as they are: pre-1.0 nothing is deployed, and a migration once written is never edited. The guard finds a rebuild by
its `new_<table>` rename, so a rebuild written another way would pass it.

**Status.** Open for the root of the risk: role bindings are not removed when an inventory is deleted. Whether they
should be is an owner question.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 439.

## 1144. A version-only ETag would miss writes from a build that predates the version column, since the expand policy lets the previous build keep serving during a rolling upgrade or after a rollback and its writes do not move the version, so a stale If-Match would pass (fixed before push; the class of 1098 and 1103, a mixed-version window; LESSONS 422 and 437)

**Symptom.** On this branch, before commit. The version column is added under
`internal/ent/migrate/compat.go`'s EXPAND policy, so the build before it can keep serving the same database during a
rolling upgrade or after a rollback. That build knows nothing of `version`. Its writes leave it as it was, so a client
holding a tag read before such a write would send an `If-Match` that still matched, and 1140's lost update would come
back through the older build.

**Root cause.** A token that only the newer build moves is not a token for the row while an older build can still write
the row.

**Why 1098 and 1103 did not prevent it.** Both are rules on data in a mixed-version window, fixed for credential types.
Neither is about a concurrency token, and the version column is new on this branch.

**Fix.** On this branch, not yet committed. The ETag is `"<version>.<digest>"`, the digest being 16 bytes of SHA-256 over
the name, the description and the sorted member ids, so a write that leaves the version still changes the tag.
`TestInventoryPatch_AWriteThatLeavesTheVersionStillMovesTheTag` (`internal/api/inventories_precondition_test.go`).

**Known limits.** From the repository. A semantic migration contract could not be declared in place of the digest:
`TestANewContractNeedsTheGuard` (`internal/ent/migrate/compat_internal_test.go`) refuses a new contract until the
apply-time guard exists.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 437, its second half.

## 1145. A browser posts every line break as CRLF, a text input drops line breaks, and the HTML parser drops a textarea's leading LF, so a three-way compare of submitted, original and stored text would have refused every edit of a value stored with LF (fixed before push; LESSONS 438)

**Symptom.** On this branch, before commit. 1141's merge compares what the form submits, what
it was opened with (the hidden `_original.<name>` input) and what is stored. A browser sends every line break as CRLF,
hidden inputs included. A text input drops line breaks. The parser drops a textarea's leading LF. Compared byte for
byte, a description stored with LF never matched its own original, so every edit of it would look like a change made
underneath and be refused. A name holding a line break would have refused every edit at all.

**Root cause.** The compare used the stored bytes as the form's bytes, but the form's bytes are what the browser
rewrote them to.

**Fix.** On this branch, not yet committed. `view.Comparable` (`internal/ui/view`) reduces text to what a browser sends
back, and both `Values.Unchanged` and the merge compare through it. `TestUnchanged_ComparesWhatABrowserSendsBack` and
`TestMergeFold_LineBreaksABrowserRewroteAreNotAChange`.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 438: compare text as the browser sends it back, not as it was stored.

## 1146. tools/schemacompat reports nothing for a header that is required only when the body names a list, since the document can only mark it optional, so a real break in behavior passes the compatibility check unflagged (open: a limit of the check, stated in the breaking fragment)

**Symptom.** On this branch. 1140 makes `If-Match` required on a `PATCH /inventories/{id}` that names `groups` or
`devices`. The OpenAPI document can only declare the header optional, since a PATCH naming neither list needs none. So
`tools/schemacompat`, which compares the documents, sees no change, and a client that worked before is now refused with
428.

**Root cause.** A requirement that depends on the body's content has no place in the document the check reads.

**Status.** Open, as a limit of the check. `changelog/inventory-if-match.breaking.md` says that the compatibility check
reports nothing for this change and why. Nothing in the check itself catches the next one.

**Lesson.** Pending. A conditional requirement is a break the schema check cannot see, so the change says so in its
breaking fragment.

## 1147. The web UI's inventories writer returned a member refusal (a device deleted after the form opened, or another organization's), a taken name and a NUL as a 500 (fixed on this branch; on main; closes 1121; the class of 1058)

**Symptom.** On main, recorded as 1121 (reasoned, not run). The inventories view's writer passed the store's errors
through unmapped, and the generic handler turns anything but not-found into a server error page. So a device deleted
after the form opened, another organization's device, a taken name or a NUL answered 500 rather than a refusal.

**Root cause.** As 1121 and 1058: the view mapped no store refusal to a field.

**Why 1121 did not prevent it.** 1121 was an open record; it named the fix (map `ErrCrossTenantMember` and
`ErrUnknownMember` to one refusal) and no branch had made it.

**Fix.** On this branch, not yet committed. `asFault` (`internal/ui/resources/inventories`) maps each of them to a field
error with a fixed text, with one sentence for an unknown member and another organization's, so the form does not tell
them apart. `TestAsFault_TheStoreRefusalsTheFormShows`.

**Known limits.** Not checked here: whether the form's own `Validate` still answers an id it does not offer before the
store is reached, which 1121's note said it did with a different answer.

**Lesson.** As 1058: a refusal the caller can correct is shown as one, beside the field it concerns.

## 1148. Spans had no boundary: any code could put caller or device text in a span's attributes, events, status text or resource, and the Runner's three RecordError calls copied adapter error text, which can quote device output, into the trace backend past the log masking (fixed on this branch; on main; a repeat of 578, 522 and 417)

**Symptom.** Found on `feat/telemetry-boundary`, 2026-11-10, while building PLAN.md Section 19 item 7 (a security
policy over what a span may carry). The exporter sent every attribute, event, recorded error, span name, status
description and resource attribute as it was given. `handleMessage` (`internal/runner/agent_handle.go`) recorded each of
its three failures with `span.RecordError`, which copies the error's text into an `exception` event. An adapter's error
can quote device output, so that text reached whatever trace backend an operator runs, where no log masking applies.

**Root cause.** A trace exporter is an output channel, and nobody had listed it as one. The logs are masked through
`internal/redact` at the handler; spans never passed through it, and nothing limited which keys, names or events a span
could carry.

**Why 578 (and 522, 417) did not prevent it.** Each of those found a new output path that skipped the masking beside it,
and each fix was per path: test output in `tools/testgate` (417, 522), the FRR methods and the grant route (578).
578's lesson says to mask where text comes in from the device. A span takes text from every layer (the API, the Runner,
the SDK itself), so there is no one place where it "comes in", and no list of output channels existed to find this one.

**Fix.** `7aac7bbc` and `b0001aa7`. Every exporter `Setup` builds (stdout and OTLP) sits behind a masking `SpanExporter`
(`internal/telemetry/masking_exporter.go`). It keeps only keys on a fixed allowlist (`telemetry.AllowedAttributeKeys`),
which `PLEIADES_TELEMETRY_DENY_ATTRIBUTES` can narrow and nothing can widen (an unknown key stops startup). It masks every
kept string with `redact.Shared()`, drops every event but the SDK's `exception` (keeping only its type), withholds a status
description that is not a declared phrase or a 5xx `StatusText`, keeps a span name or instrumentation scope only when
declared, keeps `error.type` only as a declared category, drops the schema URL, filters the resource, and drops a batch
whose masking panics (failing closed). `Setup` installs span limits (values cut at 1024 bytes). The Runner's failures use
`telemetry.RecordFailure` with a fixed `Outcome` phrase, and each error log line carries the span's `trace_id` so the text
in the masked log can be found from the span. Tests: `TestMaskingExporterMasksEveryTextChannel`,
`TestMaskingExporterDropsABatchItCannotMask`, `TestSetup_ExportsNoValueUnderAnUnlistedKey`,
`TestSetup_MasksSecretShapesUnderAListedKey`, `TestSetup_ExportsNoRecordedErrorText`,
`TestSetup_WithholdsAFreeStatusDescription`, `TestSetup_ExportsOnlyDeclaredSpanNames`,
`TestSetup_ExportsOnlyDeclaredScopeDetails`, `TestSetup_FiltersTheResourceTheEnvironmentSets`,
`TestSetup_ExportsNoPanicText`, `TestSetup_OTLPExportCarriesOnlyThePolicy` (`internal/telemetry`) and
`TestAgent_SpanFailuresAreFixedPhrases` (`internal/runner`). `docs/10-running-in-production.md`'s Telemetry section states
the boundary.

**Known limits.** 1158: masking under an allowed key catches only secret shapes and known values.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 440: an observability channel is an output channel; allowlist what crosses it and mask what is kept.

## 1149. The HTTP method reached the request metrics' labels and the span name as the client sent it, before authentication, so any client that reached the port could grow Prometheus label sets without limit, a cardinality denial of service (fixed on this branch; on main)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-10, in review. Go's server accepts any token as a method. The API's metrics
(`http_requests_total`, `http_request_duration_seconds`) and its span name and `http.request.method` attribute took the
method as sent, and they are recorded before authentication and rate limiting. Each new token is a new label set, held in
memory by the Controller and by every Prometheus that scrapes it.

**Root cause.** A label was filled from caller input. Every other label (route pattern, status code) is a bounded
identifier; the method was assumed to be one too.

**Fix.** `6d73079b`. `boundedMethod` (`internal/api/middleware.go`) records a method outside the standard set as
`_OTHER`, OpenTelemetry's spelling, on the metrics and the span; the masked request log keeps it as sent. The span name is
built from `boundedMethod` and `routePattern` alone. Measured by `TestRouter_MethodLabelIsBounded`
(`internal/api/telemetry_labels_test.go`).

**Lesson.** LESSONS 440: bound what crosses an observability channel before authentication.

## 1150. url.path was recorded on the API span before authentication and rate limiting with no span limits, so one request could put about 1 MB of caller text on a span, and roughly 2 GiB of spans could queue while the collector was down (fixed on this branch; on main; a repeat in kind of 431)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-10, in review. Since 1032 the API span records `url.path` as the client sent
it, which is right for telling two requests apart. The SDK had no span limits, so the attribute was as long as the
request line the server accepts (about 1 MB). With the collector unreachable, the batch queue holds those spans, and the
worst case was roughly 2 GiB of queued caller text.

**Root cause.** Nothing bounded the size of a span. 1032 fixed which form of the path is recorded and did not ask how
long it could be.

**Why 431 did not prevent it.** 431's fix bounded and escaped text a remote server wrote into one client's errors
(`kubeapi.Explain`). Its lesson was about text from a remote system reaching an error. Text from a caller reaching a
recorder that keeps it is the same risk, and no rule or check carried 431's bound to the tracer.

**Fix.** `7aac7bbc`. `Setup` installs span limits: every attribute value is cut at 1024 bytes. Measured at about 20 KB for
a span from a long path by `TestRouter_ALongPathCannotSizeTheExportedSpan` (`internal/api/telemetry_limits_test.go`);
`TestSetup_CapsAttributeValues` (`internal/telemetry`). The docs say `url.path` is recorded before authentication and can
be denied.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 440: bound an observability channel's size before authentication.

## 1151. The OpenTelemetry SDK's internal logger (stdr on os.Stderr, which log.SetOutput does not reach) printed a malformed OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS value raw, usually a collector token; the branch's first fix masked the ErrorHandler path instead, which log.SetOutput already masked, and its changelog claimed the leak fixed (fixed before push; the leak on main; a repeat in kind of 23 and, for the claim, of 1041)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-10. The SDK reports a malformed `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` entry through its
internal logger, which is `stdr` writing to `os.Stderr` directly, and the message carries the value that failed to
parse. That value is usually the collector's token. The process's masked logging is installed with `log.SetOutput`, which
the SDK's internal logger never reads. The branch's first version replaced the SDK's `ErrorHandler` and said in its
changelog that the token no longer reached standard error. The fp-reviewer found that the ErrorHandler path already went
through `log`, so it was already masked, and the leak was on the logger path the first fix had not touched.

**Root cause.** The SDK has three writers: the exporter, the ErrorHandler and the internal logger. The first fix found
two. The changelog was written from the fix's intent, not from a test that put a token into the variable and read
standard error.

**Why 23 and 1041 did not prevent it.** 23 found a mask that covered a command's success path and not its error path;
the lesson was about one package's paths. 1041 found text on a branch claiming more than its code did. Neither names the
step that would have caught this: enumerating every writer a dependency has before claiming one of them closed.

**Fix.** `7aac7bbc`. `Setup` calls `otel.SetLogger` with a sink (`newMaskedLogger`, `internal/telemetry/errorhandler.go`)
that writes only the message and the error's type, masked, never the key-value pairs. The changelog fragment now says
only that the SDK's own messages no longer print the values they fail to parse. Test:
`TestSetup_TheSDKsInternalLoggerPrintsNoValues`, which sets a malformed header holding a token and reads standard error;
`TestMaskedLoggerDropsValuesAndNames`.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 440: enumerate every writer the SDK has; the exporter, the ErrorHandler and the internal logger are
three separate paths.

## 1152. The OpenTelemetry SDK's error handler wrote up to 4 MiB of a collector's reply into the log unescaped, so a collector, or anything answering on its address, could forge log lines (CWE-117) (fixed on this branch; on main; a repeat of 431, and the class of 1064)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-10, in review. An OTLP export error carries the collector's reply body, read
up to 4 MiB, and the SDK's default handler printed it through `log` as it was: newlines, control characters and all.

**Root cause.** Remote text reached a log with no bound and no escaping. The log handler masks secrets; it does not
escape or cut a message.

**Why 431 and 1064 did not prevent it.** 431 bounded and escaped one client's remote text (`kubeapi.Explain`); 1064 made
the CLI's error printing escape newlines (`termsafe`). Both fixes live at their own call sites. The SDK's handler is a
writer neither path covers, and it was not on any list.

**Fix.** `7aac7bbc`. The handler set by `otel.SetErrorHandler` masks the report, escapes it with `termsafe`, and cuts it to
one line of 2048 bytes on a character boundary. Tests: `TestSetup_ErrorReportsAreOneBoundedLine`,
`TestSetup_MasksTheSDKsOwnErrorReports`, `TestReportLineCutsOnACharacterBoundary`.

**Lesson.** As 431: text a remote system wrote is bounded and escaped before it reaches a log or an error, whoever wrote
the code that prints it.

## 1153. Inbound baggage and tracestate, key=value text a caller chooses, were propagated: baggage into each request's context, where the global propagator otelhttp uses (the moby client v0.5.0 wraps its transport with it) could write it to a managed host's Docker engine during onboarding, and tracestate onto the NATS dispatch headers kept in JetStream (fixed on this branch; on main)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-10, in review. The global propagator was W3C trace context plus baggage. The
API extracted both from every request, before authentication. The moby client (v0.5.0) wraps its HTTP transport with
otelhttp, which injects through the global propagator by default, so a caller's baggage could ride an outbound request to
a managed host's Docker engine during onboarding. A caller's `tracestate` travelled with the span context onto the
dispatch's NATS headers and was stored in the JetStream stream.

The first commit message also claimed that baggage reached NATS through the dispatch publish. The claim-refuter showed
that the publish builds its context from `context.Background()` plus the span, so baggage never reached it; only
`tracestate` did. The message was corrected before push.

**Root cause.** Propagated context from outside was treated as the platform's own. `telemetry.Propagator` was W3C Trace
Context plus W3C Baggage, and the span context carries `tracestate` onward. Both are caller input.

**Fix.** `7aac7bbc`. The propagator reads and writes `traceparent` only, and the masking exporter strips `tracestate` from
what it exports. Tests: `TestPropagator_CarriesNoBaggage`, `TestPropagator_ExtractsNoTraceState`,
`TestSetup_DropsEventsAndTraceStateItDoesNotKnow`, `TestPropagator_RoundTripsTraceContext`.

**Lesson.** LESSONS 442.

## 1154. An unauthenticated caller's traceparent sampled flag decided whether the API traced its request, since the sampler was ParentBased at the edge (fixed on this branch; on main)

**Symptom.** Found on this branch, 2026-11-10, in review. A `ParentBased` sampler follows a remote parent's sampled flag.
At the API that parent is whoever sent the request, so a caller could have every request it sent traced, whatever the
operator's ratio, or keep its own requests out of the trace.

**Root cause.** The operator's sampling ratio applied only to requests with no parent.
